I continue to use an absolute benchmark of about 0.1 on the dependency-score scale as a conservative practical-importance threshold, rather than a literal relative 10% criterion, because dependency scores are negative-valued and relative changes are unstable near zero. For direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. For interactions, I choose the direction so that a positive signed estimate represents stronger dependency or a larger association in the focal subgroup when that is the anticipated hypothesis.\n\nThe highest-value refinement is to extend the accepted large KEAP1-loss to weaker NFE2L2 axis into non-Avana screens. The broad effect H13 is accepted, and library robustness has already been established for SMARCA4-loss to SMARCA2 and TP53-loss to USP7, but KEAP1/NFE2L2 remains one of the few major axes without a non-Avana test. This is a context-robustness comparison, not a new biological direction; the anticipated raw contrast is positive because KEAP1 loss is expected to reduce NFE2L2 dependency in any screen where the biological signal exists. If it replicates, I can describe the KEAP1/NFE2L2 association as robust across screen libraries within this dataset. If it fails because of small non-Avana cell counts, the broad association can remain supported but should be described with library-coverage caveats.\n\nThe new STAT3 probes target a currently weak signal area with three biologically plausible upstream pathway perturbations: PTEN loss, STK11 loss, and KRAS mutation. These exposures activate or are associated with PI3K-AKT, MAPK/immune signaling, and STAT3-associated transcriptional programs. The registered direction is stronger STAT3 dependency, so a positive signed estimate would support these pathway alterations as markers of STAT3 dependency. The alternatives are a null pathway-specific effect, an effect opposite to the expected direction, or a smaller effect than the 0.1 benchmark. PIK3CA mutation is already active and should be considered together with these probes. If only some PI3K/RAS pathway markers are positive, that would suggest a partial pathway association rather than a coherent STAT3 axis.\n\nThe new DNA-damage and transcription probes test whether BRCA2 loss or MSI-high status have effects beyond the WRN axis. BRCA2 loss on DHX9 is biologically plausible because both relate to genome instability, R-loop resolution, and DNA repair stress; MSI-high on POLR2A tests whether MSI creates broader transcriptional vulnerability. These could uncover meaningful new axes. The alternative is that the WRN-MSI association is highly specific, in which case null results here strengthen specificity and reduce the chance that MSI-high is simply a general transcription-repair vulnerability marker.\n\nThe secretory/receptor trafficking probe, EGFR amplification on TMED10, is a new mechanistic hypothesis. TMED10 is involved in membrane protein trafficking, and EGFR amplification may increase demand for secretory-pathway components. The anticipated direction is stronger TMED10 dependency. A positive result would be an unexpected but biologically interpretable axis. A null result would complement the negative ERBB2/TMED10 and EGFR/dependency_EGFR tests and support the conclusion that amplification of these receptor genes does not broadly drive secretory-pathway dependency in this dataset.\n\nThe KIF18A probes test a plausible SWI/SNF mitotic vulnerability. SMARCA4 loss is already strongly associated with SMARCA2 dependency, and ARID1A loss is mechanistically nearby. If either SMARCA4 loss or ARID1A loss is associated with stronger KIF18A dependency, that would identify a chromosome segregation dependency associated with chromatin remodeling defects. If both are null, the large SMARCA4-loss effect on SMARCA2 appears specific to SMARCA2 synthetic lethality and does not generalize to the tested mitotic target. This is a clean falsifiable test: expected raw contrast is more negative in SWI/SNF-deficient cells, and the signed estimate will be positive under the registered direction.\n\nMYC amplification on MDM2 is included despite the TP53-intact MYC probe being null because the unconditional relationship may differ if the effect is concentrated in TP53-altered contexts or if MYC amplification acts through replication stress and p53-independent MDM2 biology. This comparison is a candidate new moderate axis. Alternatives include a null overall effect, a positive effect below the practical benchmark, or an effect restricted to a TP53 context that would need a later refinement.\n\nFinally, I add two CDKN2A-MDM2 heterogeneity probes: Cas9 activity and mutation burden. Cas9 activity is a technical robustness check: a positive signed interaction with high Cas9 activity would indicate that the accepted moderate CDKN2A-MDM2 effect is stronger in screens with higher editing efficiency, which would support technical validity but also raise the concern that lower-Cas9 screens understate the effect. A null Cas9 interaction would strengthen the conclusion that the CDKN2A-MDM2 association is not driven by screen performance. The mutation-burden interaction tests whether the CDKN2A-MDM2 effect is modified by genomic instability or p53-pathway stress. Anticipation is uncertain because prior CDKN2A-MDM2 effects are coherent across TP53 status and library status, but mutational context could plausibly amplify or attenuate the dependency.\n\nOverall, these proposals prioritize (1) library robustness of an accepted large axis, (2) new pathway-specific STAT3 hypotheses, (3) specificity tests for accepted axes, (4) plausible SWI/SNF and secretory-pathway dependencies, and (5) context robustness of the newly accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 axis. I am not requesting validation at this analyze stage; validation will be considered after assessing these discovery results, preferably only for a new result strong enough to alter the accepted axis set or clarify the CDKN2A-MDM2 conclusion.","appraise":"I assessed all newly delivered discovery results using the same practical benchmark of roughly 0.1 absolute dependency-score difference, while recognizing that a literal relative threshold is awkward for negative dependency scores. All estimates are already signed to the registered direction. H106 is the central new result: unconditional CDKN2A loss was associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, signed +0.117 (95% +0.082 to +0.152) in adequate cells. Although the lower bound is below the 0.1 benchmark, the point estimate meets it and the result is coherent with the already accepted and independently validated TP53-intact and TP53-loss stratum effects, H77 and H95. I therefore accept H106 as a dataset-specific moderate CDKN2A-to-MDM2 association and close it. H107 tested TP53 heterogeneity of that association; the signed interaction was +0.008 (95% -0.077 to +0.093), negligible and uncertain. This does not support the registered direction that TP53 loss weakens the CDKN2A effect, so I reject H107. It also does not prove absence of all heterogeneity, only that the current evidence does not justify a meaningful TP53 interaction. H108 is the most important unresolved robustness result: in non-Avana screens CDKN2A loss had signed +0.125 (95% +0.029 to +0.222), which is promising in magnitude and direction but based on only 47 exposed cells and a wide interval. Because library robustness matters for interpreting H106, I leave H108 unresolved and request validation. H109, CDKN2A loss among TP53-loss adenocarcinomas, had signed +0.161 (95% +0.067 to +0.256) with 57 exposed cells; this supports the accepted TP53-loss stratum in the dominant lineage, but with imprecision, so I accept it as a context replication and close. H110, MTAP loss among TP53-loss cells, was essentially null, signed -0.006 (95% -0.065 to +0.053), supporting CDKN2A specificity rather than a generic MTAP or 9p21 effect, so I reject and close it. H92, CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact adenocarcinomas, had signed +0.103 (95% +0.057 to +0.148), supporting effect presence in the dominant subtype; the lower bound is below benchmark, so I accept it with caution and close. H111, ARID1A loss among SMARCA4-intact cells, was null, signed -0.003 (95% -0.025 to +0.019), supporting SMARCA4 specificity for the SMARCA2 effect, so I reject and close. H112 tested the accepted SMARCA4-to-SMARCA2 effect in non-Avana libraries: signed +0.801 (95% +0.748 to +0.853) with adequate small cells. This is large and directionally identical, so I accept it as library-robust within the dataset and close. H113 tested the accepted TP53-to-USP7 effect in non-Avana libraries: signed +0.321 (95% +0.085 to +0.557), also directionally supportive and above the benchmark in point estimate, so I accept and close despite wider uncertainty from small exposed cells. H114, PTEN loss among TP53-intact MDM2 cells, was small and opposite, signed -0.018 (95% -0.050 to +0.013), so I reject and close. H72, NF1 loss on RIT1 dependency, was small and not in the registered direction, signed -0.021 (95% -0.049 to +0.008), so I reject and close. H91, KEAP1 loss on USP7 dependency, was small and uncertain, signed +0.030 (95% -0.014 to +0.074), so I reject and close. Overall, the new evidence strengthens the CDKN2A-MDM2 association as broad but moderate, supports specificity against MTAP, PTEN, and KEAP1 probes, and confirms library robustness of the two large accepted axes. Discovery R95 was +0.125 with interval +0.029 to +0.222. Independent validation R105 was +0.172 with independent interval +0.037 to +0.307. The direction is replicated, the point estimates are moderate and above the practical benchmark, and the stringent validation interval excludes zero. I therefore accept H108 and close it, while explicitly retaining uncertainty in its exact magnitude.  H67 new validation: The claim was that TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency specifically in MTAP-loss-positive cells. Discovery R57 was +0.284 with interval +0.105 to +0.463, which originally supported the claim. Independent validation R106 was +0.265, a similar and meaningful point estimate, but its independent interval was -0.047 to +0.576 and crossed zero. Thus the validation is directionally consistent but not statistically conclusive, especially with only 61 exposed cells. I do not reject H67 because there is no evidence against the direction and the point estimate remains plausible, but I also do not keep it accepted because the newly delivered independent evidence does not confirm a scientifically meaningful stratum-specific effect. I therefore downgrade H67 to unresolved and defer it. The broad TP53-loss effect on USP7 remains strongly supported by H11 and its validation R52, and the MTAP-intact stratum H68 remains supported by discovery. The interaction test H18 did not support meaningful modification of the TP53-USP7 association by MTAP status. Therefore, the most defensible conclusion is that TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency broadly, with the MTAP-positive subgroup currently uncertain because of imprecision. Four large dataset-specific associations remain strongly supported: MSI-high versus MSI-low is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency, and SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. record.narrative: I assessed all newly delivered discovery estimates using the same signed-estimate convention and the practical absolute benchmark of about 0.1 on the dependency-score scale. Dependency scores are negative-valued, so a literal relative 10% change is unstable near zero; the 0.1 benchmark is therefore used as a conservative scientific-importance threshold rather than a causal claim. For direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. For interactions, a positive signed estimate represents a larger focal-subgroup association when the hypothesis was registered that way. H93 tested CDKN2A loss on MDM2 dependency among TP53-intact Avana-library cells. The signed estimate was +0.117, 95% CI +0.074 to +0.160, with adequate cell sizes (281 exposed, 1121 comparator). The lower bound is slightly below the 0.1 benchmark, but the point estimate is above it and the result is highly coherent with the already accepted broad CDKN2A-MDM2 association and with independently validated TP53-intact and TP53-loss strata. I therefore accept H93 as a context-complete replication in the dominant TP53-intact Avana stratum and close it. H115 tested the accepted KEAP1-loss to weaker NFE2L2 association in non-Avana screens. The signed estimate was +0.794, 95% CI +0.746 to +0.842, with 40 exposed and 195 comparator cells. Although exposed cells are modest, the effect is enormous, far above the benchmark, and directionally identical to the broad validated effect. I accept it with a small-cell precision caveat and close it, supporting library robustness of this major axis within this dataset. H90 tested whether MSI-high remains associated with much stronger WRN dependency in cells with aneuploidy above the median. The signed estimate was +0.801, 95% CI +0.761 to +0.841, with 65 exposed cells. This is a large, directionally supportive context replication, so I accept and close H90. H116 is the most important new discovery: PTEN loss was associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, signed estimate +0.267, 95% CI +0.215 to +0.319, with 266 exposed cells. This is far above the practical benchmark and biologically plausible through PI3K/PTEN-related signaling pathways. However, it is a single new-axis discovery among several STAT3 probes, the estimate is unadjusted for co-occurring molecular alterations, and independent confirmation is not yet available. I therefore record H116 as unresolved but active and request independent validation rather than prematurely accepting it as a new supported axis. The remaining STAT3 probes did not support a coherent broader PI3K/RAS pathway effect: H117 STK11 loss was +0.015, CI -0.014 to +0.043; H118 KRAS mutation was -0.018, CI -0.042 to +0.007; H73 PIK3CA mutation was -0.014, CI -0.041 to +0.014. All are small, uncertain, and far below the benchmark, so I reject and close them. H125 tested Cas9-activity modification of the CDKN2A-MDM2 interaction. The signed interaction was +0.048, 95% CI -0.027 to +0.123. It does not support a meaningful high-Cas9 interaction, but the upper bound crosses the practical benchmark and the cell counts, while adequate, are not large. I keep H125 unresolved and deferred rather than rejecting it as proof of absence. H126 tested mutation-burden modification of the CDKN2A-MDM2 interaction and was essentially null, -0.001, CI -0.069 to +0.068, entirely below the benchmark; I reject and close it. H119 tested BRCA2 loss on DHX9 dependency and found a small null effect, +0.012, CI -0.020 to +0.044. H120 tested MSI-high on POLR2A dependency and found a small opposite/null effect, -0.004, CI -0.035 to +0.028. H122 tested SMARCA4 loss on KIF18A dependency and found a small opposite/null effect, -0.007, CI -0.026 to +0.013. All are below the benchmark and do not support new axes; I reject and close them. Overall, the new evidence strengthens the accepted large axes: MSI-high-WRN remains strong in high-aneuploidy cells, KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency is library-robust, and the CDKN2A-MDM2 association is now replicated in the largest TP53-intact Avana context. It also identifies a potentially major new PTEN-loss to stronger STAT3 dependency association, but I hold final acceptance pending independent validation. Multiplicity remains relevant for new subgroup or subgroup-marker claims, and all current conclusions remain associations in this supplied dataset rather than causal or externally generalizable effects.

For direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. For interactions, I choose the direction so that a positive signed estimate represents stronger dependency or a larger association in the focal subgroup when that is the anticipated hypothesis.\n\nThe highest-value refinement is to extend the accepted large KEAP1-loss to weaker NFE2L2 axis into non-Avana screens. The broad effect H13 is accepted, and library robustness has already been established for SMARCA4-loss to SMARCA2 and TP53-loss to USP7, but KEAP1/NFE2L2 remains one of the few major axes without a non-Avana test. This is a context-robustness comparison, not a new biological direction; the anticipated raw contrast is positive because KEAP1 loss is expected to reduce NFE2L2 dependency in any screen where the biological signal exists. If it replicates, I can describe the KEAP1/NFE2L2 association as robust across screen libraries within this dataset. If it fails because of small non-Avana cell counts, the broad association can remain supported but should be described with library-coverage caveats.\n\nThe new STAT3 probes target a currently weak signal area with three biologically plausible upstream pathway perturbations: PTEN loss, STK11 loss, and KRAS mutation. These exposures activate or are associated with PI3K-AKT, MAPK/immune signaling, and STAT3-associated transcriptional programs. The registered direction is stronger STAT3 dependency, so a positive signed estimate would support these pathway alterations as markers of STAT3 dependency. The alternatives are a null pathway-specific effect, an effect opposite to the expected direction, or a smaller effect than the 0.1 benchmark. PIK3CA mutation is already active and should be considered together with these probes. If only some PI3K/RAS pathway markers are positive, that would suggest a partial pathway association rather than a coherent STAT3 axis.\n\nThe new DNA-damage and transcription probes test whether BRCA2 loss or MSI-high status have effects beyond the WRN axis. BRCA2 loss on DHX9 is biologically plausible because both relate to genome instability, R-loop resolution, and DNA repair stress; MSI-high on POLR2A tests whether MSI creates broader transcriptional vulnerability. These could uncover meaningful new axes. The alternative is that the WRN-MSI association is highly specific, in which case null results here strengthen specificity and reduce the chance that MSI-high is simply a general transcription-repair vulnerability marker.\n\nThe secretory/receptor trafficking probe, EGFR amplification on TMED10, is a new mechanistic hypothesis. TMED10 is involved in membrane protein trafficking, and EGFR amplification may increase demand for secretory-pathway components. The anticipated direction is stronger TMED10 dependency. A positive result would be an unexpected but biologically interpretable axis. A null result would complement the negative ERBB2/TMED10 and EGFR/dependency_EGFR tests and support the conclusion that amplification of these receptor genes does not broadly drive secretory-pathway dependency in this dataset.\n\nThe KIF18A probes test a plausible SWI/SNF mitotic vulnerability. SMARCA4 loss is already strongly associated with SMARCA2 dependency, and ARID1A loss is mechanistically nearby. If either SMARCA4 loss or ARID1A loss is associated with stronger KIF18A dependency, that would identify a chromosome segregation dependency associated with chromatin remodeling defects. If both are null, the large SMARCA4-loss effect on SMARCA2 appears specific to SMARCA2 synthetic lethality and does not generalize to the tested mitotic target. This is a clean falsifiable test: expected raw contrast is more negative in SWI/SNF-deficient cells, and the signed estimate will be positive under the registered direction.\n\nMYC amplification on MDM2 is included despite the TP53-intact MYC probe being null because the unconditional relationship may differ if the effect is concentrated in TP53-altered contexts or if MYC amplification acts through replication stress and p53-independent MDM2 biology. This comparison is a candidate new moderate axis. Alternatives include a null overall effect, a positive effect below the practical benchmark, or an effect restricted to a TP53 context that would need a later refinement.\n\nFinally, I add two CDKN2A-MDM2 heterogeneity probes: Cas9 activity and mutation burden. Cas9 activity is a technical robustness check: a positive signed interaction with high Cas9 activity would indicate that the accepted moderate CDKN2A-MDM2 effect is stronger in screens with higher editing efficiency, which would support technical validity but also raise the concern that lower-Cas9 screens understate the effect. A null Cas9 interaction would strengthen the conclusion that the CDKN2A-MDM2 association is not driven by screen performance. The mutation-burden interaction tests whether the CDKN2A-MDM2 effect is modified by genomic instability or p53-pathway stress. Anticipation is uncertain because prior CDKN2A-MDM2 effects are coherent across TP53 status and library status, but mutational context could plausibly amplify or attenuate the dependency.\n\nOverall, these proposals prioritize (1) library robustness of an accepted large axis, (2) new pathway-specific STAT3 hypotheses, (3) specificity tests for accepted axes, (4) plausible SWI/SNF and secretory-pathway dependencies, and (5) context robustness of the newly accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 axis. I am not requesting validation at this stage because the selected analyses are discovery claims; validation will be considered after assessing whether any new effect is strong enough to change the accepted axis set or resolve an important context uncertainty.","appraise":"I assessed all newly delivered discovery estimates using the same signed-estimate convention and the practical absolute benchmark of about 0.1 on the dependency-score scale. Dependency scores are negative-valued, so a literal relative 10% change is unstable near zero; the 0.1 benchmark is therefore used as a conservative scientific-importance threshold rather than a causal claim. For direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. For interactions, a positive signed estimate represents a larger focal-subgroup association when the hypothesis was registered that way. H93 tested CDKN2A loss on MDM2 dependency among TP53-intact Avana-library cells. The signed estimate was +0.117, 95% CI +0.074 to +0.160, with adequate cell sizes (281 exposed, 1121 comparator). The lower bound is slightly below the 0.1 benchmark, but the point estimate is above it and the result is highly coherent with the already accepted broad CDKN2A-MDM2 association and with independently validated TP53-intact and TP53-loss strata. I therefore accept H93 as a context-complete replication in the dominant TP53-intact Avana stratum and close it. H115 tested the accepted KEAP1-loss to weaker NFE2L2 association in non-Avana screens. The signed estimate was +0.794, 95% CI +0.746 to +0.842, with 40 exposed and 195 comparator cells. Although exposed cells are modest, the effect is enormous, far above the benchmark, and directionally identical to the broad validated effect. I accept it with a small-cell precision caveat and close it, supporting library robustness of this major axis within this dataset. H90 tested whether MSI-high remains associated with much stronger WRN dependency in cells with aneuploidy above the median. The signed estimate was +0.801, 95% CI +0.761 to +0.841, with 65 exposed cells. This is a large, directionally supportive context replication, so I accept and close H90. H116 is the most important new discovery: PTEN loss was associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, signed estimate +0.267, 95% CI +0.215 to +0.319, with 266 exposed cells. This is far above the practical benchmark and biologically plausible through PI3K/PTEN-related signaling pathways. However, it is a single new-axis discovery among several STAT3 probes, the estimate is unadjusted for co-occurring molecular alterations, and independent confirmation is not yet available. I therefore record H116 as unresolved but active and request independent validation rather than prematurely accepting it as a new supported axis. The remaining STAT3 probes did not support a coherent broader PI3K/RAS pathway effect: H117 STK11 loss was +0.015, CI -0.014 to +0.043; H118 KRAS mutation was -0.018, CI -0.042 to +0.007; H73 PIK3CA mutation was -0.014, CI -0.041 to +0.014. All are small, uncertain, and far below the benchmark, so I reject and close them. H125 tested Cas9-activity modification of the CDKN2A-MDM2 interaction. The signed interaction was +0.048, 95% CI -0.027 to +0.123. It does not support a meaningful high-Cas9 interaction, but the upper bound crosses the practical benchmark and the cell counts, while adequate, are not large. I keep H125 unresolved and deferred rather than rejecting it as proof of absence. record.narrative: Both due assessments involve signed estimates. For direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group. H95 is the CDKN2A-loss versus no-CDKN2A-loss comparison on MDM2 dependency restricted to TP53-loss cells. Discovery R81 was +0.111 (95% CI +0.035 to +0.186), and the independent validation R92 is +0.132 (stringent independent interval +0.016 to +0.249). The two estimates are directionally and magnitude-consistent and exclude zero, supporting a real dataset-specific association in the TP53-loss stratum. The validation interval does not exclude values below the absolute 0.1 practical benchmark, so the exact magnitude is imprecise, but the broader CDKN2A-loss to stronger MDM2 association is already robust across TP53-intact, TP53-loss, lineage, and library contexts. Therefore H95 remains accepted and closed as a moderate association with magnitude uncertainty. H116 tests PTEN loss versus intact PTEN on STAT3 dependency, direction -1, so positive signed estimates mean stronger STAT3 dependency with PTEN loss. Discovery R113 was +0.267 (95% CI +0.215 to +0.319), and independent validation R119 is +0.283 (independent interval +0.208 to +0.358). The validation is large, precise enough for the practical absolute benchmark, and excludes the benchmark; it confirms the discovery estimate rather than merely confirming a small nonzero effect. I therefore accept H116 and close the main PTEN-STAT3 claim as a newly supported strong dataset-specific axis. This does not yet establish causality or generalizability outside this supplied dataset. Co-occurring alterations and context dependence remain unresolved; the existing PTEN-STAT3 context/specificity probes H127 through H132, plus the newly registered driver-negative PTEN-STAT3 proposal, are the next priority. The accepted axis set now contains four previously established large associations, MSI-high to stronger WRN, KEAP1 loss to weaker NFE2L2, TP53 loss to weaker USP7, and SMARCA4 loss to stronger SMARCA2, plus the moderate but context-robust CDKN2A-loss to stronger MDM2 axis, and the new strong PTEN-loss to stronger STAT3 association. Negative findings continue to support specificity: STK11 loss, KRAS mutation, and PIK3CA mutation did not show meaningful STAT3 associations; MTAP loss was not broadly associated with USP7; and several cross-axis probes remain null. Main unresolved items are the MTAP-positive TP53-USP7 stratum H67, the Cas9-interaction check H125, and PTEN-STAT3 context and specificity analyses. All conclusions remain associations within the supplied dataset.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction

Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

For direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. For interactions, a positive signed estimate represents a larger focal-subgroup association when the hypothesis was registered that way. H93 tested CDKN2A loss on MDM2 dependency among TP53-intact Avana-library cells. The signed estimate was +0.117, 95% CI +0.074 to +0.160, with adequate cell sizes (281 exposed, 1121 comparator). The lower bound is slightly below the 0.1 benchmark, but the point estimate is above it and the result is highly coherent with the already accepted broad CDKN2A-MDM2 association and with independently validated TP53-intact and TP53-loss strata. I therefore accept H93 as a context-complete replication in the dominant TP53-intact Avana stratum and close it. H115 tested the accepted KEAP1-loss to weaker NFE2L2 association in non-Avana screens. The signed estimate was +0.794, 95% CI +0.746 to +0.842, with 40 exposed and 195 comparator cells. Although exposed cells are modest, the effect is enormous, far above the benchmark, and directionally identical to the broad validated effect. I accept it with a small-cell precision caveat and close it, supporting library robustness of this major axis within this dataset. H90 tested whether MSI-high remains associated with much stronger WRN dependency in cells with aneuploidy above the median. The signed estimate was +0.801, 95% CI +0.761 to +0.841, with 65 exposed cells. This is a large, directionally supportive context replication, so I accept and close H90. H116 is the most important new discovery: PTEN loss was associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, signed estimate +0.267, 95% CI +0.215 to +0.319, with 266 exposed cells. This is far above the practical benchmark and biologically plausible through PI3K/PTEN-related signaling pathways. However, it is a single new-axis discovery among several STAT3 probes, the estimate is unadjusted for co-occurring molecular alterations, and independent confirmation is not yet available. I therefore record H116 as unresolved but active and request independent validation rather than prematurely accepting it as a new supported axis. The remaining STAT3 probes did not support a coherent broader PI3K/RAS pathway effect: H117 STK11 loss was +0.015, CI -0.014 to +0.043; H118 KRAS mutation was -0.018, CI -0.042 to +0.007; H73 PIK3CA mutation was -0.014, CI -0.041 to +0.014. All are small, uncertain, and far below the benchmark, so I reject and close them. H125 tested Cas9-activity modification of the CDKN2A-MDM2 interaction. The signed interaction was +0.048, 95% CI -0.027 to +0.123. record.narrative:
No assessments are due. I am registering new refinements and falsifiable probes around the newly accepted PTEN-loss to stronger STAT3-dependency axis, specificity tests for accepted large axes, replication-stress/cell-cycle hypotheses, and one global technical-bias check. Direction convention remains: for direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. For interactions with direction -1, a positive signed estimate means a larger exposed-minus-comparator dependency effect in the focal subgroup than in the complement. Because dependency scores are negative and often near zero, I continue to interpret practical importance using an absolute difference of roughly 0.1 on the dependency-score scale rather than a literal relative 10% change, while still treating uncertainty and direction as decisive.

The first three proposals test context dependence of the accepted PTEN-STAT3 axis with formal interactions rather than only stratified mean effects. The TP53-loss interaction asks whether PTEN loss has a larger STAT3-dependency effect in TP53-loss cells, which would suggest pathway interaction or co-occurrence confounding; a null result would support independence from TP53 status. The PIK3CA-mutation interaction asks whether PTEN loss and PI3K-pathway mutation act as a coherent pathway signal. Prior PIK3CA mutation had a small null main STAT3 effect, so a positive interaction could indicate that PTEN matters mainly in a PI3K-mutant context, whereas a null result supports a more PTEN-specific association. The adenocarcinoma-lineage interaction tests whether the PTEN effect is confined to adenocarcinoma or extends across the lung lineage subtypes in this dataset. These are refinements, not reversals: the broad PTEN-STAT3 claim remains supported.

The PTEN-MDM2 and PTEN-USP7 probes test specificity of the PTEN axis. If PTEN loss also produces a meaningful MDM2 dependency effect, especially stronger MDM2 dependency, it would broaden the PTEN phenotype to p53/MDM2-associated biology, although that would need careful replication and consideration of co-occurring TP53/CDKN2A status. If PTEN-MDM2 is null or tiny, this supports STAT3 as the primary STAT3-associated dependency signal for PTEN loss in this dataset. For USP7, the direction +1 convention makes a positive signed estimate mean weaker USP7 dependency with PTEN loss, i.e., a partial mimicry of the accepted TP53-loss effect. The anticipated direction is uncertain; a strong positive result would suggest PTEN affects the p53-MDM2-USP7 network, while a null result would help separate PTEN-STAT3 from the TP53-USP7 axis.

The CDKN2A-loss by PTEN-loss interaction on MDM2 asks whether the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 association is modified by PTEN status. A positive interaction would mean CDKN2A loss increases MDM2 dependency more in PTEN-loss cells, potentially revealing a PTEN-CDKN2A-MDM2 relationship. A null interaction would support the growing conclusion that CDKN2A-MDM2 is a broadly context-robust axis, including across PTEN status. This is preferable to adding another simple stratum because it directly tests effect modification while using the accepted main effect as motivation.

The SMARCA4-loss probes on WRN and DHX9 test whether the accepted SMARCA4-SMARCA2 association is a broader replication-stress vulnerability or a SMARCA2-specific synthetic-lethal effect. Chromatin remodeling defects can create transcription-replication conflict and DNA repair stress, so stronger WRN or DHX9 dependency is biologically plausible. Positive results would define new axes; null results would strengthen the specificity of the large SMARCA4-SMARCA2 effect. MYC amplification on WRN is similar: MYC amplification is classically linked to replication stress, and a positive result would be a new replication-stress axis. RB1 loss on POLR2A tests a related cell-cycle transcription hypothesis, with RB1 loss plausibly increasing dependency on transcription elongation under replication stress. The alternative in each case is null or an opposite effect below the practical benchmark.

The MTAP-loss comparison restricted to TP53-loss cells addresses the deferred MTAP-related TP53-USP7 stratum. H67 tested TP53 loss within MTAP-loss cells and had a directionally supportive but imprecise validation. Testing MTAP loss itself within TP53-loss cells clarifies whether MTAP status shifts baseline USP7 dependency and may explain why the TP53 effect was attenuated in MTAP-positive cells. This is not validation; it is a mechanistic/stratum decomposition that may make the remaining MTAP question interpretable.

The Avana versus non-Avana WRN comparison is a technical robustness check. It does not test the MSI-high subgroup alone; it tests whether WRN dependency scores overall differ between library types. A near-null global library effect would increase confidence that accepted WRN findings are not simply an artifact of the dominant Avana library. A meaningful library effect would require describing accepted WRN associations as library-contextual and would inform later context-specific analyses.

Overall, these proposals allocate exploration toward: (1) formalizing whether the new PTEN-STAT3 axis is independent of TP53, PIK3CA, lineage, and MDM2/USP7 pathways; (2) testing cross-pathway interaction for CDKN2A-MDM2 and PTEN; (3) testing whether accepted large axes have additional replication-stress dependencies or are target-specific; and (4) resolving the deferred MTAP/TP53-USP7 question. All proposed claims remain dataset-specific associations unless replicated and interpreted cautiously; they are not causal or externally generalizable statements.

record.narrative: I assessed the newly delivered discovery estimates using the signed-estimate convention already registered for each claim. For direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate corresponds to stronger dependency in the exposed group because dependency scores are more negative for stronger dependency; for direction +1 contrasts, a positive signed estimate corresponds to weaker dependency in the exposed group. For interactions, a positive signed estimate represents a larger registered focal-subgroup contrast than in the complement. Because dependency scores are signed and centered away from a stable positive scale, a literal relative 10% difference is unstable, especially near zero, so I continued to use an absolute dependency-score difference of roughly 0.1 as the scientific-importance benchmark while also requiring direction and uncertainty to support the registered claim. H133 is the key new positive result: PTEN loss was associated with stronger STAT3 dependency in cells lacking KRAS, BRAF V600E, EGFR amplification, and ERBB2 amplification, signed estimate +0.264, 95% CI +0.197 to +0.332, with 161 exposed and 974 comparator cells. The effect is large, precise enough for the practical benchmark, and excludes the 0.1 threshold. I accept H133 as a dataset-specific context-supported association, but as a refinement of the already accepted PTEN-STAT3 axis rather than evidence of causality or external generalizability. Residual confounding by other measured or unmeasured alterations, library context, and lineage subtype cannot be excluded, and the claim arose from multiple context probes, so I requested independent validation of H133. H134 tested PTEN-STAT3 interaction by TP53 loss; signed estimate -0.097, 95% CI -0.217 to +0.024, with adequate but small focal exposed cells. The upper bound is far below a meaningful positive interaction, so there is no support for PTEN having a larger stronger-STAT3 effect in TP53-loss cells; I reject the registered interaction and close it, while noting that the negative point estimate could reflect attenuation but was not the registered direction and is too imprecise for a confident opposite claim. H135 tested PIK3CA interaction; signed estimate +0.001, 95% CI -0.150 to +0.152. The point estimate is null and the interval is wide, crossing both practical directions around the benchmark; I therefore leave it unresolved and deferred rather than claiming absence of effect modification. H136 tested adenocarcinoma lineage interaction; signed estimate +0.001, 95% CI -0.115 to +0.117. It gives no evidence of adenocarcinoma-specific enhancement of the PTEN-STAT3 association, but the interval still admits moderate modification in either direction, so it is unresolved and deferred. H137 tested PTEN loss on MDM2 dependency; signed estimate -0.015, 95% CI -0.043 to +0.014. This is small and opposite to a meaningful stronger-dependency signal, supporting STAT3 specificity for PTEN in this dataset; reject and close. H138 tested PTEN loss on USP7 dependency under direction +1, where positive would mean weaker USP7; signed estimate -0.005, 95% CI -0.057 to +0.046, far below benchmark and not supportive; reject and close. H139 tested CDKN2A-loss MDM2 interaction by PTEN loss; signed estimate +0.009, 95% CI -0.093 to +0.112, with only 51 exposed PTEN-loss CDKN2A cells. It does not support positive interaction, but the upper bound is near the benchmark and the focal cell count is modest, so I keep it unresolved and deferred while noting that the main CDKN2A-MDM2 association is already broadly robust. H140 and H141 tested SMARCA4 loss against WRN and DHX9; signed estimates +0.003 and -0.006, respectively, both entirely below the practical benchmark. These reject broader replication-stress dependencies for the accepted SMARCA4-SMARCA2 axis in this dataset and support its target specificity. H142 tested MYC amplification against WRN; signed estimate -0.033, 95% CI -0.064 to -0.002. It excludes a meaningful stronger-WRN effect and instead suggests a very small opposite association, but it is below the 0.1 practical threshold, so I reject the registered stronger-dependency claim without endorsing the small opposite effect as important. H144 tested MTAP loss within TP53-loss cells for USP7 dependency under direction +1; signed estimate -0.119, 95% CI -0.312 to +0.075, with 73 exposed cells. The negative signed point estimate is intriguing because it suggests MTAP loss may make USP7 dependency stronger among TP53-loss cells, but the interval is wide and the claim direction and cell counts do not justify acceptance or rejection of an opposite effect; I keep it unresolved and deferred. H145 tested global WRN dependency difference between Avana and non-Avana libraries; signed estimate +0.022, 95% CI -0.012 to +0.055. Although statistically nonzero at the discovery interval, the effect is well below the scientific benchmark, so I reject a meaningful global library artifact in WRN dependency and close the robustness check. Overall, the new evidence strengthens specificity of accepted axes and identifies PTEN-STAT3 driver-negative context support, but it does not establish causal mechanisms or generalizable effects. Multiplicity, cell-size dependence, residual molecular confounding, and library or technical context remain limits; the only validation request is H133 because it is the strongest new context claim and would benefit from independent confirmation.

prompt:
Iteration 10/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: The due response-deadline validations are assessed using the registered signed-estimate convention. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. I use an absolute dependency-score separation of roughly 0.1 as the scientific-practical benchmark, with direction and uncertainty decisive, because dependency scores are negative and centered and a literal relative 10% comparison is unstable near zero. H108 tested CDKN2A loss versus no CDKN2A loss on MDM2 dependency in non-Avana CRISPR-library cells. Discovery R95 was +0.125, and independent validation R105 was +0.172, with validation interval +0.037 to +0.307. The estimates are directionally consistent, exclude zero, and support a real dataset-specific association. The validation interval does not exclude magnitudes below the practical benchmark, so the exact size remains imprecise, but the CDKN2A-loss to stronger MDM2 axis is already robust across TP53-intact, TP53-loss, lineage, and library strata. I therefore accept H108 and close it. H67 tested TP53 loss versus TP53-intact on USP7 dependency within MTAP-loss cells under direction +1, so positive estimates indicate weaker USP7 dependency with TP53 loss. Discovery R57 was +0.284 with a 95% interval excluding zero and the practical benchmark, but independent validation R106 was +0.265 with a stringent independent interval -0.047 to +0.576. The validation point estimate agrees with discovery, but the interval does not exclude zero or values below the practical threshold. Because the broad TP53-loss to weaker USP7 axis is independently accepted and this subgroup result is directionally consistent, I do not reject H67. However, because independent validation did not confirm the stratum-specific effect with adequate precision, I keep H67 unresolved and active. H133 tested PTEN loss versus intact PTEN on STAT3 dependency in cells lacking KRAS mutation, BRAF V600E, EGFR amplification, and ERBB2 amplification. Discovery R120 was +0.264, and validation R132 was +0.304 with a stringent interval +0.196 to +0.413. The effect is large, directionally consistent, and excludes the practical benchmark. I accept H133 and close it as a validated dataset-specific refinement of the PTEN-loss to stronger STAT3 axis. This supports PTEN-STAT3 specificity beyond the main population and major-driver-negative context, but it does not establish causality or external generalizability; residual molecular confounding, lineage context, and library context remain possible. Overall synthesis: the supplied-dataset evidence now supports a coherent set of dependency axes: MSI-high to stronger WRN, KEAP1 loss to weaker NFE2L2, TP53 loss to weaker USP7, SMARCA4 loss to stronger SMARCA2, CDKN2A loss to stronger MDM2, and PTEN loss to stronger STAT3. The PTEN-STAT3 axis is now validated both overall and in the driver-negative context. The CDKN2A-MDM2 axis is validated across multiple strata, including non-Avana and TP53-loss contexts. Negative findings continue to support target specificity: KRAS mutation did not support stronger KRAS dependency, EGFR amplification did not support stronger EGFR dependency, ERBB2 amplification did not support stronger ERBB2 dependency, BRAF V600E did not support stronger BRAF dependency, and many cross-axis probes were null or below benchmark. The principal unresolved uncertainty is whether MTAP loss attenuates the TP53-loss to weaker USP7 association. The positive enhancement interaction is rejected, but attenuation remains suggested by imprecise stratum data. I registered one refinement: a reversed TP53-loss by MTAP-loss interaction for USP7 to test attenuation rather than enhancement, because this is the most informative next way to resolve the H67 loose end without requesting redundant validation. Pending PTEN-STAT3 context and specificity probes H127-H132 should also be prioritized to define the boundaries of the new PTEN axis.

Iteration 11/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due. I am registering a focused batch of context, specificity, and mechanism-disambiguation comparisons rather than repeating accepted main effects or exact active probes. The accepted supplied-dataset axes remain: MSI-high with stronger WRN; KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2; TP53 loss with weaker USP7; SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2; CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2; and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3. The first four proposals define the boundary and specificity of the newly validated PTEN-STAT3 axis. PIK3CA-mutant and PIK3CA-wild-type strata test whether PTEN behaves like a coherent PI3K-pathway marker or retains association independent of PIK3CA mutation. CDKN2A-intact and SMARCA4-intact strata test whether the PTEN effect could be confounded by other accepted axes. For direction -1 PTEN-STAT3 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger STAT3 dependency in PTEN-loss cells; a precise estimate above the practical absolute threshold of roughly 0.1 would support context-specific PTEN biology, while null results would favor robustness and independence. The CDKN2A-on-STAT3 and SMARCA4-on-STAT3 probes test target specificity. Strong positive effects would suggest broader p53-network or chromatin-remodeling effects on STAT3, whereas nulls would strengthen the interpretation that PTEN is a relatively STAT3-specific predictor among the tested axes. The MTAP-loss-on-USP7 probe among TP53-intact cells complements the deferred TP53-loss stratum and the active attenuation-interaction probe. A positive signed estimate would mean stronger USP7 dependency with MTAP loss among TP53-intact cells, which could help explain attenuation of the TP53-loss USP7 effect; a null or opposite result would suggest that the unresolved MTAP question is not explained by a simple TP53-intact MTAP baseline shift. Finally, KEAP1 loss on WRN and MSI-high on USP7 are cross-repair-network probes. They are registered with uncertain expectations and direction -1 stronger-dependency hypotheses because NRF2-driven oxidative stress and dMMR/replication stress are plausible DNA-damage-response modifiers, but existing evidence does not strongly predict either outcome. These proposals remain supplied-dataset associations only; causal claims, external generalizability, and clinical utility are not inferred.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: No assessments are due (assessments_due is empty), so the full analyze budget goes to requesting 12 new discovery analyses on currently untested, high-priority context/specificity/robustness probes. I keep the signed-estimate convention: for direction -1 mean differences a positive signed value means stronger dependency in the exposed group (since dependency scores are more negative = stronger dependency); for direction +1 a positive signed value means weaker dependency in the exposed group; for interactions a positive signed value means the registered focal contrast is larger in the named subgroup than in its complement. Because dependency scores are negative/centered, a literal relative 10% difference is unstable near zero, so I continue to use an absolute dependency-score separation of ~0.1 as the practical-importance benchmark, with sign and uncertainty decisive. The accepted supplied-dataset axes are MSI-high->stronger WRN, KEAP1 loss->weaker NFE2L2, TP53 loss->weaker USP7, SMARCA4 loss->stronger SMARCA2, CDKN2A loss->stronger MDM2, and PTEN loss->stronger STAT3 (the last validated overall and in a driver-negative context). This batch maps the boundary of the PTEN-STAT3 axis and tests target specificity plus the residual MTAP question. PTEN-STAT3 boundary/confounding: H147/H148 (PIK3CA-intact vs mutant) test whether PTEN acts as a coherent PI3K-pathway marker or retains an independent association; H127/H128 (TP53-intact vs loss), H149 (CDKN2A-intact), H150 (SMARCA4-intact) test confounding by the three other accepted axes; H130 (Avana library) is a technical-consistency check mirroring the library strata already done for the other axes. Target specificity for STAT3: H151 (CDKN2A loss on STAT3) and H152 (SMARCA4 loss on STAT3) ask whether the accepted p53-network and chromatin axes leak onto STAT3 (a positive effect would broaden them; a null would reinforce PTEN as the more STAT3-specific predictor here). Residual MTAP question: H153 (MTAP loss on USP7 within TP53-intact cells) probes the TP53-intact side of the attenuation hypothesis, complementing H67/H144/H146 on the TP53-loss side. Cross-repair probes: H154 (KEAP1 loss on WRN) and H155 (MSI-high on USP7) test whether the NRF2/oxidative-stress and dMMR/replication-stress networks modify the WRN and USP7 axes; these are exploratory with uncertain expectations and should not override the established specificity map unless large and precise. All claims remain dataset-specific associations; no causality or external generalizability is inferred, and multiplicity, cell-size dependence, molecular co-occurrence, and library/lineage context remain limits.

record.narrative: I applied the registered signed-direction convention throughout. For direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group because dependency scores are more negative for stronger dependency; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. Because dependency scores are negative-valued and not centered at a stable zero, I continued to use an absolute dependency-score separation of roughly 0.1 as the practical scientific benchmark, with sign and interval precision decisive.  The new PTEN-STAT3 context probes are unusually coherent and large. H127, in TP53-intact cells, estimated +0.287 (95% CI +0.227 to +0.347; n=212 exposed, 1382 comparator), clearly supporting stronger STAT3 dependency with PTEN loss; I accept and close it. H128, in TP53-loss cells, estimated +0.190 (95% CI +0.085 to +0.296; n=54 exposed, 352 comparator), which is positive and above the point threshold but has only modest exposed-cell precision and a lower bound slightly below the 0.1 benchmark. I accept the direction as evidence for a dataset-specific TP53-loss stratum effect, but the exact magnitude is uncertain, so I keep H128 active and request independent validation as the one useful validation for this batch. H130, H147, H148, H149, and H150 further show PTEN-loss stronger STAT3 dependency in Avana library, PIK3CA-intact, PIK3CA-mutant, CDKN2A-intact, and SMARCA4-intact contexts. All estimates are positive, most intervals exclude 0.1, and they support robustness of the PTEN-STAT3 association within these measured contexts. I accept and close these as dataset-specific context checks. I do not interpret them as causal or externally generalizable; residual molecular co-occurrence, lineage subtype context, and multiplicity remain limits.  The specificity checks for STAT3 are clean. H151 tested CDKN2A loss against STAT3 and estimated only -0.005 (95% CI -0.032 to +0.021), rejecting a meaningful CDKN2A-to-STAT3 association. H152 tested SMARCA4 loss against STAT3 and estimated only -0.005 (95% CI -0.032 to +0.022), rejecting a meaningful SMARCA4-to-STAT3 association. Together with earlier PTEN-null results on MDM2 and USP7, this strengthens the interpretation that PTEN loss is relatively STAT3-specific among the axes tested, though it does not prove exclusivity against unmeasured predictors.  The MTAP baseline check H153 asked whether MTAP loss is associated with stronger USP7 dependency among TP53-intact cells. The estimate was -0.019 (95% CI -0.041 to +0.004), entirely below the practical benchmark and not supportive of a stronger-dependency effect. I reject it and close it. This argues against a simple explanation in which TP53-intact MTAP-loss cells alone have stronger USP7 dependency, but it does not resolve the still-imprecise TP53-loss/MTAP-loss attenuation question. The MTAP loose end therefore remains an unresolved exploratory issue, not a confirmed mechanism.  Cross-repair-network probes were uninformative in the direction registered. H154 tested KEAP1 loss against WRN and estimated +0.007 (95% CI -0.023 to +0.037), well below benchmark, so I reject a meaningful KEAP1-to-WRN association. H155 tested MSI-high against USP7 and estimated +0.057 (95% CI -0.013 to +0.127); the point estimate is below the practical benchmark, but the interval admits a modest positive effect, so I leave it unresolved and deferred rather than overclaiming absence of effect.  Overall, the new evidence strongly reinforces PTEN loss as a dataset-specific predictor of stronger STAT3 dependency across several measured strata, while supporting target specificity for the established axes. The only validation request is H128 because it is the newly accepted stratum with the least interval precision and the most direct scientific value in confirming the TP53-loss context of the PTEN-STAT3 axis.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
