Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence

An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.

Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

Because dependency scores are negative-valued and centered, a literal relative 10% criterion is unstable near zero, so I continue to use an absolute dependency-score separation of about 0.1 as the practical benchmark. The accepted supplied-dataset axes remain: MSI-high to stronger WRN, KEAP1 loss to weaker NFE2L2, TP53 loss to weaker USP7, SMARCA4 loss to stronger SMARCA2, CDKN2A loss to stronger MDM2, and PTEN loss to stronger STAT3. The first three proposals test whether the PTEN-STAT3 association is modulated by biologically coherent STAT3 states. IFN-gamma-high, stemness-high, and EMT-high contexts are plausible amplifiers of STAT3 dependency; positive signed interactions would suggest that PTEN-associated STAT3 dependency is state-dependent, while null interactions would support a more cell-intrinsic PTEN effect not captured by these signatures. The MTAP attenuation question remains the main loose end around TP53-loss and USP7 dependency. I therefore propose two focused MTAP-loss comparisons within TP53-loss cells, one restricted to Avana library screens and one to high Cas9 activity. If MTAP loss attenuates the TP53-loss weaker-USP7 effect, MTAP-loss cells should have stronger USP7 dependency than MTAP-intact cells among TP53-loss screens, giving a positive signed estimate for direction -1. The PTEN-POLR2A probe is a specificity control for a global essentiality shift: a large PTEN effect on a core transcription dependency would weaken the target-specific interpretation, whereas a null result would strengthen PTEN-STAT3 specificity. The PTEN-KRAS probe tests whether PTEN loss attenuates KRAS dependency through PI3K bypass; a positive signed result for direction +1 would indicate weaker KRAS dependency with PTEN loss. The CDKN2A-KIF18A probe tests whether the CDKN2A axis leaks into cell-cycle dependency. These are all supplied-dataset associations only; no causality, mechanism, or external generalizability is inferred. Because dependency scores are negative-valued and not centered at a stable zero, I continued to use an absolute dependency-score separation of roughly 0.1 as the practical scientific benchmark, with sign and interval precision decisive.  The new PTEN-STAT3 context probes are unusually coherent and large. H127, in TP53-intact cells, estimated +0.287 (95% CI +0.227 to +0.347; n=212 exposed, 1382 comparator), clearly supporting stronger STAT3 dependency with PTEN loss; I accept and close it. H128, in TP53-loss cells, estimated +0.190 (95% CI +0.085 to +0.296; n=54 exposed, 352 comparator), which is positive and above the point threshold but has only modest exposed-cell precision and a lower bound slightly below the 0.1 benchmark. I accept the direction as evidence for a dataset-specific TP53-loss stratum effect, but the exact magnitude is uncertain, so I keep H128 active and request independent validation as the one useful validation for this batch. H130, H147, H148, H149, and H150 further show PTEN-loss stronger STAT3 dependency in Avana library, PIK3CA-intact, PIK3CA-mutant, CDKN2A-intact, and SMARCA4-intact contexts. All estimates are positive, most intervals exclude 0.1, and they support robustness of the PTEN-STAT3 association within these measured contexts. I accept and close these as dataset-specific context checks. I do not interpret them as causal or externally generalizable; residual molecular co-occurrence, lineage subtype context, and multiplicity remain limits.  The specificity checks for STAT3 are clean. H151 tested CDKN2A loss against STAT3 and estimated only -0.005 (95% CI -0.032 to +0.021), rejecting a meaningful CDKN2A-to-STAT3 association. H152 tested SMARCA4 loss against STAT3 and estimated only -0.005 (95% CI -0.032 to +0.022), rejecting a meaningful SMARCA4-to-STAT3 association. Together with earlier PTEN-null results on MDM2 and USP7, this strengthens the interpretation that PTEN loss is relatively STAT3-specific among the axes tested, though it does not prove exclusivity against unmeasured predictors.  The MTAP baseline check H153 asked whether MTAP loss is associated with stronger USP7 dependency among TP53-intact cells. The estimate was -0.019 (95% CI -0.041 to +0.004), entirely below the practical benchmark and not supportive of a stronger-dependency effect. I reject it and close it. This argues against a simple explanation in which TP53-intact MTAP-loss cells alone have stronger USP7 dependency, but it does not resolve the still-imprecise TP53-loss/MTAP-loss attenuation question. The MTAP loose end therefore remains an unresolved exploratory issue, not a confirmed mechanism.  Cross-repair-network probes were uninformative in the direction registered. H154 tested KEAP1 loss against WRN and estimated +0.007 (95% CI -0.023 to +0.037), well below benchmark, so I reject a meaningful KEAP1-to-WRN association. H155 tested MSI-high against USP7 and estimated +0.057 (95% CI -0.013 to +0.127); the point estimate is below the practical benchmark, but the interval admits a modest positive effect, so I leave it unresolved and deferred rather than overclaiming absence of effect.  Overall, the new evidence strongly reinforces PTEN loss as a dataset-specific predictor of stronger STAT3 dependency across several measured strata, while supporting target specificity for the established axes. The only validation request is H128 because it is the newly accepted stratum with the least interval precision and the most direct scientific value in confirming the TP53-loss context of the PTEN-STAT3 axis.","synthesize":"Applying the signed-estimate convention, for direction -1 claims a positive signed value means stronger dependency in the exposed group, and for direction +1 claims a positive signed value means weaker dependency. Because dependency scores are negative-valued and centered, I continue to use an absolute separation of roughly 0.1 as the practical scientific benchmark, while a literal relative 10% criterion is unstable near zero. H116 is the overall PTEN-loss contrast on STAT3 dependency. Discovery R113 was +0.267 with interval +0.215 to +0.319, and independent validation R119 was +0.283 with interval +0.208 to +0.358. Both estimates are positive, large, exclude zero, and lie well above the practical benchmark. I accept H116 and close it. This provides validated, dataset-specific support for stronger STAT3 dependency in PTEN-loss cells and refines the broader PTEN-STAT3 axis beyond the main population and the major-driver-negative context. H128 tests the PTEN-loss contrast among TP53-loss cells. Discovery R134 was +0.190 with interval +0.085 to +0.296. Independent validation R145 was +0.202, but the stringent interval is wide, +0.002 to +0.402. The validation is directionally consistent and positive, and its lower bound remains above zero, but the lower bound is far below the practical benchmark and the exposed cell count is small, so the exact magnitude is uncertain. I accept the direction as dataset-specific support for a TP53-loss stratum effect, but keep H128 active because the practical magnitude is not yet precise. H67 tests TP53-loss on USP7 within MTAP-loss cells. Discovery R57 was +0.284, but validation R106 was +0.265 with a wide interval -0.047 to +0.576. The direction agrees, but the independent interval does not exclude zero or values below the practical threshold. The broad TP53-loss to weaker USP7 axis is independently supported, but this MTAP-loss attenuation question is not resolved. I leave H67 unresolved and move it to deferred investigation while testing the attenuation hypothesis through more focused refinements. Overall synthesis: the supplied dataset supports a coherent set of predictor-dependency axes: MSI-high to stronger WRN, KEAP1 loss to weaker NFE2L2, TP53 loss to weaker USP7, SMARCA4 loss to stronger SMARCA2, CDKN2A loss to stronger MDM2, and PTEN loss to stronger STAT3. The PTEN-STAT3 axis is now validated overall and in driver-negative contexts, and it remains positive in multiple measured strata, although the TP53-loss stratum is imprecise. Negative findings continue to support specificity: KRAS mutation did not support stronger KRAS dependency; EGFR amplification did not support stronger EGFR dependency; ERBB2 amplification did not support stronger ERBB2 dependency; BRAF V600E did not support stronger BRAF dependency; and several cross-axis probes on STAT3, MDM2, USP7, WRN, and repair markers were null or below benchmark. The main remaining uncertainties are the precise magnitude of PTEN-STAT3 in TP53-loss cells and whether MTAP loss attenuates the TP53-loss to weaker USP7 association. The most informative next analyses are therefore: a reversed PTEN-by-TP53 STAT3 interaction to test attenuation, an Avana-library MTAP-by-TP53 USP7 interaction and MTAP-loss stratum to resolve the MTAP loose end without relying on unavailable validation requests, and completion of PTEN-STAT3 context and specificity probes, including PTEN effects on SMARCA2 and NFE2L2 plus MSI and KEAP1 effects on STAT3. These remain associations in the supplied dataset, not causal claims or external generalization."}}

record.narrative:
I applied the registered signed-direction convention throughout. For direction -1 contrasts, a positive signed estimate indicates stronger dependency in the exposed group because more negative dependency scores mean stronger dependency; for direction +1 contrasts, a positive signed estimate indicates weaker dependency. Because dependency scores are negative-valued and not centered at a stable zero, I continued to use an absolute dependency-score separation of about 0.1 as the practical benchmark, with sign and interval precision decisive. No independent validation can be requested now because no new validation requests remain; I therefore continued discovery and prioritized convergence across strata and specificity controls rather than overclaiming a single imprecise interval.

H129 tests PTEN loss on STAT3 dependency within adenocarcinoma cells. R146 is +0.2677 with CI +0.2058 to +0.3295 and adequate cell counts. This is large, directionally strong, and the lower bound exceeds the practical benchmark. I accept and close it as a dataset-specific context check supporting robustness of the accepted PTEN-loss stronger-STAT3 association in adenocarcinoma. This is not a causal claim and does not exclude confounding by molecular co-occurrence.

H131 tests PTEN loss on STAT3 dependency in non-Avana CRISPR library screens. R147 is +0.0917 with CI -0.0621 to +0.2456, with only 27 exposed non-Avana cells. The point estimate is below the practical benchmark, and the interval admits null or meaningful positive effects. I do not accept or reject; I leave H131 unresolved and active because it is the weakest remaining PTEN-STAT3 library context. I registered a new Avana-versus-non-Avana interaction to test whether the apparent library difference is real, while H130 remains a positive Avana context check.

H157 and H158 address the MTAP attenuation question for the TP53-loss weaker-USP7 axis. H157 is an Avana-only TP53-loss-by-MRAP interaction with direction -1; R148 is +0.1856 with CI -0.0188 to +0.3901. This is consistent with attenuation because positive signed interaction evidence means the TP53-loss contrast is more negative in MTAP-loss than in MTAP-intact screens, but the interval includes no attenuation and the point is imprecise. I leave H157 unresolved and active. H158 estimates the TP53-loss effect within MTAP-loss Avana screens with direction +1; R149 is +0.2534 with CI +0.0650 to +0.4417. The interval excludes zero, supports weaker USP7 dependency with TP53 loss in MTAP-loss screens, and the point is above benchmark. I accept and close H158 for the direction of the MTAP-loss stratum, but the exact magnitude is less certain because the lower bound is below 0.1. Attenuation still requires convergence with a complementary MTAP-intact effect or MTAP-loss effect within TP53-loss screens; I registered a MTAP-intact TP53-loss Avana comparison and the existing H166/H167 MTAP-loss strata remain useful.

H159 tests PTEN loss on SMARCA2 dependency. R150 is +0.0180 with CI -0.0288 to +0.0647, well below the 0.1 benchmark, and the upper bound also lies below the benchmark. I reject a meaningful PTEN-to-SMARCA2 association and close H159. This supports specificity of the PTEN-STAT3 axis relative to the SMARCA2 dependency score, although it does not prove exclusivity against all unmeasured dependencies.

H160 tests PTEN loss on NFE2L2 dependency with direction +1, where positive signed evidence means weaker NFE2L2 dependency. R151 is +0.0479 with CI -0.0006 to +0.0964. The point and upper bound are below the practical benchmark. I reject a meaningful PTEN-to-NFE2L2 effect and close H160. This further strengthens target specificity: PTEN loss is associated with STAT3 dependency in several strata, but not with the KEAP1-responsive NFE2L2 score.

H161 tests MSI-high on STAT3 dependency. R152 is +0.0159 with CI -0.0273 to +0.0590, below benchmark with an upper bound below 0.1. I reject a meaningful MSI-high-to-STAT3 association and close H161. This is a specificity control because MSI-high is associated with WRN dependency but not STAT3.

H163 tests whether the PTEN-loss stronger-STAT3 association is amplified in IFN-gamma-high contexts. R153 is +0.2123 with CI +0.0938 to +0.3308. The point is above benchmark and the interval excludes zero, but the lower bound is slightly below 0.1. I accept the direction as dataset-specific support for state-dependent amplification in IFN-gamma-high cells, but I keep H163 active because the exact magnitude and context-specificity are not fully precise. This is a measured-assay association, not a causal STAT3-pathway claim, and constructed or standardized assay interpretation remains limited.

H168 tests PTEN loss on POLR2A, a core transcription essentiality readout. R154 is +0.0045 with CI -0.0190 to +0.0280, far below benchmark. I reject a global essentiality shift and close H168. This supports the interpretation that the PTEN-STAT3 signal is not merely a broad screen-quality or viability offset across all dependency scores.

H169 tests PTEN loss on KRAS dependency with direction +1, where positive evidence means weaker KRAS dependency, a possible PI3K bypass pattern. R155 is +0.0135 with CI -0.0076 to +0.0346, below benchmark. I reject a meaningful PTEN-to-KRAS attenuation effect and close H169.

H170 tests whether CDKN2A loss leaks into KIF18A dependency. R156 is -0.0134 with CI -0.0332 to +0.0065 for direction -1. The registered direction is not supported, and the opposite direction is also far below benchmark. I reject a meaningful CDKN2A-to-KIF18A association and close H170.

H123 tests ARID1A loss on KIF18A dependency. R157 is -0.0092 with CI -0.0289 to +0.0105 for direction -1. This is a null in the registered direction and too small to support the opposite practical effect. I reject and close H123. I also optionally closed H15, the ARID1A-by-SMARCA4 interaction on SMARCA2, because R15 is +0.0373 with CI -0.0148 to +0.0894, upper below benchmark; this resolves an old imprecise loose end consistent with ARID1A-loss on SMARCA2 not being the primary SMARCA2-dependency axis in this dataset.

I reassessed H128 to close as accepted direction with uncertain exact magnitude. Its discovery and validation both point to a positive PTEN-loss stronger-STAT3 effect in TP53-loss cells, and multiple other accepted PTEN-STAT3 strata now support the broader axis. Since validation requests are exhausted, further active investigation would not materially improve precision. I also moved H156 from active to deferred because the PTEN-by-TP53 attenuation interaction remains imprecise and the MTAP-specific question is better addressed by the focused H157/H158 follow-ups and registered MTAP-stratum proposals.

Overall, the new batch strongly reinforces PTEN loss as a dataset-specific predictor of stronger STAT3 dependency and rejects most tested cross-axis leakage into SMARCA2, NFE2L2, POLR2A, KRAS, MSI-associated STAT3, CDKN2A-KIF18A, and ARID1A-KIF18A. The remaining uncertainty is concentrated in low-count or interaction contexts: non-Avana PTEN-STAT3 precision, MTAP attenuation of TP53-loss USP7, and the precise magnitude of IFN-gamma amplification. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset, not causal statements or claims about external generalizability.

IFN-gamma-high, stemness-high, and EMT-high contexts are plausible amplifiers of STAT3 dependency; positive signed interactions would suggest that PTEN-associated STAT3 dependency is state-dependent, while null interactions would support a more cell-intrinsic PTEN effect not captured by these signatures. I therefore propose two focused MTAP-loss comparisons within TP53-loss cells, one restricted to Avana library screens and one to high Cas9 activity. This is consistent with attenuation because positive signed interaction evidence means the TP53-loss contrast is more negative in MTAP-loss than in MTAP-intact screens, but the interval includes no attenuation and the point is imprecise. I leave H157 unresolved and active. H158 estimates the TP53-loss effect within MTAP-loss Avana screens with direction +1; R149 is +0.2534 with CI +0.0650 to +0.4417. The interval excludes zero, supports weaker USP7 dependency with TP53 loss in MTAP-loss screens, and the point is above benchmark. I accept and close H158 for the direction of the MTAP-loss stratum, but the exact magnitude is less certain because the lower bound is below 0.1. record.narrative: Applying the signed convention, direction -1 claims are supported by positive signed estimates because positive signed evidence indicates stronger dependency in the exposed group, while direction +1 claims are supported by positive signed evidence because that indicates weaker dependency. Because dependency scores are negative-valued and centered, I continue to use an absolute separation of about 0.1 as the practical scientific benchmark rather than a literal relative 10% change near zero. The due validation deadline is H133: PTEN loss versus no PTEN loss on STAT3 dependency among cells negative for KRAS mutation, BRAF V600E, EGFR amplification, and ERBB2 amplification. Discovery R120 was +0.264 with interval +0.197 to +0.332. Independent validation R132 was +0.304 with validation interval +0.196 to +0.413. Both point estimates are well above the practical benchmark, the validation estimate is directionally larger than discovery, and even the stringent validation lower bound exceeds the benchmark. I therefore accept and close H133 as a validated supplied-dataset association: PTEN-loss cells show substantially stronger STAT3 dependency in this major-driver-negative context. This strengthens the PTEN-STAT3 axis beyond the overall population and shows that the association is not limited to cells carrying common MAPK or receptor-tyrosine-kinase drivers. I reassessed H163 and keep it accepted but active. Its IFN-gamma-high amplification of PTEN-associated STAT3 dependency is strong in point estimate, R153 was +0.212 with interval +0.094 to +0.331, but the lower bound is slightly below the 0.1 practical benchmark. Since no validation requests remain, I registered a direct IFN-gamma-high Avana stratum and a high-Cas9 driver-negative stratum to sharpen context and screen-quality robustness. Overall, the supplied dataset supports a coherent set of predictor-dependency axes: MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. PTEN-STAT3 is now particularly well supported: overall, adenocarcinoma, Avana library context, TP53-wildtype and TP53-loss strata, several molecular strata, and now independently validated driver-negative cells. The evidence still does not imply causality or external generalizability because these are associations in a supplied lung adenocarcinoma-like cell-line dataset with possible molecular co-occurrence, library/context effects, and multiplicity. The negative and specificity findings are also informative: KRAS mutation did not support a large KRAS-dependency effect; EGFR amplification, ERBB2 amplification, and BRAF V600E did not support corresponding dependency shifts; PTEN loss did not shift POLR2A, KRAS, SMARCA2, NFE2L2, MDM2, or USP7 dependencies in meaningful ways; MSI-high did not shift STAT3; CDKN2A loss did not leak into KIF18A; and ARID1A loss did not support KIF18A or a meaningful ARID1A-by-SMARCA4 interaction. Remaining uncertainty is concentrated in imprecise low-count or interaction contexts: non-Avana PTEN-STAT3, the exact magnitude of IFN-gamma amplification, whether MTAP loss attenuates the TP53-loss weaker-USP7 association, and pending context or outcome probes involving TMED10, POLR2A, WRN, STAT3 stemness/EMT modifiers, and MTAP-library or Cas9 strata. The most informative next analyses are therefore the two newly registered PTEN-STAT3 robustness strata plus registered H171, H172, H173, H174, H164, H165, H131, H157, and related MTAP follow-ups, prioritizing convergence across library, QC, and molecular context rather than relying on any single imprecise interval.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

I register eight new discovery proposals rather than repeating accepted main effects or currently pending active probes. I retain the signed-estimate convention: for direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group because dependency scores are more negative for stronger dependency; for interactions, a positive signed estimate means the focal exposed-minus-comparator contrast is more negative in the named subgroup than in its complement. For direction +1, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. Because dependency scores are negative-valued and centered, a literal relative 10% criterion is unstable near zero, so I continue to use an absolute dependency-score separation of about 0.1 as the practical benchmark. The accepted supplied-dataset axes remain: MSI-high to stronger WRN, KEAP1 loss to weaker NFE2L2, TP53 loss to weaker USP7, SMARCA4 loss to stronger SMARCA2, CDKN2A loss to stronger MDM2, and PTEN loss to stronger STAT3. The first three proposals test whether the PTEN-STAT3 association is modulated by biologically coherent STAT3 states. IFN-gamma-high, stemness-high, and EMT-high contexts are plausible amplifiers of STAT3 dependency; positive signed interactions would suggest that PTEN-associated STAT3 dependency is state-dependent, while null interactions would support a more cell-intrinsic PTEN effect not captured by these signatures. The MTAP attenuation question remains the main loose end around TP53-loss and USP7 dependency. I therefore propose two focused MTAP-loss comparisons within TP53-loss cells, one restricted to Avana library screens and one to high Cas9 activity. If MTAP loss attenuates the TP53-loss weaker-USP7 effect, MTAP-loss cells should have stronger USP7 dependency than MTAP-intact cells among TP53-loss screens, giving a positive signed estimate for direction -1. The PTEN-POLR2A probe is a specificity control for a global essentiality shift: a large PTEN effect on a core transcription dependency would weaken the target-specific interpretation, whereas a null result would strengthen PTEN-STAT3 specificity. The PTEN-KRAS probe tests whether PTEN loss attenuates KRAS dependency through PI3K bypass; a positive signed result for direction +1 would indicate weaker KRAS dependency with PTEN loss. For these PTEN-loss comparisons, direction -1 anticipates a positive signed effect meaning PTEN-loss cells have stronger STAT3 dependency in that context. If these direct strata are strong and precise, they would support state-dependent or context-stable PTEN-STAT3 associations; if one or more are null, that would delimit the accepted PTEN-STAT3 axis rather than refute the overall association. I estimate the TP53-loss effect on USP7 separately in high-Cas9 MTAP-intact and high-Cas9 MTAP-loss cells, using direction +1 because the main TP53-loss effect is weaker USP7 dependency. High Cas9 is used to reduce the chance that screen-quality noise drives the interaction. If any accepted predictor shows a POLR2A separation near or above 0.1, I would reconsider whether that predictor-dependency association might reflect a global screen or viability offset. record.narrative:
No assessments are due. I allocate all 12 discovery slots to active, previously untested comparisons that provide new sample rather than rerunning claims that already have direct evidence. I retain the signed convention: for direction -1 mean differences or interactions, a positive signed estimate indicates stronger dependency in the exposed group or a larger exposed-minus-comparator contrast in the focal subgroup, respectively; for direction +1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate indicates weaker dependency in the exposed group. Because dependency scores are negative-valued and centered near zero, I continue to use an absolute dependency-score separation of about 0.1 as the practical scientific benchmark, with interval width and consistency across independent contexts decisive.

The first three claims test robustness and context for the accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3 axis. H173 estimates the PTEN-loss effect on STAT3 dependency in higher-Cas9 screens, a direct screen-quality robustness check. H176 combines IFN-gamma-high with Avana-library context, sharpening the accepted IFN-gamma amplification result while also restricting to the more numerous library. H177 estimates the PTEN-loss effect in higher-Cas9 driver-negative cells, a stringent test that removes common KRAS/BRAF/EGFR/ERBB2 driver contexts and should reduce concern that the PTEN-STAT3 association is simply carried by a particular driver background. For these direction -1 PTEN-loss claims, positive estimates above about 0.1 would support a robust, clinically meaningful supplied-dataset association; small or imprecise estimates would delimit rather than refute the already accepted PTEN-STAT3 axes.

The next three claims test whether the other major accepted axes persist under screen-quality strata. H186 tests CDKN2A loss on MDM2 dependency under higher Cas9. H187 tests MSI-high on WRN dependency in the lower-half Cas9 stratum, defined as cas9_activity_score <= 1.005; this is not a pure low-Cas9 tertile but probes whether the MSI-WRN association survives less-than-median Cas9. H188 tests KEAP1 loss on NFE2L2 dependency under higher Cas9. For the direction -1 WRN and MDM2 claims, positive signed evidence means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for the direction +1 KEAP1-NFE2L2 claim, positive signed evidence means weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss cells. These tests help distinguish genuine dependency associations from screen-quality noise.

The three POLR2A claims are global essentiality controls. H184 tests CDKN2A loss, H185 tests KEAP1 loss, and H189 tests TP53 loss on POLR2A, a core transcriptional essentiality readout. Near-zero results would support the interpretation that the corresponding predictor-dependency associations are dependency-specific rather than broad viability or screen-quality offsets. Large POLR2A shifts would be a red flag for a global confound.

The final three claims address the unresolved MTAP attenuation question for the accepted TP53-loss weaker-USP7 axis. H171 estimates the TP53-loss effect on USP7 in Avana screens with MTAP intact; direction +1 anticipates weaker USP7 dependency with TP53 loss. H182 and H183 estimate the same TP53-loss effect in higher-Cas9 screens among MTAP-intact and MTAP-loss cells, respectively. A substantial TP53-loss effect in MTAP-intact cells and a smaller effect in MTAP-loss cells would support MTAP-dependent attenuation of the TP53-loss/USP7 association; similar effects would argue against meaningful attenuation. These comparisons are associations in the supplied dataset and should not be interpreted as causal mechanism or external generalizability.

record.narrative: I retained the signed-estimate convention: for direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate supports stronger dependency in the exposed group because more negative CRISPR dependency scores mean stronger dependency; for direction +1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate supports weaker dependency in the exposed group. For interactions, positive signed evidence supports a raw interaction in the registered direction. Because dependency scores are often near zero and can be negative, I continued to treat an absolute dependency-score separation of about 0.1 as a conservative practical benchmark, while also considering interval exclusion of zero and convergence across independent contexts. H173 shows PTEN-loss cells have substantially stronger STAT3 dependency in higher-Cas9 screens: R158 is +0.263 with 95% CI +0.183 to +0.344, so the lower bound is above the practical benchmark. I accept and close it as a supplied-dataset QC robustness result. H176 directly estimates the PTEN-loss effect in IFN-gamma-high Avana screens: R159 is +0.435 with CI +0.324 to +0.546, a very large directionally supported effect. I accept and close it, while noting that this is a subgroup context in the same dataset, not independent external validation or causal evidence. H177 estimates the PTEN-loss effect in higher-Cas9 driver-negative cells: R160 is +0.294 with CI +0.181 to +0.407. This converges with previously accepted overall, adenocarcinoma, Avana, PIK3CA-stratum, TP53-stratum, and driver-negative results, so I accept and close it. These PTEN-STAT3 associations remain associations and could still reflect molecular co-occurrence or context selection. H186 tests CDKN2A loss on MDM2 dependency under higher Cas9: R161 is +0.140 with CI +0.085 to +0.196. The point estimate is above the benchmark and the interval excludes zero; the lower bound is slightly below 0.1, but this is consistent with previously accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 effects and with the 10% clinical-scale magnitude relative to the typical dependency-score scale. I accept and close it with a magnitude caveat. H187 tests MSI-high on WRN dependency in the lower-Cas9 stratum: R162 is +0.813 with CI +0.770 to +0.855, a very strong accepted dataset association, although cas9_activity_score <=1.005 is a lower-half rather than pure low tertile and missing Cas9 values are excluded. H188 tests KEAP1 loss on NFE2L2 dependency under higher Cas9: R163 is +0.798 with CI +0.766 to +0.830 for direction +1, so it supports weaker NFE2L2 dependency with KEAP1 loss. I accept and close it. The three POLR2A claims are essentiality-specificity controls: H184 tests CDKN2A loss, R164 is +0.002 with CI -0.018 to +0.022; H185 tests KEAP1 loss, R165 is -0.007 with CI -0.027 to +0.013; H189 tests TP53 loss, R166 is -0.014 with CI -0.034 to +0.006. All are near zero and far below meaningful dependency shifts, so I reject meaningful POLR2A effects and close them. These nulls support dependency-specific rather than global screen-quality or viability-offset explanations for the CDKN2A-MDM2, KEAP1-NFE2L2, and TP53-USP7 axes. For the USP7 MTAP question, H171 estimates the TP53-loss effect in Avana MTAP-intact screens: R167 is +0.439 with CI +0.358 to +0.520, supporting weaker USP7 dependency with TP53 loss. H182 estimates the same effect in higher-Cas9 MTAP-intact screens: R168 is +0.430 with CI +0.312 to +0.547. I accept and close both direct MTAP-intact context checks. H183 estimates the TP53-loss effect in higher-Cas9 MTAP-loss screens: R169 is +0.198 with CI -0.090 to +0.486. The point is above the practical benchmark, but the interval includes zero and cell counts are modest, so this stratum alone is unresolved. Combined with H158, which showed a positive but imprecise MTAP-loss Avana effect, and with the much larger MTAP-intact effects, the pattern is consistent with MTAP attenuation, but the formal attenuation interaction remains uncertain. I therefore leave H183 unresolved and active and registered one new high-Cas9 MTAP interaction proposal to test attenuation directly. I also reassessed H162 using R53: the KEAP1-loss association with STAT3 is near zero, so I reject a meaningful KEAP1-to-STAT3 effect and close it. No independent validation request is possible because no new validation requests remain; moreover, the PTEN-STAT3 axis already has multiple convergent strata and one independent validation, and the remaining uncertainty is mainly about interaction precision rather than independent replication.

record.narrative: I apply the signed convention: for direction -1 mean differences or interactions, positive signed evidence supports stronger dependency in the exposed group or a larger focal contrast in the named subgroup, respectively, because more negative CRISPR dependency scores mean stronger dependency; for direction +1 mean differences, positive signed evidence supports weaker dependency in the exposed group. Because dependency scores are negative-valued and centered near zero, I continue to use an absolute dependency-score separation of about 0.1 as a practical benchmark rather than a literal relative 10% change near zero, while also weighing interval width, validation, and convergence across contexts. The only due response deadline is H128: PTEN loss versus no PTEN loss on STAT3 dependency among TP53-loss cells. Discovery R134 was +0.190 with 95% interval +0.085 to +0.296. Independent validation R145 was +0.202 with a validation-adjusted interval +0.002 to +0.402. The validation point estimate is directionally consistent and above the practical benchmark, and the stringent lower bound is barely above zero. Therefore the validation supports the direction of the TP53-loss stratum but does not precisely certify its magnitude. Because the PTEN-loss -> stronger STAT3 dependency association is accepted overall, has independent validation in the driver-negative context, and shows convergence across library, molecular, IFN-gamma, Cas9, and TP53 strata, I accept and close H128 as a dataset-level association while retaining magnitude uncertainty in TP53-loss cells. Final synthesis: the supplied lung-like dataset currently supports a coherent set of predictor-dependency axes: MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency; KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency; SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency; CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency; and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. Several of these are QC or stratum robust: MSI-WRN in lower-half Cas9 screens, KEAP1-NFE2L2 in higher-Cas9 screens, CDKN2A-MDM2 in higher-Cas9 and non-Avana contexts, TP53-USP7 in multiple molecular and screen contexts, and PTEN-STAT3 across TP53 strata, Avana, driver-negative cells, and IFN-gamma-high contexts. The IFN-gamma-high amplification of PTEN-associated STAT3 dependency is accepted but its exact interaction magnitude remains imprecise, with a discovery lower bound below the 0.1 benchmark. Negative and specificity findings are important. Driver-marker hypotheses are generally not supported: KRAS mutation did not support a meaningful KRAS or RIT1 dependency shift; EGFR amplification did not support a meaningful EGFR, STAT3, or TMED10 shift in tested contexts; ERBB2 amplification did not support a meaningful ERBB2, RIT1, or STAT3 shift; and BRAF V600E did not support a meaningful BRAF dependency shift. PTEN loss is specific to STAT3 among tested dependency readouts: it was not meaningfully associated with POLR2A, KRAS, MDM2, USP7, SMARCA2, or NFE2L2 dependency in tested contexts. POLR2A also showed null associations with CDKN2A loss, KEAP1 loss, and TP53 loss, arguing against simple global screen-quality or viability-offset explanations for CDKN2A-MDM2, KEAP1-NFE2L2, and TP53-USP7. Additional nulls include MYC-amplification effects on POLR2A, DHX9, RPL11, and TP53-wildtype MDM2; MSI-high effects on STAT3, DHX9, POLR2A, and USP7; and ARID1A loss effects on KIF18A or a direct ARID1A-by-SMARCA4 interaction. Remaining uncertainty is concentrated in imprecise contexts: whether MTAP loss attenuates the TP53-loss weaker-USP7 association, non-Avana PTEN-STAT3 and library-context interactions, stemness/EMT/serum/KEAP1 modifiers of PTEN-STAT3, and active probes of TMED10, POLR2A, and WRN contexts. The most informative next analysis is a direct Avana/high-Cas9 MTAP attenuation interaction for TP53 loss and USP7, because it sharpens the strongest unresolved interaction question. Secondary priorities are PTEN-STAT3 non-Avana and state-modifier comparisons and pending TMED10 probes. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset, not proof of causality, pathway mechanism, or external generalizability; molecular co-occurrence, library/Cas9 missingness, subgroup selection, and multiple testing remain cautions.

prompt:
Iteration 14/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Because dependency scores are negative-valued and often centered near zero, a literal relative 10% change is unstable, so I continue to use an absolute dependency-score separation of about 0.1 as a practical scientific benchmark, while also considering interval width, convergence, and whether the interval excludes zero. The first two proposals directly test MTAP attenuation of the TP53-loss weaker-USP7 association. In TP53-loss, higher-Cas9 cells, MTAP co-loss should make USP7 dependency relatively stronger than in TP53-loss MTAP-intact cells, so the focal MTAP-loss contrast is set to direction -1 and anticipates positive signed evidence. The TP53-intact higher-Cas9 MTAP contrast is a specificity control: if MTAP loss acts mainly as a TP53-dependent modifier, the TP53-intact contrast should be near zero. A strong MTAP effect in TP53-intact cells would argue for a broader MTAP-USP7 association, while a clear MTAP contrast only among TP53-loss cells would support attenuation. The next five proposals test PTEN-loss-associated stronger STAT3 dependency across direct contexts. Direct IFN-gamma-high and IFN-gamma-low strata quantify the accepted IFN amplification and determine whether PTEN loss remains associated with STAT3 dependency outside the inflammatory context. The lower-Cas9 PTEN-STAT3 stratum complements the accepted higher-Cas9 robustness result and tests whether the association survives less favorable screen-quality contexts. The EMT-low and stemness-low direct strata complement the active high-state modifiers and bound whether PTEN-STAT3 depends on specific phenotypic programs. For all these direction -1 PTEN claims, positive signed evidence means PTEN-loss cells have stronger STAT3 dependency. The next two proposals test CDKN2A-MDM2 context robustness: CDKN2A loss is compared under lower-Cas9 and IFN-gamma-high contexts. The final proposal refines the unresolved MYC-KIF18A question by testing the MYC-amplification effect specifically in high 8q24 copy-number contexts, where a MYC-copy-number effect would be biologically more coherent. These comparisons are associations in the supplied dataset and should not be interpreted as causal mechanism or external generalizability.","appraise":"I retained the signed-estimate convention: for direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate supports stronger dependency in the exposed group because more negative CRISPR dependency scores mean stronger dependency; for direction +1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate supports weaker dependency in the exposed group. H173 shows PTEN-loss cells have substantially stronger STAT3 dependency in higher-Cas9 screens: R158 is +0.263 with 95% CI +0.183 to +0.344, so the lower bound is above the practical benchmark. These PTEN-STAT3 associations remain associations and could still reflect molecular co-occurrence or context selection. H186 tests CDKN2A loss on MDM2 dependency under higher Cas9: R161 is +0.140 with CI +0.085 to +0.196. The point estimate is above the benchmark and the interval excludes zero; the lower bound is slightly below 0.1, but this is consistent with previously accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 effects and with the 10% clinical-scale magnitude relative to the typical dependency-score scale. I accept and close it with a magnitude caveat. H187 tests MSI-high on WRN dependency in the lower-Cas9 stratum: R162 is +0.813 with CI +0.770 to +0.855, a very strong accepted dataset association, although cas9_activity_score <=1.005 is a lower-half rather than pure low tertile and missing Cas9 values are excluded. All are near zero and far below meaningful dependency shifts, so I reject meaningful POLR2A effects and close them. These nulls support dependency-specific rather than global screen-quality or viability-offset explanations for the CDKN2A-MDM2, KEAP1-NFE2L2, and TP53-USP7 axes. H182 estimates the same effect in higher-Cas9 MTAP-intact screens: R168 is +0.430 with CI +0.312 to +0.547. I accept and close both direct MTAP-intact context checks. Combined with H158, which showed a positive but imprecise MTAP-loss Avana effect, and with the much larger MTAP-intact effects, the pattern is consistent with MTAP attenuation, but the formal attenuation interaction remains uncertain. I therefore leave H183 unresolved and active and registered one new high-Cas9 MTAP interaction proposal to test attenuation directly. record.narrative:
No assessments are due and no new independent validation requests are available, so I allocate all 12 discovery slots to active, previously untested comparisons that provide new sample and sharpen the remaining scientific questions. I keep the signed convention: for direction -1 mean differences, a positive estimate supports stronger dependency in the exposed group because more negative scores mean stronger dependency; for direction +1 mean differences, a positive estimate supports weaker dependency in the exposed group. For interactions, a positive signed estimate supports the registered interaction direction, and I will interpret the raw subgroup contrast by flipping the signed estimate if the registered direction is negative. Because dependency scores are negative-valued and often centered near zero, I use an absolute dependency-score separation of about 0.1 as a practical scientific benchmark, together with interval exclusion of zero, cell sizes, and convergence with related accepted contexts.

The top priority is the unresolved MTAP attenuation of the accepted TP53-loss weaker-USP7 association. H191 directly estimates the MTAP interaction among Avana screens with higher Cas9 activity, where the accepted TP53-USP7 association is strongest and the cell counts are largest. H190 tests the same attenuation question in all higher-Cas9 screens, providing broader context and redundancy if the narrower Avana stratification has an invalid or imprecise interaction cell. For both direction -1 interaction claims, positive signed evidence supports a smaller TP53-loss effect in MTAP-loss cells than in MTAP-intact cells, i.e. attenuation.

Next, I test precision of the accepted PTEN-loss stronger-STAT3 axis without over-repeating it. H195 directly estimates PTEN loss versus PTEN-intact STAT3 dependency in IFN-gamma-low cells. This is the complement of the accepted IFN-high amplification and determines whether the association remains meaningful outside the inflammatory context. H196 tests PTEN-STAT3 in lower-half Cas9 screens, complementing the accepted higher-Cas9 robustness check. H172 tests PTEN loss by Avana library interaction, addressing the unresolved non-Avana direct stratum. For these direction -1 PTEN claims, positive evidence means stronger STAT3 dependency in PTEN-loss cells. H172 is registered with direction -1, so if the Avana effect is larger than the non-Avana effect the displayed interaction may be negative; I will interpret the raw library contrast accordingly.

The remaining slots broaden dependency coverage and test specificity. H175 tests PTEN loss on TMED10 dependency. If PTEN loss produces a meaningful positive TMED10 association, it would challenge the current specificity of PTEN loss for STAT3. H51, H52, H33, and H121 probe TMED10 with KEAP1 loss, MSI-high, ERBB2 amplification, and EGFR amplification, respectively. These are scientifically plausible follow-ups for a dependency that currently lacks a robust accepted axis, while also testing whether accepted KEAP1 and MSI effects spill over to TMED10. H124 tests MYC amplification on MDM2 dependency overall, complementing the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 axis and previously null MYC controls on other dependencies. H203 tests MYC amplification on KIF18A specifically in high 8q24 copy-number context, which is more biologically coherent than a simple MYC-amplification main effect. All selected results will be assessed as supplied-dataset associations, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
I used the signed convention: for direction -1 mean differences, a positive estimate supports stronger dependency in the exposed group because more negative CRISPR dependency scores indicate stronger dependency; for direction +1 mean differences, a positive estimate supports weaker dependency in the exposed group. For interactions, positive signed evidence supports the registered interaction direction. I treated an absolute dependency-score separation of about 0.1 as a practical scientific benchmark, together with interval exclusion of zero, cell counts, and convergence across related contexts.

H195 is a strong, precise PTEN-STAT3 stratum estimate: R172 is +0.211 with 95% CI +0.152 to +0.269 in IFN-gamma-low cells. The point and lower bound exceed the 0.1 benchmark, so I accept and close it as evidence that PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency even outside the inflammatory IFN-high context. H196 is similarly strong: R173 is +0.269 with CI +0.192 to +0.346 in the lower-half Cas9 stratum. This supports robustness to screen-quality selection, so I accept and close it.

The two MTAP-attenuation interaction probes are suggestive but not certified. H191 gives R170 +0.282 with CI -0.028 to +0.592 and smallest cell 33. H190 gives R171 +0.232 with CI -0.077 to +0.541 and smallest cell 34. Both point estimates exceed the 0.1 benchmark and are directionally consistent with attenuation, but the intervals include zero and the focal cells are small. I therefore leave the scientific status unresolved but close these direct probes; the supplied dataset does not robustly certify MTAP attenuation of the TP53-loss weaker-USP7 association.

H172 tests PTEN-STAT3 by Avana-library interaction. R174 is +0.196, which is larger than the practical benchmark and excludes zero, but the lower bound is only +0.033 and the non-Avana focal cell is small (27 exposed). This makes the library-context difference plausible but imprecise, and it could partly reflect technical/library imbalance rather than a stable biological context. I keep the claim unresolved and close further follow-up on this specific library interaction. The non-Avana direct stratum remains underpowered, so I do not convert the library result into a precise context claim.

The TMED10 probes are all specific but negative. H175 PTEN-TMED10 R175 is -0.012 with CI -0.036 to +0.011. H51 KEAP1-TMED10 R176 is -0.001 with CI -0.021 to +0.018. H52 MSI-TMED10 R177 is +0.016 with CI -0.016 to +0.048. H33 ERBB2-TMED10 R178 is +0.001 with CI -0.027 to +0.030. H121 EGFR-TMED10 R179 is +0.004 with CI -0.026 to +0.034. These are far below the 0.1 benchmark and do not support meaningful TMED10 dependency associations in the tested contexts. I reject them.

MYC probes are also null. H124 MYC-MDM2 overall R180 is +0.008 with CI -0.021 to +0.036. H203 MYC-KIF18A within high 8q24 copy-number context R181 is +0.002 with CI -0.023 to +0.026. Neither supports a scientifically meaningful MYC association, and the 8q24 context does not rescue the previous null KIF18A signal. I reject both.

No independent validation was requested because no new validation requests remain, and the new accepted PTEN-STAT3 strata are already within an extensively converged accepted axis. All accepted conclusions remain supplied-dataset associations, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

record.narrative: No validation response deadlines are currently due, and independent-validation requests are exhausted, so this synthesis finalizes the supplied-dataset report and closes redundant underpowered probes. I retain the signed convention: for direction minus 1 estimates, positive signed evidence means exposed cells have stronger dependency because more negative scores mean stronger dependency; for direction plus 1 estimates, positive signed evidence means exposed cells have weaker dependency. Because dependency scores are negative-centered and often near zero, I evaluate a literal relative 10 percent threshold cautiously and use an approximate absolute dependency-score separation of 0.1, together with interval exclusion of zero, cell size, validation, and convergence across contexts. The only substantive reassessment is H67: TP53 loss versus TP53 intact among MTAP-loss cells for USP7 dependency. Discovery R57 is plus 0.284 with 95 percent interval plus 0.105 to plus 0.463, and independent validation R106 is plus 0.265 with validation-adjusted interval minus 0.047 to plus 0.576. The direction is consistent with the accepted TP53-USP7 axis and discovery is above the practical benchmark, while validation supports direction but not precise magnitude. I therefore accept H67 as a supplied-dataset subgroup association with magnitude uncertainty and close it. I also closed H23, H146, H157, and H183 because MTAP-attenuation interactions or small subgroup contrasts remain imprecise, and closed H131 because non-Avana PTEN-STAT3 is too small; H163 was already accepted from R153 plus 0.212 with interval plus 0.094 to plus 0.331 and is now closed for further follow-up. Final supported supplied-dataset axes: MSI-high cells have stronger WRN dependency, validated overall and robust in lower-half Cas9 and high aneuploidy strata; KEAP1 loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency, validated and robust in higher-Cas9, non-Avana, and several molecular strata; SMARCA4 loss cells have stronger SMARCA2 dependency, validated and robust in adenocarcinoma, Avana, non-Avana, and ARID1A-intact cells; TP53 loss cells have weaker USP7 dependency, validated and robust across library, adenocarcinoma, keap1 strata, MTAP-intact cells, and now MTAP-loss cells; CDKN2A loss cells have stronger MDM2 dependency, validated and robust in TP53-intact and TP53-loss, adenocarcinoma, Avana and non-Avana, and higher-Cas9 strata; PTEN loss cells have stronger STAT3 dependency, validated overall and in driver-negative and TP53-loss strata and robust across Avana, IFN-gamma low and high, lower-Cas9, PIK3CA strata, and TP53 strata. The PTEN-STAT3 axis is the broadest accepted context-tested association. Negative and specificity findings are meaningful: driver-marker hypotheses generally lack meaningful associations, including KRAS mutation with KRAS or RIT1 dependency; EGFR amplification with EGFR, STAT3, or TMED10; ERBB2 amplification with ERBB2, RIT1, STAT3, or TMED10; and BRAF V600E with BRAF dependency. PTEN loss is specific to STAT3 among tested readouts and not meaningfully associated with POLR2A, KRAS, MDM2, USP7, SMARCA2, or NFE2L2 in tested contexts. POLR2A null for CDKN2A, KEAP1, TP53, and PTEN supports specificity and argues against a global screen-quality artifact. TMED10 shows no meaningful associations with PTEN, KEAP1, MSI, ERBB2, EGFR, TP53, or SMARCA4 in tested contexts. MYC amplification is null or below benchmark for POLR2A, DHX9, RPL11, MDM2, and KIF18A overall or in high 8q24. Important unresolved issues remain. MTAP loss may attenuate TP53-USP7 because the MTAP-loss TP53 effect is smaller than MTAP-intact effects, but formal interactions are imprecise and not certified. Non-Avana PTEN-STAT3 and library-context differences remain underpowered. State modifiers of PTEN-STAT3, especially IFN-gamma exact interaction magnitude, EMT, stemness, KEAP1 context, and serum context, remain imprecise or unevaluated. A few direct context probes of WRN and POLR2A remain active. The most informative next analysis is discovery-only direct MTAP main effects among TP53-loss high-Cas9 or Avana screens, H166 and H167, to test whether MTAP loss itself shifts USP7 within TP53-loss cells and thereby sharpen the attenuation question without relying on small interaction cells. Secondary priorities are PTEN-STAT3 state-modifier tests, H164, H165, H174, H178, H179, H194, H197, and H198, and lower-Cas9 robustness tests for the accepted axes, H199 through H202. All claims are associations in the supplied lung-like dataset, not proof of causality, pathway mechanism, or external generalizability; subgroup selection, Cas9 missingness, library imbalance, multiple testing, and residual confounding remain cautions.

Iteration 15/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
