only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation

All associations supplied-dataset only.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"No assessments are due and no independent validation requests remain, so this stage registers discovery-only comparisons that can sharpen the accepted supplied-dataset axes and the remaining MTAP question. I retain the signed convention: for direction -1 estimates, a positive signed estimate supports stronger dependency in the exposed group because more negative CRISPR scores mean stronger dependency; for direction +1 estimates, a positive signed estimate supports weaker dependency in the exposed group. For raw anticipated direction, negative means I expect exposed-minus-comparator to be more negative, and positive means I expect exposed-minus-comparator to be less negative or positive. Because dependency scores are negative-valued and often centered near zero, a literal 10 percent relative change is unstable for many scores, so I continue to treat an absolute dependency-score separation of roughly 0.1 as a practical scientific benchmark, while also requiring interval separation from zero and adequate cell counts. The first eleven proposals test the six major accepted axes across median-split aneuploidy. Aneuploidy is a measured genome-instability predictor and is scientifically meaningful because it may track copy-number burden, mutation rate, MSI-associated biology, or general chromosomal instability. The accepted WRN axis has already been tested in the high-aneuploidy stratum, so I test WRN in the low-aneuploidy stratum: MSI-high cells should still show stronger WRN dependency if the MSI-WRN association is not confined to highly aneuploid contexts. If the low-aneuploidy estimate is near zero or the interval includes zero, the accepted association may be more context-dependent, although the prior interaction did not robustly reject a difference by aneuploidy. For KEAP1 loss, direction +1, the prediction is weaker NFE2L2 dependency in both high and low aneuploidy strata, consistent with a constitutive KEAP1-NFE2L2 axis. record.narrative:
No assessments are currently due and no new independent validation requests remain, so this analyze stage allocates all 12 discovery slots to active, previously untested claims that are likely to provide new sample. I retain the signed convention: for direction -1 mean differences, a positive estimate supports stronger dependency in the exposed group because more negative CRISPR dependency scores indicate stronger dependency; for direction +1 mean differences, a positive estimate supports weaker dependency in the exposed group. For direction -1 interactions, a positive estimate supports a stronger exposed-minus-comparator contrast in the named subgroup than in its complement. Because dependency scores are negative-centered and many are near zero, I continue to use an approximate absolute dependency-score separation of 0.1 as a practical scientific benchmark alongside interval exclusion of zero and adequate cell counts.

The first priority is the unresolved MTAP-loss attenuation of the accepted TP53-loss weaker-USP7 association. H166 estimates MTAP-loss versus MTAP-intact USP7 dependency directly within TP53-loss Avana screens, and H167 estimates the same contrast within TP53-loss higher-Cas9 screens. Positive signed estimates for these direction -1 claims would support the hypothesis that MTAP-loss TP53-deficient cells have stronger USP7 dependency than MTAP-intact TP53-deficient cells, consistent with attenuation of the TP53 effect. H193 is the TP53-intact high-Cas9 contrast and helps determine whether any MTAP effect is TP53-dependent rather than a general USP7 association.

The second priority is context specificity of the accepted PTEN-loss stronger-STAT3 association. H164 and H165 test whether the PTEN effect is modified by high stemness or high EMT state. H174 tests PTEN loss specifically within KEAP1-loss cells, a cross-pathway test of inflammatory or NRF2-associated context. H178 tests PTEN loss directly within EMT-high cells, providing a magnitude estimate rather than only an interaction. H194 tests PTEN loss within IFN-gamma-high cells, complementing the accepted IFN-low PTEN-STAT3 stratum and the previously Avana-selected IFN-high estimate. These probes are intended to sharpen whether PTEN-STAT3 is a broadly stable supplied-dataset association or whether its magnitude varies across biological states.

The remaining probes test robustness and context dependence of other accepted axes. H199 tests CDKN2A loss on MDM2 dependency in lower-half Cas9 screens. H201 tests KEAP1 loss on NFE2L2 dependency in lower-half Cas9 screens; for this direction +1 claim, positive evidence again supports weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss cells. H202 tests SMARCA4 loss on SMARCA2 dependency in lower-half Cas9 screens. These are important because screen-quality selection could otherwise make accepted axes appear more robust than they are. H214 tests MSI-high versus MSI-stable WRN dependency in the low-aneuploidy stratum, complementing the accepted high-aneuploidy WRN stratum and testing whether the MSI-WRN association survives a less chromosomally unstable background.

I intentionally avoid duplicate or near-duplicate claims and avoid very likely underpowered narrow strata where the focal cell count is known to be near the validity floor. All requested results will be interpreted as associations in the supplied lung-like dataset, not as causal, mechanistic, or externally generalizable claims.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

MTAP attenuation remains unresolved pending these direct MTAP contrasts.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"No assessments are due and no independent validation requests remain, so this stage registers discovery-only comparisons that can sharpen the accepted supplied-dataset axes and the remaining MTAP question. I retain the signed convention: for direction -1 estimates, a positive signed estimate supports stronger dependency in the exposed group because more negative CRISPR scores mean stronger dependency; for direction +1 estimates, a positive signed estimate supports weaker dependency in the exposed group. For raw anticipated direction, negative means I expect exposed-minus-comparator to be more negative, and positive means I expect exposed-minus-comparator to be less negative or positive. Because dependency scores are negative-valued and often centered near zero, a literal 10 percent relative change is unstable for many scores, so I continue to treat an absolute dependency-score separation of roughly 0.1 as a practical scientific benchmark, while also requiring interval separation from zero and adequate cell counts. The first eleven proposals test the six major accepted axes across median-split aneuploidy. Aneuploidy is a measured genome-instability predictor and is scientifically meaningful because it may track copy-number burden, mutation rate, MSI-associated biology, or general chromosomal instability. The accepted WRN axis has already been tested in the high-aneuploidy stratum, so I test WRN in the low-aneuploidy stratum: MSI-high cells should still show stronger WRN dependency if the MSI-WRN association is not confined to highly aneuploid contexts. If the low-aneuploidy estimate is near zero or the interval includes zero, the accepted association may be more context-dependent, although the prior interaction did not robustly reject a difference by aneuploidy. For KEAP1 loss, direction +1, the prediction is weaker NFE2L2 dependency in both high and low aneuploidy strata, consistent with a constitutive KEAP1-NFE2L2 axis. For SMARCA4 loss, direction -1, the prediction is stronger SMARCA2 dependency in both aneuploidy strata, consistent with SMARCA4-SMARCA2 synthetic lethality not depending strongly on genome-wide chromosomal instability. For TP53 loss, direction +1, the prediction is weaker USP7 dependency across aneuploidy strata, testing whether the broad TP53-USP7 association survives a more chromosomally unstable or more stable background. For CDKN2A loss, direction -1, the prediction is stronger MDM2 dependency in both strata, testing whether this deletion effect is not simply an artifact of high copy-number burden. For PTEN loss, direction -1, the prediction is stronger STAT3 dependency in both aneuploidy strata, testing whether PTEN-STAT3 remains present across genome-instability states. Alternatives for each are: a robust positive signed estimate near the accepted magnitude, a smaller but meaningful stratum-specific attenuation, a null estimate indicating a context-dependent effect, or insufficient valid cells. The final proposal targets the unresolved MTAP attenuation question more directly. The accepted TP53-USP7 association is that TP53 loss corresponds to weaker USP7 dependency. The interaction probes suggested that MTAP loss may attenuate this attenuation, but the formal interactions were imprecise. This proposal estimates the MTAP-loss main contrast within TP53-loss, Avana, higher-Cas9 cells, a population chosen to be more homogeneous in technical context. If attenuation is real, MTAP-loss cells should have stronger USP7 dependency than MTAP-intact cells within TP53 loss, giving raw negative and signed positive evidence for direction -1. If there is no MTAP effect, the interval should include zero and the estimate should be small. A large effect in this cell could indicate a strong TP53-dependent MTAP modifier, but still should not be interpreted as causal without mechanistic validation. All proposals are supplied-dataset associations and do not establish causality, pathway mechanism, or external generalizability.","analyze":"No assessments are currently due and no new independent validation requests remain, so this analyze stage allocates all 12 discovery slots to active, previously untested claims that are likely to provide new sample. The only substantive reassessment is H67: TP53 loss versus TP53 intact among MTAP-loss cells for USP7 dependency. Final supported supplied-dataset axes: MSI-high cells have stronger WRN dependency, validated overall and robust in lower-half Cas9 and high aneuploidy strata; KEAP1 loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency, validated and robust in higher-Cas9, non-Avana, and several molecular strata; SMARCA4 loss cells have stronger SMARCA2 dependency, validated and robust in adenocarcinoma, Avana, non-Avana, and ARID1A-intact cells; TP53 loss cells have weaker USP7 dependency, validated and robust across library, adenocarcinoma, keap1 strata, MTAP-intact cells, and now MTAP-loss cells; CDKN2A loss cells have stronger MDM2 dependency, validated and robust in TP53-intact and TP53-loss, adenocarcinoma, Avana and non-Avana, and higher-Cas9 strata; PTEN loss cells have stronger STAT3 dependency, validated overall and in driver-negative and TP53-loss strata and robust across Avana, IFN-gamma low and high, lower-Cas9, PIK3CA strata, and TP53 strata. The PTEN-STAT3 axis is the broadest accepted context-tested association. Negative and specificity findings are meaningful: driver-marker hypotheses generally lack meaningful associations, including KRAS mutation with KRAS or RIT1 dependency; EGFR amplification with EGFR, STAT3, or TMED10; ERBB2 amplification with ERBB2, RIT1, STAT3, or TMED10; and BRAF V600E with BRAF dependency. PTEN loss is specific to STAT3 among tested readouts and not meaningfully associated with POLR2A, KRAS, MDM2, USP7, SMARCA2, or NFE2L2 in tested contexts. POLR2A null for CDKN2A, KEAP1, TP53, and PTEN supports specificity and argues against a global screen-quality artifact. TMED10 shows no meaningful associations with PTEN, KEAP1, MSI, ERBB2, EGFR, TP53, or SMARCA4 in tested contexts. MYC amplification is null or below benchmark for POLR2A, DHX9, RPL11, MDM2, and KIF18A overall or in high 8q24. Important unresolved issues remain. MTAP loss may attenuate TP53-USP7 because the MTAP-loss TP53 effect is smaller than MTAP-intact effects, but formal interactions are imprecise and not certified. Non-Avana PTEN-STAT3 and library-context differences remain underpowered. State modifiers of PTEN-STAT3, especially IFN-gamma exact interaction magnitude, EMT, stemness, KEAP1 context, and serum context, remain imprecise or unevaluated. A few direct context probes of WRN and POLR2A remain active. The most informative next analysis is discovery-only direct MTAP main effects among TP53-loss high-Cas9 or Avana screens, H166 and H167, to test whether MTAP loss itself shifts USP7 within TP53-loss cells and thereby sharpen the attenuation question without relying on small interaction cells. Secondary priorities are PTEN-STAT3 state-modifier tests, H164, H165, H174, H178, H179, H194, H197, and H198, and lower-Cas9 robustness tests for the accepted axes, H199 through H202. record.narrative: I used the signed convention: for direction -1 mean differences and interactions, positive evidence supports stronger dependency in the exposed or focal contrast because more negative CRISPR scores indicate stronger dependency; for direction +1 claims, positive evidence supports weaker dependency in the exposed group. I evaluated practical importance using the supplied 10 percent relative rule together with an approximate absolute dependency-score separation of 0.1, interval exclusion of zero, cell sizes, and convergence across related contexts. H166 (R182 +0.167, CI -0.036 to +0.370) and H167 (R183 +0.206, CI -0.102 to +0.513) are directionally consistent with MTAP-loss strengthening USP7 dependency among TP53-loss cells, but both intervals cross zero and focal cells are small (67 and 34 exposed), so these direct attenuation probes remain unresolved and are closed to further immediate follow-up; I assess H167 once as the canonical direct MTAP-loss/TP53-loss/high-Cas9 probe rather than repeating the duplicate H192. H193 (R184 -0.026, CI -0.062 to +0.010) rejects a positive MTAP-loss stronger-USP7 effect in TP53-intact higher-Cas9 screens because the point is negative and the upper bound is far below the practical benchmark. H164 (R185 -0.010, CI -0.130 to +0.110) is a near-null stemness interaction with wide uncertainty, so it remains unresolved and deferred pending direct stemness strata. H165 (R186 +0.141, CI +0.011 to +0.271) has a positive EMT interaction above the benchmark, but the lower bound is close to null and the focal cell is modest; I revise the previous reject to unresolved and defer it, while accepting the direct EMT-high stratum H178. The accepted direct PTEN-STAT3 strata are precise: H174 within KEAP1-loss R187 +0.247 (CI +0.133 to +0.361), H178 within EMT-high R188 +0.378 (CI +0.261 to +0.495), and H194 within IFN-gamma-high R189 +0.423 (CI +0.319 to +0.526), all with lower bounds above 0.1 and adequate cells. H199 (R190 +0.099, CI +0.049 to +0.150) is modestly below the absolute benchmark but the lower bound is clinically meaningful relative to the MDM2 mean, it excludes zero, and it adds lower-Cas9 robustness to the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 axis; I accept with magnitude uncertainty. H201, H202, and H214 are strong and precise: lower-Cas9 KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 +0.797 (CI +0.766 to +0.828), lower-Cas9 SMARCA4-loss stronger SMARCA2 +0.771 (CI +0.742 to +0.801), and low-aneuploidy MSI-high stronger WRN +0.776 (CI +0.733 to +0.820). Overall, this round strengthens robustness and context coverage of the major accepted supplied-dataset axes without certifying MTAP attenuation or precise EMT/stemness interaction magnitudes. No validation was requested because voluntary validation requests are exhausted. All conclusions are associations in the supplied lung-like dataset, not causal or externally generalizable claims; multiplicity, subgroup selection, Cas9 and library missingness, co-mutation confounding, and residual technical effects remain cautions.

For raw anticipated direction, negative means I expect exposed-minus-comparator to be more negative, and positive means I expect exposed-minus-comparator to be less negative or positive. Because dependency scores are negative-valued and often centered near zero, a literal 10 percent relative change is unstable for many scores, so I continue to treat an absolute dependency-score separation of roughly 0.1 as a practical scientific benchmark, while also requiring interval separation from zero and adequate cell counts. The first eleven proposals test the six major accepted axes across median-split aneuploidy. Aneuploidy is a measured genome-instability predictor and is scientifically meaningful because it may track copy-number burden, mutation rate, MSI-associated biology, or general chromosomal instability. The accepted WRN axis has already been tested in the high-aneuploidy stratum, so I test WRN in the low-aneuploidy stratum: MSI-high cells should still show stronger WRN dependency if the MSI-WRN association is not confined to highly aneuploid contexts. If the low-aneuploidy estimate is near zero or the interval includes zero, the accepted association may be more context-dependent, although the prior interaction did not robustly reject a difference by aneuploidy. For KEAP1 loss, direction +1, the prediction is weaker NFE2L2 dependency in both high and low aneuploidy strata, consistent with a constitutive KEAP1-NFE2L2 axis. For SMARCA4 loss, direction -1, the prediction is stronger SMARCA2 dependency in both aneuploidy strata, consistent with SMARCA4-SMARCA2 synthetic lethality not depending strongly on genome-wide chromosomal instability. For TP53 loss, direction +1, the prediction is weaker USP7 dependency across aneuploidy strata, testing whether the broad TP53-USP7 association survives a more chromosomally unstable or more stable background. For CDKN2A loss, direction -1, the prediction is stronger MDM2 dependency in both strata, testing whether this deletion effect is not simply an artifact of high copy-number burden. For PTEN loss, direction -1, the prediction is stronger STAT3 dependency in both aneuploidy strata, testing whether PTEN-STAT3 remains present across genome-instability states. Alternatives for each are: a robust positive signed estimate near the accepted magnitude, a smaller but meaningful stratum-specific attenuation, a null estimate indicating a context-dependent effect, or insufficient valid cells. record.narrative: No independent validation response deadlines are due, and voluntary validation requests are exhausted, so this synthesis does not request new validation and instead finalizes the supplied-dataset report and curates the active discovery queue. I retained the signed convention used throughout: for direction -1 contrasts, a positive signed estimate means exposed cells have stronger dependency because more negative CRISPR scores mean stronger dependency; for direction +1 contrasts, a positive signed estimate means exposed cells have weaker dependency. Because dependency scores are negative-centered and many comparisons involve values near zero, I interpreted the 10% clinical-significance threshold relative to the comparator/mean dependency magnitude and used an approximate absolute separation near 0.1 as a conservative practical benchmark when a literal percentage is unstable; the principal accepted axes far exceed this standard, while smaller accepted effects were accepted only when the relative magnitude, interval exclusion of zero, and convergence across related contexts were compelling. I closed several unanalyzed low-priority active probes: H55 and H143 because POLR2A has repeatedly failed to show meaningful associations with candidate molecular predictors, reducing the chance that new POLR2A probes are informative; H132 because PTEN's broad specificity has already been demonstrated across multiple non-STAT3 outcomes and WRN-PTEN is now lower priority; and H215 because the MTAP-loss probe restricted simultaneously to TP53-loss, Avana, and higher Cas9 is too narrow and small to resolve the attenuation question. I deferred secondary robustness probes H200 and H206-H211 to reserve the next 12-slot analysis window for the most decisive remaining questions. The supported axes are: MSI-high cells show strongly increased WRN dependency, validated overall and robust across Cas9 and aneuploidy-related strata; KEAP1-loss cells show strongly weaker NFE2L2 dependency, validated and robust across Cas9, lineage, and several technical strata; SMARCA4-loss cells show strongly increased SMARCA2 dependency, validated and robust across ARID1A status, lineage, libraries, and Cas9 strata; TP53-loss cells show weaker USP7 dependency, validated and robust across libraries, lineage, KEAP1 and MTAP strata; CDKN2A-loss cells show increased MDM2 dependency, validated and robust across TP53 status, libraries, lineage, and Cas9 strata; and PTEN-loss cells show increased STAT3 dependency, validated overall and broadly consistent across TP53 status, driver-negative eligibility, PIK3CA status, CDKN2A/SMARCA4-intact contexts, library, Cas9, IFN-gamma, EMT-high, and KEAP1-loss contexts. Negative findings are also scientifically meaningful: driver-marker hypotheses for KRAS, EGFR, ERBB2, and BRAF generally do not show meaningful gene-specific dependencies or consistent downstream dependencies in tested contexts; MYC amplification is null for POLR2A, DHX9, RPL11, MDM2, and KIF18A; PTEN loss is specific to STAT3 among the other tested dependency readouts; and TMED10 and many POLR2A readouts are null in tested contexts, supporting specificity rather than a global screen-quality artifact. The main unresolved issue is MTAP attenuation of the TP53-USP7 axis: the TP53-loss weaker-USP7 effect is smaller among MTAP-loss cells than MTAP-intact cells, but the direct MTAP-loss versus MTAP-intact effect within TP53-loss remains imprecise. I therefore registered two focused direct MTAP main effects within TP53-loss: an overall TP53-loss probe and a lower-Cas9 probe. These are the most informative next analyses because they test whether MTAP loss directly strengthens USP7 dependency within TP53-deficient cells rather than relying on small interaction cells. In parallel, the active queue retains direct PTEN-STAT3 context probes for EMT-low, stemness-high and stemness-low, serum 10% and 2%, plus selected NFE2L2 and STAT3 aneuploidy robustness tests. If direct MTAP effects become positive with intervals excluding zero and exceeding the practical benchmark, the supplied data would support MTAP loss as a modifier that partially offsets TP53-loss-related USP7 hypo-dependency. If they are null, the apparent attenuation should remain a hypothesis generated by subgroup contrasts rather than an established modifier effect. All conclusions are associations in this supplied lung-like dataset; causality, pathway mechanism, clinical actionability, and external generalizability remain unestablished because of possible co-mutation confounding, Cas9/library missingness, technical batch effects, multiple testing, and subgroup selection.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative:
No assessments are currently due and independent validation requests are exhausted, so this analyze stage uses all 12 slots for previously registered, previously untested discovery claims that are likely to yield new sample. I avoided cached probes such as H216 because it displays R130 and would not provide a new discovery result. I retained the signed convention: for direction -1 contrasts, positive evidence supports stronger dependency in the exposed/focal group because more negative CRISPR scores mean stronger dependency; for direction +1 contrasts, positive evidence supports weaker dependency in the exposed/focal group. I continue to judge practical importance using the supplied relative rule together with an approximate absolute dependency-score separation near 0.1, interval exclusion of zero, and cell-size validity.

The first priority is technical robustness of the accepted TP53-loss weaker-USP7 axis in lower-Cas9 screens: H218 directly estimates TP53-loss versus TP53-intact USP7 dependency with Cas9_activity_score <= 1.005. This complements the accepted high-Cas9 direct effect and helps determine whether screen-quality selection contributed to that accepted supplied-dataset association. The second priority is the unresolved MTAP attenuation question: H217 directly estimates MTAP-loss versus MTAP-intact USP7 dependency within TP53-loss lower-Cas9 screens. A positive signed estimate above the practical benchmark would support MTAP loss as a modifier within TP53-deficient cells; a null or small estimate would keep the attenuation hypothesis unresolved.

The next six slots probe context specificity of the accepted PTEN-loss stronger-STAT3 association. H180 and H181 directly estimate PTEN-loss versus PTEN-intact STAT3 dependency in serum-10 and serum-2 contexts, testing whether the effect survives different serum culture states. H197 estimates the PTEN effect directly in EMT-low cells, complementing the accepted EMT-high stratum and testing whether the effect is confined to mesenchymal-like cells. H179 estimates it directly in high-stemness cells, giving a direct magnitude check after the near-null stemness interaction. H219 and H221 estimate the PTEN effect in high-hypoxia and high-proliferation contexts, respectively, allowing a more direct test of whether these biological states attenuate or preserve the PTEN-STAT3 supplied-dataset association. These are selected to sharpen context specificity while avoiding excessive reliance on interaction-only estimates.

The remaining slots test robustness of other accepted axes and cross-context independence. H204 and H205 directly estimate KEAP1-loss versus KEAP1-intact NFE2L2 dependency in high- and low-aneuploidy strata, testing whether the huge KEAP1-NFE2L2 association is robust to chromosomal-instability background. H223 tests the TP53-loss weaker-USP7 association directly within PTEN-loss cells, while H224 tests the CDKN2A-loss stronger-MDM2 association directly within PTEN-loss cells. These cross-context direct effects test whether the TP53-USP7 and CDKN2A-MDM2 axes remain in a PTEN-loss background and are not merely carried by the main accepted effects across the whole population. All results will remain associations in the supplied lung-like dataset, with cautions for multiple testing, subgroup selection, missingness, co-mutation confounding, and residual technical effects.

results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

I therefore registered two focused direct MTAP main effects within TP53-loss: an overall TP53-loss probe and a lower-Cas9 probe. These are the most informative next analyses because they test whether MTAP loss directly strengthens USP7 dependency within TP53-deficient cells rather than relying on small interaction cells. In parallel, the active queue retains direct PTEN-STAT3 context probes for EMT-low, stemness-high and stemness-low, serum 10% and 2%, plus selected NFE2L2 and STAT3 aneuploidy robustness tests. If direct MTAP effects become positive with intervals excluding zero and exceeding the practical benchmark, the supplied data would support MTAP loss as a modifier that partially offsets TP53-loss-related USP7 hypo-dependency. If they are null, the apparent attenuation should remain a hypothesis generated by subgroup contrasts rather than an established modifier effect. record.narrative: I assessed the twelve newly delivered discovery results using the signed convention: for direction -1 contrasts, a positive estimate supports stronger dependency in the exposed/focal group because more negative CRISPR scores mean stronger dependency; for direction +1 contrasts, a positive estimate supports weaker dependency in the exposed group. I judged acceptance using interval exclusion of zero, practical magnitude, cell sizes, and whether the result was a genuine robustness/context test rather than another slice of an already accepted association. For dependency scores that are negative and often near zero, I used an approximate absolute separation near 0.1 as a conservative practical benchmark alongside the supplied relative rule. H218 (TP53-loss versus intact USP7 in lower-Cas9 screens) accepted: R194 +0.413 (95% CI +0.308 to +0.519). This shows the accepted TP53-loss weaker-USP7 supplied-dataset association is not confined to higher-Cas9 screens, though Cas9_activity_score is incomplete and the result is not causal. H180, H181, H179, H197, H219, and H221 accepted the direct PTEN-loss versus PTEN-intact STAT3 contrast across serum-10, serum-2, stemness-high, EMT-low, high-hypoxia, and high-proliferation contexts respectively: R196 +0.286 (+0.216 to +0.357), R197 +0.275 (+0.151 to +0.398), R199 +0.260 (+0.155 to +0.364), R198 +0.237 (+0.179 to +0.295), R200 +0.236 (+0.133 to +0.339), and R201 +0.288 (+0.212 to +0.363). These are large, precise, and mostly have lower bounds above the practical benchmark; H181 is slightly smaller but still meaningful and excludes zero. They should not be overcounted as independent replications because they are overlapping context-specific slices of the same broad PTEN-loss stronger-STAT3 association, which was already validated overall. H204 and H205 accepted KEAP1-loss versus KEAP1-intact NFE2L2 in high and low aneuploidy halves: R202 +0.794 (+0.766 to +0.822) and R203 +0.797 (+0.768 to +0.826). record.narrative: No new independent-validation response deadlines are present and voluntary validation requests are exhausted, so this synthesis finalizes the supplied-dataset interpretation from the already integrated discovery and validation evidence. I retained the signed convention throughout: for direction -1 contrasts, positive evidence means the exposed/focal group has stronger dependency because more negative CRISPR scores mean stronger dependency; for direction +1 contrasts, positive evidence means the exposed/focal group has weaker dependency. Because dependency scores are negative-centered and often near zero, I used the supplied relative 10% rule together with a conservative absolute dependency-score separation of about 0.1 as a practical benchmark, while emphasizing interval exclusion of zero and convergent validation where available. Major supported associations in this supplied lung-like dataset are: MSI-high cells have strongly greater WRN dependency, H10 discovery +0.790 with validation +0.799 and robustness across Cas9 and aneuploidy-related strata; KEAP1-loss cells have strongly weaker NFE2L2 dependency, H13 discovery +0.796 with validation +0.799 and robustness across lineage, Cas9, library, and aneuploidy strata; SMARCA4-loss cells have strongly greater SMARCA2 dependency, H20 discovery +0.784 with validation +0.790 and robustness across ARID1A status, lineage, libraries, and Cas9 strata, while ARID1A loss alone is null; TP53-loss cells have weaker USP7 dependency, H11 discovery +0.396 with validation +0.448 and robustness across libraries, lineage, Cas9, KEAP1 and MTAP strata; CDKN2A-loss cells have greater MDM2 dependency, H106 discovery +0.117 and TP53 stratum effects validated at approximately +0.12 to +0.13, with consistency across libraries, Cas9, lineage, and PTEN-loss background; and PTEN-loss cells have greater STAT3 dependency, H116 discovery +0.267 with validation +0.283 and broad consistency across TP53 status, driver-negative eligibility, PIK3CA status, CDKN2A and SMARCA4 contexts, library, Cas9, IFN-gamma, EMT, stemness, hypoxia, proliferation, and serum contexts. These axes are large relative to the comparator and far above the 0.1 practical absolute benchmark, and the main axes received independent validation. Context-specific acceptances should not be counted as separate replications because they overlap with the broad validated effects; their value is showing that the effects are not obviously confined to a small subgroup. Negative and specificity findings are also important. Driver-gene hypotheses were not supported: KRAS mutation did not indicate stronger KRAS dependency H1; EGFR amplification did not indicate stronger EGFR dependency H3 with null validation; ERBB2 amplification did not indicate stronger ERBB2 dependency H4; BRAF V600E did not indicate stronger BRAF dependency H5; and many related subgroup, co-mutation, and interaction refinements were null. MYC amplification was null for the tested core outputs POLR2A, DHX9, RPL11, MDM2, and KIF18A. TMED10 was generally null across tested predictors, and many POLR2A comparisons were null. PTEN loss was not a global dependency shift: it was not meaningfully associated with MDM2 H137, USP7 H138, SMARCA2 H159, NFE2L2 H160, or POLR2A H168, supporting specificity for STAT3 among the tested readouts. ARID1A loss alone was not associated with SMARCA2 dependency and did not appear necessary for the SMARCA4-loss axis. The main unresolved scientific issue is MTAP attenuation of the TP53-USP7 axis. TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency appears smaller among MTAP-loss cells than MTAP-intact cells, with the direct TP53 effect in MTAP-loss cells H67 about +0.284 compared with about +0.421 in MTAP-intact cells H68, but the interaction H18 is imprecise and the direct MTAP-loss versus MTAP-intact effect within TP53-loss is directionally positive yet underpowered: H216 +0.119 with interval -0.075 to +0.312, and the lower-Cas9 stratum H217 +0.144 with interval -0.146 to +0.434. This is consistent with MTAP loss partially offsetting TP53-loss-related USP7 hypo-dependency, but it does not establish a scientifically meaningful modifier effect. I closed PTEN-loss versus PTEN-intact STAT3 probes by high versus low aneuploidy, H212 and H213, because the PTEN-STAT3 association was validated overall and is already supported across many independent-context direct estimates; testing additional overlapping strata adds little compared with resolving the MTAP question. The most informative next analysis is a focused direct estimate of MTAP-loss versus MTAP-intact USP7 dependency among TP53-loss cells, H216 and any carefully pre-specified technical strata, with the following interpretation: a positive effect with lower bound above the practical benchmark would support MTAP loss as an offsetting modifier of TP53-loss-associated USP7 hypo-dependency, whereas a null or small precise effect would leave the attenuation pattern as a subgroup-generated hypothesis. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset; causality, pathway mechanism, clinical actionability, and external generalizability remain unestablished because of possible co-mutation confounding, incomplete Cas9 and growth-rate data, library and batch effects, multiple testing, and subgroup selection.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

record.narrative: No assessments are due and voluntary independent validation is exhausted, so this explore stage registers targeted follow-up comparisons for the main unresolved scientific question: whether MTAP loss attenuates the accepted TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency, or whether this apparent attenuation is an artifact of technical screen quality, subgroup selection, or genomic co-deletion context. I retain the signed convention: for direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate supports stronger USP7 dependency in the exposed/focal group because more negative CRISPR dependency scores indicate stronger dependency; for a direction -1 interaction, a positive signed estimate supports a raw negative interaction. For USP7, I use an approximate absolute dependency-score separation near 0.1 as a practical benchmark together with interval exclusion of zero and cell-size validity. The first proposal directly estimates MTAP-loss versus MTAP-intact USP7 dependency among TP53-loss cells in higher screen_roc_auc screens. Expected direction is negative raw, or positive signed under direction -1: MTAP-loss cells should show relatively stronger USP7 dependency than MTAP-intact TP53-loss cells if MTAP loss partially offsets TP53-loss-associated USP7 hypo-dependency, especially when technical screen discrimination is higher. The second proposal estimates the same direct MTAP contrast in lower screen_roc_auc screens as a technical-quality complement; a similar positive signed effect would make the attenuation less likely to be confined to selected high-quality screens, whereas a null or materially smaller effect would suggest the apparent MTAP signal may depend on screen-quality stratification or noise. The third proposal directly estimates the TP53-loss effect interaction with MTAP loss within higher screen_roc_auc screens. The raw expected interaction is negative, so under direction -1 positive signed evidence supports attenuation: TP53-loss weaker USP7 dependency is smaller in MTAP-loss cells than in MTAP-intact complement cells. The fourth and fifth proposals test a genomic confounding alternative. MTAP and CDKN2A are genomically linked, and CDKN2A-loss has an independent accepted axis toward stronger MDM2 dependency. If CDKN2A-loss itself mimics the MTAP-loss effect among TP53-loss cells, positive signed evidence for stronger USP7 dependency would support 9p21 co-deletion confounding of the MTAP attenuation signal; if CDKN2A-loss has no comparable effect, especially in higher-quality screens, the attenuation pattern is more likely to reflect MTAP-specific context rather than generic co-deletion. These comparisons remain associations in the supplied lung-like dataset and do not establish causality, mechanism, clinical actionability, or external generalizability. Some comparisons may fail the 20-observation-per-cell rule, and all interpretations should remain cautious about multiple testing and subgroup selection.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

If high screen_roc_auc direct and interaction probes remain imprecise, keep the MTAP attenuation hypothesis unresolved rather than treating the small positive H216 estimate as a scientifically meaningful modifier effect.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"No assessments are due and voluntary independent validation is exhausted, so this explore stage registers targeted follow-up comparisons for the main unresolved scientific question: whether MTAP loss attenuates the accepted TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency, or whether this apparent attenuation is an artifact of technical screen quality, subgroup selection, or genomic co-deletion context. I retain the signed convention: for direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate supports stronger USP7 dependency in the exposed/focal group because more negative CRISPR dependency scores indicate stronger dependency; for a direction -1 interaction, a positive signed estimate supports a raw negative interaction. For USP7, I use an approximate absolute dependency-score separation near 0.1 as a practical benchmark together with interval exclusion of zero and cell-size validity. The first proposal directly estimates MTAP-loss versus MTAP-intact USP7 dependency among TP53-loss cells in higher screen_roc_auc screens. Expected direction is negative raw, or positive signed under direction -1: MTAP-loss cells should show relatively stronger USP7 dependency than MTAP-intact TP53-loss cells if MTAP loss partially offsets TP53-loss-associated USP7 hypo-dependency, especially when technical screen discrimination is higher. The second proposal estimates the same direct MTAP contrast in lower screen_roc_auc screens as a technical-quality complement; a similar positive signed effect would make the attenuation less likely to be confined to selected high-quality screens, whereas a null or materially smaller effect would suggest the apparent MTAP signal may depend on screen-quality stratification or noise. The third proposal directly estimates the TP53-loss effect interaction with MTAP loss within higher screen_roc_auc screens. The raw expected interaction is negative, so under direction -1 positive signed evidence supports attenuation: TP53-loss weaker USP7 dependency is smaller in MTAP-loss cells than in MTAP-intact complement cells. The fourth and fifth proposals test a genomic confounding alternative. MTAP and CDKN2A are genomically linked, and CDKN2A-loss has an independent accepted axis toward stronger MDM2 dependency. If CDKN2A-loss itself mimics the MTAP-loss effect among TP53-loss cells, positive signed evidence for stronger USP7 dependency would support 9p21 co-deletion confounding of the MTAP attenuation signal; if CDKN2A-loss has no comparable effect, especially in higher-quality screens, the attenuation pattern is more likely to reflect MTAP-specific context rather than generic co-deletion.
