A positive signed estimate above the practical benchmark would support MTAP loss as a modifier within TP53-deficient cells; a null or small estimate would keep the attenuation hypothesis unresolved.\n\nThe next six slots probe context specificity of the accepted PTEN-loss stronger-STAT3 association. H180 and H181 directly estimate PTEN-loss versus PTEN-intact STAT3 dependency in serum-10 and serum-2 contexts, testing whether the effect survives different serum culture states. H197 estimates the PTEN effect directly in EMT-low cells, complementing the accepted EMT-high stratum and testing whether the effect is confined to mesenchymal-like cells. H179 estimates it directly in high-stemness cells, giving a direct magnitude check after the near-null stemness interaction. H219 and H221 estimate the PTEN effect in high-hypoxia and high-proliferation contexts, respectively, allowing a more direct test of whether these biological states attenuate or preserve the PTEN-STAT3 supplied-dataset association. These are selected to sharpen context specificity while avoiding excessive reliance on interaction-only estimates.\n\nThe remaining slots test robustness of other accepted axes and cross-context independence. H204 and H205 directly estimate KEAP1-loss versus KEAP1-intact NFE2L2 dependency in high- and low-aneuploidy strata, testing whether the huge KEAP1-NFE2L2 association is robust to chromosomal-instability background. H223 tests the TP53-loss weaker-USP7 association directly within PTEN-loss cells, while H224 tests the CDKN2A-loss stronger-MDM2 association directly within PTEN-loss cells. These cross-context direct effects test whether the TP53-USP7 and CDKN2A-MDM2 axes remain in a PTEN-loss background and are not merely carried by the main accepted effects across the whole population. All results will remain associations in the supplied lung-like dataset, with cautions for multiple testing, subgroup selection, missingness, co-mutation confounding, and residual technical effects.","appraise":"I assessed the twelve newly delivered discovery results using the signed convention: for direction -1 contrasts, a positive estimate supports stronger dependency in the exposed/focal group because more negative CRISPR scores mean stronger dependency; for direction +1 contrasts, a positive estimate supports weaker dependency in the exposed group. I judged acceptance using interval exclusion of zero, practical magnitude, cell sizes, and whether the result was a genuine robustness/context test rather than another slice of an already accepted association. For dependency scores that are negative and often near zero, I used an approximate absolute separation near 0.1 as a conservative practical benchmark alongside the supplied relative rule. H218 (TP53-loss versus intact USP7 in lower-Cas9 screens) accepted: R194 +0.413 (95% CI +0.308 to +0.519). This shows the accepted TP53-loss weaker-USP7 supplied-dataset association is not confined to higher-Cas9 screens, though Cas9_activity_score is incomplete and the result is not causal. H180, H181, H179, H197, H219, and H221 accepted the direct PTEN-loss versus PTEN-intact STAT3 contrast across serum-10, serum-2, stemness-high, EMT-low, high-hypoxia, and high-proliferation contexts respectively: R196 +0.286 (+0.216 to +0.357), R197 +0.275 (+0.151 to +0.398), R199 +0.260 (+0.155 to +0.364), R198 +0.237 (+0.179 to +0.295), R200 +0.236 (+0.133 to +0.339), and R201 +0.288 (+0.212 to +0.363). These are large, precise, and mostly have lower bounds above the practical benchmark; H181 is slightly smaller but still meaningful and excludes zero. They should not be overcounted as independent replications because they are overlapping context-specific slices of the same broad PTEN-loss stronger-STAT3 association, which was already validated overall. H204 and H205 accepted KEAP1-loss versus KEAP1-intact NFE2L2 in high and low aneuploidy halves: R202 +0.794 (+0.766 to +0.822) and R203 +0.797 (+0.768 to +0.826). These provide very strong robustness for the accepted KEAP1-loss weaker-NFE2L2 axis across chromosomal-instability background. H223 accepted TP53-loss versus TP53-intact USP7 within PTEN-loss cells: R204 +0.451 (+0.256 to +0.646), supporting the TP53-USP7 axis in a PTEN-loss background. H224 accepted CDKN2A-loss versus CDKN2A-intact MDM2 within PTEN-loss cells: R205 +0.125 (+0.029 to +0.221). The lower bound is below the absolute 0.1 benchmark and the interval is wide, but the point is above benchmark, zero is excluded, and it adds cross-context robustness to the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 axis; I accept it with magnitude uncertainty. H217 remains unresolved: MTAP-loss versus MTAP-intact USP7 within lower-Cas9 TP53-loss cells is directionally positive R195 +0.144 but imprecise, CI -0.146 to +0.434, with only 33 exposed observations. It cannot establish that MTAP loss strengthens USP7 dependency within TP53-deficient cells, so the MTAP attenuation question remains unresolved and this stratum-specific probe is deferred. I deferred direct complements H198, H220, and H222 because the corresponding high or accepted direct strata are already robust, and further complement testing is low priority relative to the remaining MTAP and aneuploidy-PTEN questions. Voluntary validation is exhausted, so no validation was requested. All accepted findings are associations in the supplied lung-like dataset; overlapping subgroup selection, multiple testing, incomplete Cas9 and growth-rate data, co-mutation confounding, and residual technical effects preclude causal or external generalizability claims.","synthesize":"No new independent-validation response deadlines are present and voluntary validation requests are exhausted, so this synthesis finalizes the supplied-dataset interpretation from the already integrated discovery and validation evidence. I retained the signed convention throughout: for direction -1 contrasts, positive evidence means the exposed/focal group has stronger dependency because more negative CRISPR scores mean stronger dependency; for direction +1 contrasts, positive evidence means the exposed/focal group has weaker dependency. Because dependency scores are negative-centered and often near zero, I used the supplied relative 10% rule together with a conservative absolute dependency-score separation of about 0.1 as a practical benchmark, while emphasizing interval exclusion of zero and convergent validation where available. Major supported associations in this supplied lung-like dataset are: MSI-high cells have strongly greater WRN dependency, H10 discovery +0.790 with validation +0.799 and robustness across Cas9 and aneuploidy-related strata; KEAP1-loss cells have strongly weaker NFE2L2 dependency, H13 discovery +0.796 with validation +0.799 and robustness across lineage, Cas9, library, and aneuploidy strata; SMARCA4-loss cells have strongly greater SMARCA2 dependency, H20 discovery +0.784 with validation +0.790 and robustness across ARID1A status, lineage, libraries, and Cas9 strata, while ARID1A loss alone is null; TP53-loss cells have weaker USP7 dependency, H11 discovery +0.396 with validation +0.448 and robustness across libraries, lineage, Cas9, KEAP1 and MTAP strata; CDKN2A-loss cells have greater MDM2 dependency, H106 discovery +0.117 and TP53 stratum effects validated at approximately +0.12 to +0.13, with consistency across libraries, Cas9, lineage, and PTEN-loss background; and PTEN-loss cells have greater STAT3 dependency, H116 discovery +0.267 with validation +0.283 and broad consistency across TP53 status, driver-negative eligibility, PIK3CA status, CDKN2A and SMARCA4 contexts, library, Cas9, IFN-gamma, EMT, stemness, hypoxia, proliferation, and serum contexts. These axes are large relative to the comparator and far above the 0.1 practical absolute benchmark, and the main axes received independent validation. Context-specific acceptances should not be counted as separate replications because they overlap with the broad validated effects; their value is showing that the effects are not obviously confined to a small subgroup. Negative and specificity findings are also important. Driver-gene hypotheses were not supported: KRAS mutation did not indicate stronger KRAS dependency H1; EGFR amplification did not indicate stronger EGFR dependency H3 with null validation; ERBB2 amplification did not indicate stronger ERBB2 dependency H4; BRAF V600E did not indicate stronger BRAF dependency H5; and many related subgroup, co-mutation, and interaction refinements were null. MYC amplification was null for the tested core outputs POLR2A, DHX9, RPL11, MDM2, and KIF18A. TMED10 was generally null across tested predictors, and many POLR2A comparisons were null. PTEN loss was not a global dependency shift: it was not meaningfully associated with MDM2 H137, USP7 H138, SMARCA2 H159, NFE2L2 H160, or POLR2A H168, supporting specificity for STAT3 among the tested readouts. ARID1A loss alone was not associated with SMARCA2 dependency and did not appear necessary for the SMARCA4-loss axis. The main unresolved scientific issue is MTAP attenuation of the TP53-USP7 axis. TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency appears smaller among MTAP-loss cells than MTAP-intact cells, with the direct TP53 effect in MTAP-loss cells H67 about +0.284 compared with about +0.421 in MTAP-intact cells H68, but the interaction H18 is imprecise and the direct MTAP-loss versus MTAP-intact effect within TP53-loss is directionally positive yet underpowered: H216 +0.119 with interval -0.075 to +0.312, and the lower-Cas9 stratum H217 +0.144 with interval -0.146 to +0.434. This is consistent with MTAP loss partially offsetting TP53-loss-related USP7 hypo-dependency, but it does not establish a scientifically meaningful modifier effect. I closed PTEN-loss versus PTEN-intact STAT3 probes by high versus low aneuploidy, H212 and H213, because the PTEN-STAT3 association was validated overall and is already supported across many independent-context direct estimates; testing additional overlapping strata adds little compared with resolving the MTAP question. The most informative next analysis is a focused direct estimate of MTAP-loss versus MTAP-intact USP7 dependency among TP53-loss cells, H216 and any carefully pre-specified technical strata, with the following interpretation: a positive effect with lower bound above the practical benchmark would support MTAP loss as an offsetting modifier of TP53-loss-associated USP7 hypo-dependency, whereas a null or small precise effect would leave the attenuation pattern as a subgroup-generated hypothesis. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset; causality, pathway mechanism, clinical actionability, and external generalizability remain unestablished because of possible co-mutation confounding, incomplete Cas9 and growth-rate data, library and batch effects, multiple testing, and subgroup selection."}}

record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation requests are exhausted, so this analyze stage selects only previously registered, previously untested claims that should provide new discovery samples. The central scientific priority remains the unresolved MTAP-loss attenuation of the accepted TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency. I therefore run all five new MTAP/CDKN2A probes: H225 and H226 directly estimate MTAP-loss versus MTAP-intact USP7 dependency within TP53-loss cells stratified by higher versus lower screen_roc_auc; H227 directly tests whether the TP53-loss USP7 effect is attenuated among MTAP-loss cells in higher screen_roc_auc contexts; H228 and H229 test whether CDKN2A loss mimics an apparent MTAP-loss effect, which would support 9p21/CDKN2A co-deletion confounding rather than MTAP-specific attenuation. I use the signed convention: for direction -1 USP7 contrasts, positive evidence means stronger USP7 dependency in the exposed/focal group, whereas for direction +1 contrasts positive evidence means weaker dependency. For dependency scores, I require interval exclusion of zero, adequate cell sizes, and practical magnitude using the relative 10% rule together with a conservative absolute dependency-score separation near 0.1. I also run H50, a direct high-Cas9 TP53-loss versus TP53-intact USP7 comparison, because the TP53-USP7 axis is central to the MTAP question and the direct high-Cas9 stratum remains untested. The remaining six claims H206-H211 provide untested direct high/low aneuploidy robustness for the SMARCA4-SMARCA2, TP53-USP7, and CDKN2A-MDM2 axes; they are not counted as independent validations if positive, but can show whether the accepted supplied-dataset associations are broadly robust to chromosomal-instability background. I deliberately avoid cached claims such as H216/H217 that already have displayed evidence and would not yield new sample. All results remain associations in the supplied lung-like dataset; causal mechanism, clinical actionability, and external generalizability remain unestablished.

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
I applied the signed convention: for direction -1 contrasts, a positive estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed/focal group because more negative CRISPR scores indicate stronger dependency; for direction +1 contrasts, a positive estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. I judged acceptance using 95% Welch interval exclusion of zero, cell-size validity, and practical magnitude using the supplied relative criterion together with a conservative approximate absolute dependency-score separation of about 0.1.

H50 and H206-H211 provide robust context-specific evidence for previously accepted supplied-dataset axes, but should not be counted as independent replications because they are overlapping subgroup slices of the same broad associations. H50 accepts TP53-loss associated weaker USP7 dependency in higher-Cas9 screens: R211 +0.385, CI +0.276 to +0.495, n=178 vs 679. H206 and H207 accept SMARCA4-loss associated stronger SMARCA2 dependency in high and low aneuploidy halves: R212 +0.775, CI +0.747 to +0.803, n=206 vs 800; R213 +0.791, CI +0.764 to +0.817, n=209 vs 792. H208 and H209 accept TP53-loss associated weaker USP7 dependency in high and low aneuploidy halves: R214 +0.359, CI +0.259 to +0.460, n=214 vs 792; R215 +0.437, CI +0.338 to +0.537, n=193 vs 808. H210 and H211 accept CDKN2A-loss associated stronger MDM2 dependency across high and low aneuploidy strata: R216 +0.102, CI +0.051 to +0.153, n=201 vs 805; R217 +0.136, CI +0.088 to +0.183, n=203 vs 798. H210 has a lower bound below the absolute 0.1 benchmark and H211 similarly has a slightly low lower bound, but both point estimates are at or above the practical benchmark, intervals exclude zero, and the axes have prior robustness and validation; therefore they are accepted with magnitude uncertainty rather than as separately validated effects.

The MTAP-loss attenuation question remains unresolved and should not be over-interpreted. H225 directly tests MTAP-loss versus MTAP-intact USP7 dependency among TP53-loss cells in higher screen_roc_auc strata: R206 +0.170, CI -0.111 to +0.450, n=37 vs 182. The point estimate exceeds the practical benchmark and has the hypothesized direction, but the interval includes zero and a null effect, and the exposed cell is only 37. record.narrative: No new validation results or response deadlines are present, and independent validation requests are exhausted, so this synthesis finalizes the supplied-dataset interpretation from all integrated discovery and validation evidence. I retained the signed convention: for direction -1 contrasts, positive evidence means stronger dependency in the exposed/focal group because more negative CRISPR dependency scores indicate stronger dependency; for direction +1 contrasts, positive evidence means weaker dependency in the exposed group. Because dependency scores are negative-centered, I used interval exclusion of zero together with the relative 10% rule and a conservative approximate absolute dependency-score separation of about 0.1 as practical significance criteria. The strongest supported supplied-dataset associations are: MSI-high cells have markedly stronger WRN dependency (H10 discovery +0.790, validation +0.799); KEAP1-loss cells have markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H13 discovery +0.796, validation +0.799); SMARCA4-loss cells have markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H20 discovery +0.784, validation +0.790), with ARID1A loss alone not sufficient to produce the same axis; TP53-loss cells have weaker USP7 dependency (H11 discovery +0.396, validation +0.448); CDKN2A-loss cells have stronger MDM2 dependency (H106 discovery +0.117, with TP53-intact and TP53-loss strata validated at approximately +0.12 to +0.13); and PTEN-loss cells have stronger STAT3 dependency (H116 discovery +0.267, validation +0.283). These effects are large relative to the comparator scale and are supported across multiple technical and genomic contexts, but context-specific acceptances are not independent replications because they overlap with the same broad associations. Negative and specificity findings are also important. Driver-gene matching hypotheses were not supported: KRAS mutation did not indicate stronger KRAS dependency, EGFR amplification did not indicate stronger EGFR dependency and its validation was null, ERBB2 amplification did not indicate stronger ERBB2 dependency, and BRAF V600E did not indicate stronger BRAF dependency. MYC amplification was null across the tested core outputs. TMED10 was broadly null across tested predictors, and many POLR2A comparisons were null. PTEN loss was not a global dependency shift: it was not meaningfully associated with MDM2, USP7, SMARCA2, NFE2L2, POLR2A, or TMED10, supporting specificity for STAT3 among the tested readouts. The main unresolved issue is whether MTAP loss attenuates the TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency. TP53-loss-associated USP7 hypo-dependency appears numerically smaller among MTAP-loss cells than MTAP-intact cells, but the interaction evidence is weak or imprecise, and the direct MTAP-loss effect among TP53-loss cells remains below a convincing accepted threshold because intervals include zero and null effects: H216 +0.119, CI -0.075 to +0.312; high-Cas9 and screen-quality strata are also positive but crossing zero. CDKN2A-loss mimicry probes did not show a visible USP7 effect, reducing support for a simple 9p21 co-deletion artifact but not formally excluding genomic confounding. I therefore record investigation-only closure of H216, H225, H226, and H227 while leaving their assessments unresolved, because additional overlapping technical MTAP strata are unlikely to convert an imprecise subgroup signal into a supported modifier claim. No causal, mechanistic, clinical, or external generalization claim is warranted, and independent validation requests are exhausted.","synthesize":"No new validation results or response deadlines are present, and independent validation requests are exhausted, so this synthesis finalizes the supplied-dataset interpretation from all integrated discovery and validation evidence. I retained the signed convention: for direction -1 contrasts, positive evidence means stronger dependency in the exposed/focal group because more negative CRISPR dependency scores indicate stronger dependency; for direction +1 contrasts, positive evidence means weaker dependency in the exposed group. Because dependency scores are negative-centered, I used interval exclusion of zero together with the relative 10% rule and a conservative approximate absolute dependency-score separation of about 0.1 as practical significance criteria. The strongest supported supplied-dataset associations are: MSI-high cells have markedly stronger WRN dependency (H10 discovery +0.790, validation +0.799); KEAP1-loss cells have markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H13 discovery +0.796, validation +0.799); SMARCA4-loss cells have markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H20 discovery +0.784, validation +0.790), with ARID1A loss alone not sufficient to produce the same axis; TP53-loss cells have weaker USP7 dependency (H11 discovery +0.396, validation +0.448); CDKN2A-loss cells have stronger MDM2 dependency (H106 discovery +0.117, with TP53-intact and TP53-loss strata validated at approximately +0.12 to +0.13); and PTEN-loss cells have stronger STAT3 dependency (H116 discovery +0.267, validation +0.283). These effects are large relative to the comparator scale and are supported across multiple technical and genomic contexts, but context-specific acceptances are not independent replications because they overlap with the same broad associations. Negative and specificity findings are also important. Driver-gene matching hypotheses were not supported: KRAS mutation did not indicate stronger KRAS dependency, EGFR amplification did not indicate stronger EGFR dependency and its validation was null, ERBB2 amplification did not indicate stronger ERBB2 dependency, and BRAF V600E did not indicate stronger BRAF dependency. MYC amplification was null across the tested core outputs. TMED10 was broadly null across tested predictors, and many POLR2A comparisons were null. PTEN loss was not a global dependency shift: it was not meaningfully associated with MDM2, USP7, SMARCA2, NFE2L2, POLR2A, or TMED10, supporting specificity for STAT3 among the tested readouts. The main unresolved issue is whether MTAP loss attenuates the TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency. TP53-loss-associated USP7 hypo-dependency appears numerically smaller among MTAP-loss cells than MTAP-intact cells, but the interaction evidence is weak or imprecise, and the direct MTAP-loss effect among TP53-loss cells remains below a convincing accepted threshold because intervals include zero and null effects: H216 +0.119, CI -0.075 to +0.312; high-Cas9 and screen-quality strata are also positive but crossing zero. record.narrative: No validation request is possible because new validation requests are exhausted, and I did not identify evidence that would be improved by a cached request. I assessed the new discovery results using the signed convention and the stated practical criteria: valid cell sizes, a 95% Welch interval excluding zero, and a meaningful dependency-score separation of roughly 0.1 or larger, interpreted together with the relative criterion. For direction -1 contrasts, positive evidence means stronger dependency in the exposed/focal group; for direction +1 contrasts, positive evidence means weaker dependency in the exposed group. H230-H232 are arbitrary marker controls for USP7 dependency among TP53-loss cells. R218 (marker D, +0.079, CI -0.062 to +0.220), R219 (marker E, +0.042, CI -0.099 to +0.183), and R220 (marker F, +0.023, CI -0.118 to +0.164) are all nonsignificant and have point estimates below the practical benchmark, but the intervals extend to moderately positive values. Because these constructed markers have no assigned biology, I do not support the tested directional claims; I mark them unresolved and closed rather than asserting a precise null, since the intervals cannot exclude a small-to-moderate effect. H234 and H235 accept the previously supported PTEN-loss associated stronger STAT3 dependency in arbitrary marker-D-positive and marker-D-negative strata: R222 (+0.259, CI +0.188 to +0.330) and R223 (+0.276, CI +0.199 to +0.354). H237 accepts CDKN2A-loss associated stronger MDM2 dependency in marker-E-positive cells: R225 (+0.117, CI +0.064 to +0.169). H238 accepts SMARCA4-loss associated stronger SMARCA2 dependency in research-signature-C-high cells: R226 (+0.787, CI +0.761 to +0.813). H239 accepts KEAP1-loss associated weaker NFE2L2 dependency in marker-F-positive cells: R227 (+0.800, CI +0.772 to +0.828). These are context-specific robustness acceptances, not independent replications, because they are subgroup slices of the same supplied dataset. H61 and H62 also accept majority-Avana library robustness for two accepted axes: MSI-high associated stronger WRN dependency, R228 (+0.794, CI +0.764 to +0.825), and KEAP1-loss associated weaker NFE2L2 dependency, R229 (+0.796, CI +0.774 to +0.818). The main new complication is arbitrary-assay specificity. H233 tests whether research-signature-A-high cells modify the TP53-loss USP7 axis under direction +1. R221 is large, valid, and opposite to the tested positive modification: -0.802, CI -0.919 to -0.685. I reject the tested positive-interaction claim, but the result is scientifically important as a specificity concern: an assay explicitly constructed to have no assigned biological role appears to modify an accepted axis by a large amount. This should not be interpreted as biology; it suggests hidden correlation, constructed-assay leakage, chance under multiple comparisons, or another nonbiological explanation. H236 similarly shows a significant but smaller opposite modification of the PTEN-loss STAT3 axis by arbitrary marker-E positivity: R224 (-0.124, CI -0.227 to -0.021). I reject the tested positive-interaction claim and leave the investigation active as a specificity/hidden-correlation concern. To clarify these findings, I registered direct stratum comparisons within research-signature-A-high and low strata for TP53-loss USP7 dependency, and within marker-E-positive and marker-E-negative strata for PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency. These direct tests will show whether the main effects persist, attenuate, reverse, or become unstable in the strata implicated by the interactions. Overall, the major accepted supplied-dataset axes remain robust across many arbitrary and technical strata, but the unexpected arbitrary-signature-A and marker-E interactions prevent an overconfident claim that every accepted association is fully independent of constructed assay structure. These remain supplied-dataset associations only; no causal, mechanistic, clinical, or external generalization is warranted.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Iteration 19/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative:
I assessed all newly delivered discovery results using the signed convention and practical acceptance criteria: valid cell sizes, a 95% Welch interval excluding zero, and a scientifically meaningful dependency-score separation, interpreted in light of the stated 10% clinical-significance threshold. Because dependency scores are negative-valued and arbitrary in units, I treated absolute magnitudes around 0.1 or larger, especially when supported by large standard deviations, as potentially meaningful. I did not request validation because no new independent-validation requests remain.

H240 and H241 directly clarify the research-signature-A specificity concern. In the signature-A-high stratum, the TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency claim is not supported: R230 is +0.003 with CI -0.110 to +0.116, cells 207/765. The point estimate is essentially null and the interval excludes large or moderate effects above roughly 0.12, though it cannot exclude a small positive effect; I leave H240 unresolved but active because the new follow-up proposals examine whether MTAP-loss status explains this stratum-specific attenuation. In the signature-A-low stratum, R231 is +0.805 with CI +0.777 to +0.833, cells 199/829; H241 is accepted as a context-specific supplied-dataset association. This strongly suggests that the TP53-loss-USP7 axis is not uniform across the constructed signature-A strata, but the biological interpretation of research signature A is undefined and should not be interpreted as biology.

H242 and H243 directly test the PTEN-loss-associated stronger STAT3 dependency in marker-E-positive and marker-E-negative strata. Both are supported: R232 is +0.328 with CI +0.255 to +0.401, and R233 is +0.204 with CI +0.130 to +0.278. The association persists in both marker-E strata, with a somewhat larger effect in marker-E-positive cells. These are robustness acceptances within the supplied dataset, not independent replications, and the constructed marker itself has no assigned biology.

H244 and H245 remain central unresolved questions for MTAP-loss attenuation of the TP53-loss-USP7 axis under higher-quality screen conditions. R234 is +0.238 with CI -0.045 to +0.521, cells 36/149/164/552; R235 is +0.220 with CI -0.061 to +0.502, cells 36/164. Both point in the attenuation direction under the signed convention but have intervals including zero and modest cell sizes in the MTAP-loss cells. I therefore keep them unresolved and active. The broadened MTAP-loss and research-signature-A-by-MTAP follow-up proposals are the most informative next tests before over-interpreting this attenuation.

H246-H249 test screen-quality robustness. PTEN-loss associated stronger STAT3 dependency is supported in both high-quality and lower-quality screen ROC-AUC strata: R236 +0.253 CI +0.181 to +0.325, and R237 +0.280 CI +0.205 to +0.355. TP53-loss associated weaker USP7 dependency is also supported in both screen-quality strata: R238 +0.426 CI +0.332 to +0.519, and R239 +0.360 CI +0.251 to +0.469. These acceptances reduce concern that screen ROC quality is a confounder for these two major axes.

H250 and H251 test whether two very large accepted axes persist in arbitrary marker-E-positive cells. R240 is +0.790 CI +0.762 to +0.817 for SMARCA4-loss associated stronger SMARCA2 dependency, and R241 is +0.796 CI +0.767 to +0.825 for KEAP1-loss associated weaker NFE2L2 dependency. Both are accepted. This supports robustness of the major axes, while the earlier marker-E interaction remains a constructed-assay specificity concern rather than a biological claim.

Overall, the new evidence strengthens the robustness of PTEN-loss STAT3, TP53-loss USP7, SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2, and KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 associations across screen-quality and marker-E strata. It also sharpens two unresolved audit issues: whether research signature A reveals hidden constructed-assay structure or a real but biologically undefined modifier, and whether MTAP-loss attenuation of TP53-loss USP7 is real but underpowered. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset only; none support causal, mechanistic, clinical, or external generalizability claims.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

R240 is +0.790 CI +0.762 to +0.817 for SMARCA4-loss associated stronger SMARCA2 dependency, and R241 is +0.796 CI +0.767 to +0.825 for KEAP1-loss associated weaker NFE2L2 dependency. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset only; none support causal, mechanistic, clinical, or external generalizability claims.","synthesize":"No new validation results or response deadlines are listed, and independent validation requests are exhausted, so no claim was newly validated this cycle. These are treated as specificity or hidden-assay concerns, not biology, because the assays have no assigned biological role. H240-H243 remain active as direct stratum tests for those concerns. Supported supplied-dataset associations are strongest and most reproducible for six axes. MSI-high cells show markedly stronger WRN dependency, with discovery/validated separations about +0.79 to +0.80 and robustness across aneuploidy, Cas9-quality, Avana-library, and other strata. KEAP1-loss cells show markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency, about +0.80 after signing to the accepted direction and validated in an independent set. SMARCA4-loss cells show markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency, about +0.78 to +0.79 and validated, whereas ARID1A loss alone does not produce the same axis. TP53-loss cells show weaker USP7 dependency, about +0.40 to +0.45 after signing and validated. CDKN2A-loss cells show stronger MDM2 dependency, about +0.12 overall and replicated or robust across TP53-intact, TP53-loss, non-Avana, adenocarcinoma, and arbitrary marker-E strata. PTEN-loss cells show stronger STAT3 dependency, about +0.27 to +0.28 and validated, and this specificity is reinforced by the absence of comparable PTEN effects on MDM2, USP7, SMARCA2, NFE2L2, POLR2A, or TMED10. Negative findings remain important. Driver matched hypotheses were not supported: KRAS mutation did not associate with stronger KRAS dependency, EGFR amplification did not associate with stronger EGFR dependency and its validation was null, ERBB2 amplification did not associate with stronger ERBB2 dependency, and BRAF V600E did not associate with stronger BRAF dependency. MYC amplification was broadly null across tested outcomes, TMED10 was null across tested predictors, and MTAP loss was not a simple main-effect driver for USP7 or MDM2. Unresolved uncertainty is concentrated in MTAP-loss attenuation of the TP53-loss USP7 association: direct and interaction estimates are often in the attenuation direction but imprecise, intervals include zero, and validation did not settle the question. The arbitrary marker/signature interactions are also unresolved but should not be interpreted as biology; they may reflect hidden correlation, leakage, chance, or constructed-assay structure. The most informative next analysis is an external, adequately powered, pre-specified test of USP7 dependency among TP53-loss cells comparing MTAP-loss with MTAP-intact samples and the TP53-loss by MTAP-loss interaction. If only the supplied dataset can be used, the next useful analyses are the pending direct strata H240-H243 to determine whether TP53-USP7 and PTEN-STAT3 main effects persist, attenuate, or become unstable in the implicated arbitrary strata, plus additional untested accepted-axis robustness strata. All conclusions are associations in this supplied lung-like dataset only, not causal, mechanistic, clinical, or generalizable claims."}}

record.narrative: No assessments were due and no new independent validation results arrived; validation request capacity is exhausted, so no claim was newly validated or rejected at this synthesis step. I reassessed three previously valid direct context tests of the accepted CDKN2A-loss/MDM2-dependency axis (H78, H79, H82) because their estimates were clinically meaningful and their 95% intervals excluded zero; they are now accepted as context-specific supplied-dataset associations. The major supported axes remain stable. MSI-high cells show markedly stronger WRN dependency, about +0.79 to +0.80 signed to the accepted stronger-dependency direction, with independent validation and robustness across Cas9 activity, Avana-library status, and aneuploidy strata. KEAP1-loss cells show markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency, about +0.80, with independent validation and robustness across Cas9, library, aneuploidy, and arbitrary-marker strata. SMARCA4-loss cells show markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency, about +0.78 to +0.79, with independent validation; ARID1A loss alone does not produce this effect. TP53-loss cells show weaker USP7 dependency, about +0.40 to +0.45, validated and robust across screen quality, Cas9 activity, library, lineage, and MTAP-intact strata. CDKN2A-loss cells show stronger MDM2 dependency, about +0.12 overall, with replication in TP53-intact, TP53-loss, non-Avana, and direct MTAP-stratum tests. Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

First, MTAP and CDKN2A are adjacent genomic lesions, so the apparent attenuation of the accepted TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency in MTAP-loss cells may be due specifically to MTAP loss, to broader CDKN2A/9p21 co-deletion structure, or to chance under limited subgroup sizes. I therefore register direct TP53-loss effects restricted to MTAP-loss/CDKN2A-intact and to MTAP-loss/CDKN2A-loss contexts, plus interaction contrasts that isolate MTAP-loss without CDKN2A loss or CDKN2A loss alone. For interaction direction -1, a negative raw interaction corresponds to a positive signed estimate and would indicate attenuation of the TP53-loss weaker-USP7 association in the focal subgroup. Under an MTAP-specific attenuation hypothesis, the MTAP-loss/CDKN2A-intact interaction should show attenuation while the CDKN2A-loss interaction may not; under a 9p21 co-deletion hypothesis, CDKN2A-loss-associated attenuation may appear more generally. A null pattern would leave attenuation unsupported. Second, research signature A showed striking stratum heterogeneity for TP53-loss USP7 dependency, and marker E produced an unexpected PTEN-loss STAT3 interaction despite robust direct marker-E strata. I therefore test whether accepted axes for CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency and MSI-high WRN dependency persist across signature-A high/low strata, and whether the TP53-loss USP7 association persists across marker-E strata. Persistence supports broad robustness of the accepted axes and confines signature/marker anomalies to assay-specificity or chance concerns; attenuation would suggest hidden constructed-assay structure or context fragility. I also register cross-context tests of accepted PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency within SMARCA4-loss cells and accepted KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 dependency within PTEN-loss cells to broaden robustness of major axes. These analyses remain discovery comparisons in the supplied dataset only and do not establish causality, mechanism, clinical relevance, or external generalizability.","analyze":"No assessments are due and independent validation requests are exhausted, so this analyze stage allocates the available discovery sample to the 12 active, previously registered, not-yet-tested claims. H242 and H243 test the accepted PTEN-loss-associated stronger STAT3 dependency within marker-E-positive and marker-E-negative direct strata, complementing the earlier rejected positive-interaction probe H236 and clarifying whether marker-E modification reflects a fragile subgroup, hidden constructed-assay correlation, or chance. Across all accepted-axis direct strata, I will require valid cell counts, a 95% Welch interval excluding zero, and a practically meaningful signed separation, roughly on the order of 0.1 absolute dependency-score units or larger together with the stated relative interpretation. For accepted axes with very large effects, persistence should produce estimates close to the overall effect; substantial attenuation or intervals including zero would indicate context fragility or insufficient power. Null arbitrary-marker or arbitrary-signature results are useful but will be interpreted cautiously because constructed assays have no assigned biology and may be underpowered. All requested analyses are subset or refinement analyses of the supplied dataset only, not independent validation, and do not support causal, mechanistic, clinical, or external generalizability claims.","appraise":"I assessed all newly delivered discovery results using the signed convention and practical acceptance criteria: valid cell sizes, a 95% Welch interval excluding zero, and a scientifically meaningful dependency-score separation, interpreted in light of the stated 10% clinical-significance threshold. In the signature-A-high stratum, the TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency claim is not supported: R230 is +0.003 with CI -0.110 to +0.116, cells 207/765. This strongly suggests that the TP53-loss-USP7 axis is not uniform across the constructed signature-A strata, but the biological interpretation of research signature A is undefined and should not be interpreted as biology.\n\nH242 and H243 directly test the PTEN-loss-associated stronger STAT3 dependency in marker-E-positive and marker-E-negative strata. The association persists in both marker-E strata, with a somewhat larger effect in marker-E-positive cells. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset only; none support causal, mechanistic, clinical, or external generalizability claims.","synthesize":"No assessments were due and no new independent validation results arrived; validation request capacity is exhausted, so no claim was newly validated or rejected at this synthesis step. record.narrative:
I assessed all newly delivered discovery results using the signed convention: each estimate and interval is already oriented to the registered hypothesis direction. Acceptance required valid cells, an interval excluding zero, and a dependency-score separation large enough to be scientifically meaningful on this scale. Because these are numerous subgroup and interaction probes in a supplied dataset, I treated positive subgroup results as context-specific associations only, not causal or external claims.

The research-signature-A/USP7 anomaly was further clarified. In signature-A-high cells, TP53 loss was not supported as being associated with weaker USP7 dependency. H253 (signature-A-high, MTAP-intact) gave a small positive signed effect +0.054 with CI -0.068 to +0.177; the interval includes zero and cannot exclude a small-to-modest positive effect, so it is unresolved but closed because further probing of this exact null stratum is not informative. H254 (signature-A-high, MTAP-loss) gave a negative signed effect -0.265 with upper bound only +0.030; this argues strongly against the registered positive effect and is rejected. H260 (signature-A-high, Cas9-high) gave -0.049 with CI -0.231 to +0.132, so it is unresolved but closed; it provides no support. By contrast, H255 (signature-A-low, MTAP-loss) gave +0.736 with CI +0.671 to +0.801 and is accepted as a context-specific association. Importantly, H267 and H269 show that the accepted CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 and MSI-high/WRN axes remain strong in signature-A-high cells: +0.137 with CI +0.085 to +0.189, and +0.807 with CI +0.756 to +0.858, respectively. This reduces concern that research signature A is a global hidden confounder and confines the signature-A anomaly mainly to the TP53-loss/USP7 axis or to constructed-assay heterogeneity.

MTAP-specific attenuation of the TP53-loss/USP7 association remains unresolved. H261 directly shows that TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency in MTAP-loss/CDKN2A-intact cells: +0.284 with CI +0.086 to +0.482, accepted. This does not itself prove attenuation; it only shows the effect remains present. The corresponding interaction H262 points toward attenuation under the signed direction (+0.132), but CI -0.080 to +0.343 includes zero and the MTAP-loss/CDKN2A-intact cell sizes are modest. H264 tests CDKN2A-loss alone and is essentially null: +0.004 with CI -0.170 to +0.177; unresolved/closed. H263 is invalid due to insufficient cell counts. Thus attenuation is plausible but not supported as a separate accepted claim.

Cas9-activity-low strata were also informative. TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency in Cas9-low/MTAP-intact cells, H257: +0.440 with CI +0.325 to +0.556, accepted. It is also associated with weaker USP7 in Cas9-low/MTAP-loss cells, H256: +0.295 with CI +0.025 to +0.564, accepted, though the point estimate is smaller and exposed cells are only 33. This pattern is compatible with attenuation but is not a direct interaction test. Overall, the TP53-loss/USP7 association remains robust across several strata, while MTAP-specific attenuation remains the central unresolved issue and H262 is kept active. No validation is requested because no new independent-validation requests remain. All accepted conclusions remain supplied-dataset associations and do not establish causality, mechanism, clinical relevance, or external generalizability.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.
