record.narrative: No assessments were due, no new independent validation estimates were delivered, and independent validation request capacity is exhausted. I therefore make no new claim assessments in this synthesis stage; active, unresolved probes retain their current statuses. The scientific synthesis is based on the complete supplied-dataset ledger. Because dependency scores are continuous standardized scores rather than ratio outcomes, I evaluated effects primarily by absolute separation on the observed dependency-score scale together with interval precision and replication; robust axes are large on this scale, while near-zero effects are treated as negative despite some intervals not excluding very small residuals. The strongest supported, validated associations in this supplied lung-adenocarcinoma CRISPR dataset are: MSI-high cells have markedly stronger WRN dependency (H10; R10 discovery and R39 validation), with persistence across Cas9-activity, Avana and non-Avana libraries, aneuploidy strata, lineage-subtype strata and research-signature strata; KEAP1-loss cells have markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H6 and H13; R6 and R38), robust across screen-quality, Cas9-activity, library, aneuploidy, arbitrary-marker and interaction probes; SMARCA4-loss cells have markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H20; R19 and R65), with direct strata accepted in ARID1A-intact and ARID1A-loss cells (H45 and H46), while ARID1A loss alone was not supported as producing the SMARCA2 effect (H7 and H111 rejected); TP53-loss cells have weaker USP7 dependency (H11; R11 and R52), robust overall and across Cas9-activity, screen-quality, library, lineage and MTAP-intact contexts; CDKN2A-loss cells have stronger MDM2 dependency (H106; H77, H95 and H108 with validation R78, R92 and R105), replicated in TP53-intact, TP53-loss, non-Avana and direct strata; and PTEN-loss cells have stronger STAT3 dependency (H116; R113 and R119), robust across TP53 status, driver-negative cells, serum condition, growth rate, hypoxia, screen quality and arbitrary-marker strata, with PTEN effects on other dependencies largely null. Important negative findings are equally central. Canonical driver-allele-to-dependency mappings were not supported in this dataset: KRAS mutation was not associated with stronger KRAS or RIT1 dependency (H1 and H2); EGFR amplification was not associated with stronger EGFR dependency and independent validation was null (H3; R3 and R13); ERBB2 amplification was not associated with ERBB2, RIT1 or TMED10 dependency (H4, H104 and H33); and BRAF V600E was not associated with BRAF dependency (H5). MYC amplification was broadly null across tested dependencies, TMED10 was null across tested predictors, MTAP loss was not a simple main-effect driver of USP7 or MDM2 dependency, and media serum percentage was not associated with STAT3 dependency. The principal unresolved issue is whether MTAP loss attenuates the TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency. Direct subgroup effects are smaller in MTAP-loss than MTAP-intact cells, and several interaction or quality-restricted probes point in the attenuation direction, but intervals commonly include zero, exposed cells are modest in important strata, and validation of the MTAP-loss TP53-loss contrast was imprecise. Accordingly, MTAP attenuation remains plausible but not accepted. Research signature A showed a striking anomaly for TP53-loss USP7 dependency, but CDKN2A-loss MDM2 and MSI-high WRN effects remained strong in signature-A-high strata (H267 and H269), making the anomaly more consistent with constructed-assay heterogeneity than a global technical confounder. Arbitrary research markers and signatures should not be interpreted as biological mechanisms. The most informative next analysis is an adequately powered, pre-specified external test of the TP53-loss by MTAP-loss interaction on USP7 dependency, with enough co-altered cells to estimate an interaction of roughly 0.20; secondary useful work is external replication of the stable PTEN-loss STAT3 and TP53-loss USP7 axes. Additional post hoc searches over constructed signatures or markers are unlikely to improve inference unless pre-specified and adequately powered. All conclusions remain associations within the supplied dataset and do not establish causality, biological mechanism, clinical relevance, or external generalizability.

record.narrative: No claim assessments are due, and independent validation capacity is exhausted. I therefore allocate the remaining discovery-comparison slots to 12 active, previously registered, untested probes that most directly address the central unresolved question: whether MTAP loss specifically attenuates the accepted TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency, or whether apparent attenuation is confounded by adjacent CDKN2A/9p21 lesion structure, library/screen quality, or limited subgroup precision. I prioritize the CDKN2A-intact TP53-loss by MTAP-loss interaction (H273), the direct MTAP-loss contrast among TP53-loss CDKN2A-intact Avana screens (H274), and the clean TP53-loss contrast among MTAP-intact CDKN2A-intact cells (H277). I also test copy-number 9p21-low specificity with both a direct TP53-loss contrast in 9p21-low cells (H275) and an interaction contrast for attenuation in 9p21-low versus its complement (H276). H282 is a specificity probe asking whether PTEN loss also affects WRN dependency within Avana screens. H270 tests whether the MSI-high WRN axis remains strong in research-signature-A-low cells, completing the stratum check that already found the axis strong in signature-A-high cells. For accepted context effects, I require valid cells in every comparison cell, a 95% Welch interval excluding zero in the signed direction, and a dependency-score separation of practical interest. Interaction estimates with intervals including zero, or point effects only near zero, will remain unresolved or negative. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset and do not establish causality, biological mechanism, clinical relevance, or external generalizability.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
I assessed every newly delivered discovery result using the signed convention: each estimate and interval is already oriented to the registered hypothesis direction. Acceptance required valid comparison cells, a 95% Welch interval excluding zero in the claimed direction, and a dependency-score separation large enough to be scientifically meaningful on this continuous CRISPR dependency scale. 

The clean TP53-loss/USP7 baseline remains robust. H277, testing TP53 loss among MTAP-intact/CDKN2A-intact cells, gave +0.423 (CI +0.335 to +0.511) for weaker USP7 dependency with TP53 loss. This is a large separation and supports the accepted TP53-loss/USP7 axis in a more genetically restricted context. H275 similarly showed a substantial TP53-loss effect within 9p21-low copy-number cells, +0.385 (CI +0.244 to +0.526), so TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency is not eliminated in that structural subgroup. However, H276 specifically tested whether the TP53-loss effect is attenuated in 9p21-low versus the remainder; the signed attenuation estimate was only +0.014 (CI -0.149 to +0.177). This rejects a practical 9p21-low structural explanation for the MTAP attenuation hypothesis.

MTAP-specific attenuation of TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency remains unresolved. H273, the CDKN2A-intact TP53-loss by MTAP-loss interaction, gave +0.139 (CI -0.078 to +0.355), compatible with attenuation under the signed direction but not statistically or practically established. H274, the direct MTAP-loss contrast among TP53-loss/CDKN2A-intact/Avana cells, gave +0.220 (CI -0.061 to +0.502); this is suggestive of MTAP-loss stronger USP7 dependency or attenuation, but the interval includes zero. H258, a broader Avana-restricted MTAP-loss contrast within TP53-loss cells, gave +0.167 (CI -0.036 to +0.370), again imprecise. I keep the more targeted H273 and H274 active, defer the less specific H258, and do not accept MTAP attenuation as a separate supported claim.

MTAP loss does not appear to be a broad modifier of accepted axes. PTEN-loss-associated stronger STAT3 dependency remained large and similar in both MTAP strata: H278 in MTAP-loss +0.249 (CI +0.116 to +0.382) and H279 in MTAP-intact +0.271 (CI +0.214 to +0.328). CDKN2A-loss-associated stronger MDM2 dependency also remained significant in MTAP strata: H280 in MTAP-intact +0.105 (CI +0.067 to +0.143) and H281 in MTAP-loss +0.165 (CI +0.081 to +0.249). These support the PTEN/STAT3 and CDKN2A/MDM2 axes as robust to MTAP status and argue against MTAP loss being a general quality or modifier variable.

Two specificity probes were negative. H282 tested PTEN loss on WRN dependency within Avana screens and found essentially no effect, -0.008 (CI -0.044 to +0.029), supporting specificity of PTEN-loss-associated stronger STAT3 rather than a global dependency change. H270 tested MSI-high-associated stronger WRN dependency in research-signature-A-low cells and found a very large effect, +0.780 (CI +0.744 to +0.817), confirming that the MSI-high/WRN axis persists in the signature-A-low stratum. 

Independent validation request capacity is exhausted, so no validation is requested. All accepted findings are associations within the supplied dataset only and do not establish causality, biological mechanism, clinical relevance, or external generalizability.

results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this exploration focuses on two remaining scientific questions. First, I register a targeted probe of whether MTAP loss attenuates the accepted TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency, while restricting to TP53-loss, CDKN2A-intact, high-Cas9-activity cells. Under MTAP-specific attenuation, MTAP loss should be associated with relatively stronger USP7 dependency (raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast negative) compared with MTAP-intact TP53-loss cells; with direction -1 this would be reported as a positive signed estimate. A near-zero or interval-crossing result will keep the attenuation hypothesis unresolved rather than accepted. Second, I test robustness of the main accepted dependency axes among cells with matched RNA and DNA omics, and in low-versus-high mutation-burden strata for USP7 and MDM2 where annotation burden could plausibly confound associations. I also test the MSI-high/WRN axis within MTAP-loss and MTAP-intact cells to determine whether MTAP loss acts as a broad modifier or 9p21 co-deletion surrogate rather than a specific modifier of TP53-loss/USP7. These comparisons are discovery associations in the supplied dataset only and do not establish causality, mechanism, clinical relevance, or external generalizability.

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains

Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: No new independent validation estimates were delivered in this synthesis window and no assessments_due were listed; the validation request budget is exhausted. The final assessment therefore relies on the supplied discovery ledger plus prior validation estimates. All statements are associations in this supplied 2000-cell, lung adenocarcinoma-dominant CRISPR dependency dataset; they do not establish causality, mechanism, clinical relevance, or external generalizability. Because dependency scores are continuous and more negative means stronger dependency, I judged meaningfulness by absolute separation on the observed dependency-score scale, interval precision, replication across strata, and prior independent validation rather than by a direct 10% relative rule. Signed estimates are already oriented to the registered hypothesis: a positive signed estimate with direction -1 means raw exposed-minus-comparator is negative, i.e. stronger dependency; a positive signed estimate with direction +1 means raw exposed-minus-comparator is positive, which for dependency means weaker dependency. Supported robust findings. 1. MSI-high cells have markedly stronger WRN dependency. This is the strongest validated axis: signed +0.790 in discovery R10 and +0.799 in validation R39. It remains large across Cas9-activity strata, Avana and non-Avana libraries, aneuploidy strata, lineage contexts, mutation-burden-adjacent contexts, matched RNA+DNA restriction, research-signature strata, and MTAP strata. The effect is far larger than the typical WRN standard deviation, so it is scientifically meaningful even though external generalizability is unproven. 2. KEAP1-loss cells have markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The accepted reverse-direction claim H13 is supported by signed +0.796 discovery R6 and +0.799 validation R38. The original stronger-NFE2L2 hypothesis is rejected. This association is large and robust across library, Cas9, aneuploidy, lineage, matched-omics, and arbitrary-marker contexts. 3. SMARCA4-loss cells have markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency. Signed +0.784 discovery R19 and +0.790 validation R65 support H20. This holds in ARID1A-loss and ARID1A-intact cells, whereas ARID1A loss alone is not accepted as producing the SMARCA2 effect. 4. TP53-loss cells have weaker USP7 dependency. Signed +0.396 discovery R11 and +0.448 validation R52 support H11. This axis is robust across screen-quality, Cas9, library, aneuploidy, lineage, mutation-burden, matched-omics, MTAP-intact, CDKN2A-intact, and combined clean contexts; the clean TP53-loss effect in MTAP-intact and CDKN2A-intact cells is still large, signed +0.423 in R256. 5. CDKN2A-loss cells have stronger MDM2 dependency. The main accepted effect is signed +0.117 discovery R93. Smaller but repeatedly supported: TP53-intact signed +0.119 discovery R59 with validation +0.129 R78; TP53-loss signed +0.111 discovery R81 with validation +0.132 R92; non-Avana signed +0.125 discovery R95 with validation +0.172 R105. A 9p21-low interaction attenuation claim was not supported, so the MDM2 effect is not reduced to a simple copy-number co-deletion artifact. 6. PTEN-loss cells have stronger STAT3 dependency. Signed +0.267 discovery R113 and +0.283 validation R119 support H116. This is unusually robust across TP53 status, driver-negative cells, serum conditions, growth-rate and hypoxia strata, screen quality, arbitrary marker strata, and MTAP strata. PTEN effects on several other dependencies, including WRN H282, are null, strengthening specificity within this dataset. Important negative findings. Canonical driver-allele-to-self-dependency mappings were not supported: KRAS mutation was not associated with stronger KRAS dependency H1 or KRAS in adenocarcinoma H16; EGFR amplification was not associated with stronger EGFR dependency H3, with validation null R13, and was not supported in EGFR/adenocarcinoma or KRAS-WT contexts; ERBB2 amplification was not associated with stronger ERBB2 dependency H4 or related dependencies; BRAF V600E was not associated with stronger BRAF dependency H5. Many secondary interactions, including BRCA2 loss with WRN or DHX9, STK11 loss with KRAS, RB1 loss with KIF18A, PIK3CA interactions, and many lineage/library/Cas9 interactions, were null, too small, or unresolved. It does not establish that MTAP loss attenuates TP53-loss USP7 dependency, although this remains the highest-priority unresolved interaction. The most informative next analysis is a pre-specified, adequately powered external replication of the TP53-loss by MTAP-loss interaction on USP7 dependency, ideally designed to estimate an interaction near 0.20 dependency-score units. If only supplied-dataset follow-up is possible, analyzing H295 is the best internal next step. Secondary external replication targets are PTEN-loss STAT3 and TP53-loss USP7, plus confirmation of the core MSI-high WRN, KEAP1-loss NFE2L2, SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2, and CDKN2A-loss MDM2 axes. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset only and do not establish causality, biological mechanism, clinical relevance, or external generalizability.","synthesize":"No new independent validation estimates were delivered in this synthesis window and no assessments_due were listed; the validation request budget is exhausted. The final assessment therefore relies on the supplied discovery ledger plus prior validation estimates. All statements are associations in this supplied 2000-cell, lung adenocarcinoma-dominant CRISPR dependency dataset; they do not establish causality, mechanism, clinical relevance, or external generalizability. Because dependency scores are continuous and more negative means stronger dependency, I judged meaningfulness by absolute separation on the observed dependency-score scale, interval precision, replication across strata, and prior independent validation rather than by a direct 10% relative rule. Signed estimates are already oriented to the registered hypothesis: a positive signed estimate with direction -1 means raw exposed-minus-comparator is negative, i.e. stronger dependency; a positive signed estimate with direction +1 means raw exposed-minus-comparator is positive, which for dependency means weaker dependency. Supported robust findings. 1. MSI-high cells have markedly stronger WRN dependency. This is the strongest validated axis: signed +0.790 in discovery R10 and +0.799 in validation R39. It remains large across Cas9-activity strata, Avana and non-Avana libraries, aneuploidy strata, lineage contexts, mutation-burden-adjacent contexts, matched RNA+DNA restriction, research-signature strata, and MTAP strata. The effect is far larger than the typical WRN standard deviation, so it is scientifically meaningful even though external generalizability is unproven. 2. KEAP1-loss cells have markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The accepted reverse-direction claim H13 is supported by signed +0.796 discovery R6 and +0.799 validation R38. The original stronger-NFE2L2 hypothesis is rejected. This association is large and robust across library, Cas9, aneuploidy, lineage, matched-omics, and arbitrary-marker contexts. 3. SMARCA4-loss cells have markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency. Signed +0.784 discovery R19 and +0.790 validation R65 support H20. This holds in ARID1A-loss and ARID1A-intact cells, whereas ARID1A loss alone is not accepted as producing the SMARCA2 effect. 4. TP53-loss cells have weaker USP7 dependency. Signed +0.396 discovery R11 and +0.448 validation R52 support H11. This axis is robust across screen-quality, Cas9, library, aneuploidy, lineage, mutation-burden, matched-omics, MTAP-intact, CDKN2A-intact, and combined clean contexts; the clean TP53-loss effect in MTAP-intact and CDKN2A-intact cells is still large, signed +0.423 in R256. 5. CDKN2A-loss cells have stronger MDM2 dependency. The main accepted effect is signed +0.117 discovery R93. Smaller but repeatedly supported: TP53-intact signed +0.119 discovery R59 with validation +0.129 R78; TP53-loss signed +0.111 discovery R81 with validation +0.132 R92; non-Avana signed +0.125 discovery R95 with validation +0.172 R105. A 9p21-low interaction attenuation claim was not supported, so the MDM2 effect is not reduced to a simple copy-number co-deletion artifact. 6. PTEN-loss cells have stronger STAT3 dependency. Signed +0.267 discovery R113 and +0.283 validation R119 support H116. This is unusually robust across TP53 status, driver-negative cells, serum conditions, growth-rate and hypoxia strata, screen quality, arbitrary marker strata, and MTAP strata. PTEN effects on several other dependencies, including WRN H282, are null, strengthening specificity within this dataset. Important negative findings. Canonical driver-allele-to-self-dependency mappings were not supported: KRAS mutation was not associated with stronger KRAS dependency H1 or KRAS in adenocarcinoma H16; EGFR amplification was not associated with stronger EGFR dependency H3, with validation null R13, and was not supported in EGFR/adenocarcinoma or KRAS-WT contexts; ERBB2 amplification was not associated with stronger ERBB2 dependency H4 or related dependencies; BRAF V600E was not associated with stronger BRAF dependency H5. MYC amplification was broadly null across tested POLR2A, DHX9, RPL11, KIF18A, MDM2, and WRN probes. TMED10 dependency was largely unassociated with tested molecular predictors. Media serum percentage was not associated with STAT3 dependency. MTAP loss was not accepted as a simple main-effect driver of USP7 or MDM2 dependency. Many secondary interactions, including BRCA2 loss with WRN or DHX9, STK11 loss with KRAS, RB1 loss with KIF18A, PIK3CA interactions, and many lineage/library/Cas9 interactions, were null, too small, or unresolved. These negative results matter: the dataset does not support a simple canonical genotype-to-self-dependency model for the driver loci tested, even though several non-self dependency associations are strong and validated. Principal unresolved uncertainty. MTAP loss may attenuate the accepted TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency, but this is not yet a supported independent claim. The accepted main TP53-loss USP7 effect is large and robust, while MTAP-loss strata and interaction estimates are generally smaller and imprecise. The available attenuation-direction evidence is suggestive: H67 signed +0.284 discovery R57 with validation +0.265 R106 but validation interval crossing zero; H146 signed +0.137 R17 crossing zero; H273 CDKN2A-intact interaction +0.139 R254 crossing zero; H283 direct high-Cas9 CDKN2A-intact contrast +0.123 R266 crossing zero and underpowered; H274 Avana CDKN2A-intact MTAP-loss contrast +0.180 R255 crossing zero. These are compatible with attenuation but do not establish it. The registered direct broader probe H295 remains the most informative supplied-dataset follow-up: MTAP-loss effect on USP7 within TP53-loss, CDKN2A-intact cells. It should be accepted only if the signed interval excludes zero with a meaningful magnitude, not merely because the point estimate points toward attenuation. All statements are associations in this supplied 2000-cell, lung adenocarcinoma-dominant CRISPR dependency dataset; they do not establish causality, mechanism, clinical relevance, or external generalizability. Because dependency scores are continuous and more negative means stronger dependency, I judged meaningfulness by absolute separation on the observed dependency-score scale, interval precision, replication across strata, and prior independent validation rather than by a direct 10% relative rule. Signed estimates are already oriented to the registered hypothesis: a positive signed estimate with direction -1 means raw exposed-minus-comparator is negative, i.e. stronger dependency; a positive signed estimate with direction +1 means raw exposed-minus-comparator is positive, which for dependency means weaker dependency. Supported robust findings. 1. MSI-high cells have markedly stronger WRN dependency. This is the strongest validated axis: signed +0.790 in discovery R10 and +0.799 in validation R39. It remains large across Cas9-activity strata, Avana and non-Avana libraries, aneuploidy strata, lineage contexts, mutation-burden-adjacent contexts, matched RNA+DNA restriction, research-signature strata, and MTAP strata. The effect is far larger than the typical WRN standard deviation, so it is scientifically meaningful even though external generalizability is unproven. 2. KEAP1-loss cells have markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The accepted reverse-direction claim H13 is supported by signed +0.796 discovery R6 and +0.799 validation R38. The original stronger-NFE2L2 hypothesis is rejected. This association is large and robust across library, Cas9, aneuploidy, lineage, matched-omics, and arbitrary-marker contexts. 3. SMARCA4-loss cells have markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency. Signed +0.784 discovery R19 and +0.790 validation R65 support H20. This holds in ARID1A-loss and ARID1A-intact cells, whereas ARID1A loss alone is not accepted as producing the SMARCA2 effect. 4. TP53-loss cells have weaker USP7 dependency. Signed +0.396 discovery R11 and +0.448 validation R52 support H11. This axis is robust across screen-quality, Cas9, library, aneuploidy, lineage, mutation-burden, matched-omics, MTAP-intact, CDKN2A-intact, and combined clean contexts; the clean TP53-loss effect in MTAP-intact and CDKN2A-intact cells is still large, signed +0.423 in R256. 5. CDKN2A-loss cells have stronger MDM2 dependency. The main accepted effect is signed +0.117 discovery R93. Smaller but repeatedly supported: TP53-intact signed +0.119 discovery R59 with validation +0.129 R78; TP53-loss signed +0.111 discovery R81 with validation +0.132 R92; non-Avana signed +0.125 discovery R95 with validation +0.172 R105. A 9p21-low interaction attenuation claim was not supported, so the MDM2 effect is not reduced to a simple copy-number co-deletion artifact. 6. PTEN-loss cells have stronger STAT3 dependency. Signed +0.267 discovery R113 and +0.283 validation R119 support H116. This is unusually robust across TP53 status, driver-negative cells, serum conditions, growth-rate and hypoxia strata, screen quality, arbitrary marker strata, and MTAP strata. PTEN effects on several other dependencies, including WRN H282, are null, strengthening specificity within this dataset. Important negative findings. Canonical driver-allele-to-self-dependency mappings were not supported: KRAS mutation was not associated with stronger KRAS dependency H1 or KRAS in adenocarcinoma H16; EGFR amplification was not associated with stronger EGFR dependency H3, with validation null R13, and was not supported in EGFR/adenocarcinoma or KRAS-WT contexts; ERBB2 amplification was not associated with stronger ERBB2 dependency H4 or related dependencies; BRAF V600E was not associated with stronger BRAF dependency H5. MYC amplification was broadly null across tested POLR2A, DHX9, RPL11, KIF18A, MDM2, and WRN probes. TMED10 dependency was largely unassociated with tested molecular predictors. Media serum percentage was not associated with STAT3 dependency. MTAP loss was not accepted as a simple main-effect driver of USP7 or MDM2 dependency. Many secondary interactions, including BRCA2 loss with WRN or DHX9, STK11 loss with KRAS, RB1 loss with KIF18A, PIK3CA interactions, and many lineage/library/Cas9 interactions, were null, too small, or unresolved. These negative results matter: the dataset does not support a simple canonical genotype-to-self-dependency model for the driver loci tested, even though several non-self dependency associations are strong and validated. Principal unresolved uncertainty. MTAP loss may attenuate the accepted TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency, but this is not yet a supported independent claim. The accepted main TP53-loss USP7 effect is large and robust, while MTAP-loss strata and interaction estimates are generally smaller and imprecise. The available attenuation-direction evidence is suggestive: H67 signed +0.284 discovery R57 with validation +0.265 R106 but validation interval crossing zero; H146 signed +0.137 R17 crossing zero; H273 CDKN2A-intact interaction +0.139 R254 crossing zero; H283 direct high-Cas9 CDKN2A-intact contrast +0.123 R266 crossing zero and underpowered; H274 Avana CDKN2A-intact MTAP-loss contrast +0.180 R255 crossing zero. These are compatible with attenuation but do not establish it. The registered direct broader probe H295 remains the most informative supplied-dataset follow-up: MTAP-loss effect on USP7 within TP53-loss, CDKN2A-intact cells. It should be accepted only if the signed interval excludes zero with a meaningful magnitude, not merely because the point estimate points toward attenuation. A second unresolved/interpretive issue is research-signature A heterogeneity for USP7: H241 shows a very large TP53-loss USP7 effect in signature-A-low cells, while H240 is near null in signature-A-high cells, and the interaction is striking. However, core axes such as MSI-high WRN and CDKN2A-loss MDM2 remain strong within signature-A strata. I therefore treat this as constructed-assay heterogeneity, not as evidence of a global technical confounder or assigned biology for research signature A. Arbitrary research markers D, E, and F similarly should not be assigned biological mechanism even where accepted associations remain stable within their strata. Other claims remain unresolved because they were not tested, had insufficient cells, or have intervals too wide to decide practical importance. Final conclusion. The evidence supports six stable dataset-internal dependency axes: MSI-high with stronger WRN, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2, SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2, TP53 loss with weaker USP7, CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3. It does not support canonical driver-allele self-dependency associations for KRAS, EGFR, ERBB2, or BRAF in this dataset. It does not establish that MTAP loss attenuates TP53-loss USP7 dependency, although this remains the highest-priority unresolved interaction. The most informative next analysis is a pre-specified, adequately powered external replication of the TP53-loss by MTAP-loss interaction on USP7 dependency, ideally designed to estimate an interaction near 0.20 dependency-score units. If only supplied-dataset follow-up is possible, analyzing H295 is the best internal next step. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset only and do not establish causality, biological mechanism, clinical relevance, or external generalizability.","synthesize":"No new independent validation estimates were delivered in this synthesis window and no assessments_due were listed; the validation request budget is exhausted. The final assessment therefore relies on the supplied discovery ledger plus prior validation estimates. All statements are associations in this supplied 2000-cell, lung adenocarcinoma-dominant CRISPR dependency dataset; they do not establish causality, mechanism, clinical relevance, or external generalizability. Because dependency scores are continuous and more negative means stronger dependency, I judged meaningfulness by absolute separation on the observed dependency-score scale, interval precision, replication across strata, and prior independent validation rather than by a direct 10% relative rule. Signed estimates are already oriented to the registered hypothesis: a positive signed estimate with direction -1 means raw exposed-minus-comparator is negative, i.e. stronger dependency; a positive signed estimate with direction +1 means raw exposed-minus-comparator is positive, which for dependency means weaker dependency. Supported robust findings. 1. MSI-high cells have markedly stronger WRN dependency. This is the strongest validated axis: signed +0.790 in discovery R10 and +0.799 in validation R39. It remains large across Cas9-activity strata, Avana and non-Avana libraries, aneuploidy strata, lineage contexts, mutation-burden-adjacent contexts, matched RNA+DNA restriction, research-signature strata, and MTAP strata. The effect is far larger than the typical WRN standard deviation, so it is scientifically meaningful even though external generalizability is unproven. 2. KEAP1-loss cells have markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The accepted reverse-direction claim H13 is supported by signed +0.796 discovery R6 and +0.799 validation R38. The original stronger-NFE2L2 hypothesis is rejected. This association is large and robust across library, Cas9, aneuploidy, lineage, matched-omics, and arbitrary-marker contexts. 3. SMARCA4-loss cells have markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency. Signed +0.784 discovery R19 and +0.790 validation R65 support H20. This holds in ARID1A-loss and ARID1A-intact cells, whereas ARID1A loss alone is not accepted as producing the SMARCA2 effect. 4. TP53-loss cells have weaker USP7 dependency. Signed +0.396 discovery R11 and +0.448 validation R52 support H11. This axis is robust across screen-quality, Cas9, library, aneuploidy, lineage, mutation-burden, matched-omics, MTAP-intact, CDKN2A-intact, and combined clean contexts; the clean TP53-loss effect in MTAP-intact and CDKN2A-intact cells is still large, signed +0.423 in R256. 5. CDKN2A-loss cells have stronger MDM2 dependency. The main accepted effect is signed +0.117 discovery R93. Smaller but repeatedly supported: TP53-intact signed +0.119 discovery R59 with validation +0.129 R78; TP53-loss signed +0.111 discovery R81 with validation +0.132 R92; non-Avana signed +0.125 discovery R95 with validation +0.172 R105. A 9p21-low interaction attenuation claim was not supported, so the MDM2 effect is not reduced to a simple copy-number co-deletion artifact. 6. PTEN-loss cells have stronger STAT3 dependency. Signed +0.267 discovery R113 and +0.283 validation R119 support H116. This is unusually robust across TP53 status, driver-negative cells, serum conditions, growth-rate and hypoxia strata, screen quality, arbitrary marker strata, and MTAP strata. PTEN effects on several other dependencies, including WRN H282, are null, strengthening specificity within this dataset. Important negative findings. Canonical driver-allele-to-self-dependency mappings were not supported: KRAS mutation was not associated with stronger KRAS dependency H1 or KRAS in adenocarcinoma H16; EGFR amplification was not associated with stronger EGFR dependency H3, with validation null R13, and was not supported in EGFR/adenocarcinoma or KRAS-WT contexts; ERBB2 amplification was not associated with stronger ERBB2 dependency H4 or related dependencies; BRAF V600E was not associated with stronger BRAF dependency H5. MYC amplification was broadly null across tested POLR2A, DHX9, RPL11, KIF18A, MDM2, and WRN probes. TMED10 dependency was largely unassociated with tested molecular predictors. Media serum percentage was not associated with STAT3 dependency. MTAP loss was not accepted as a simple main-effect driver of USP7 or MDM2 dependency. Many secondary interactions, including BRCA2 loss with WRN or DHX9, STK11 loss with KRAS, RB1 loss with KIF18A, PIK3CA interactions, and many lineage/library/Cas9 interactions, were null, too small, or unresolved. These negative results matter: the dataset does not support a simple canonical genotype-to-self-dependency model for the driver loci tested, even though several non-self dependency associations are strong and validated. Principal unresolved uncertainty. MTAP loss may attenuate the accepted TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency, but this is not yet a supported independent claim. The accepted main TP53-loss USP7 effect is large and robust, while MTAP-loss strata and interaction estimates are generally smaller and imprecise. The available attenuation-direction evidence is suggestive: H67 signed +0.284 discovery R57 with validation +0.265 R106 but validation interval crossing zero; H146 signed +0.137 R17 crossing zero; H273 CDKN2A-intact interaction +0.139 R254 crossing zero; H283 direct high-Cas9 CDKN2A-intact contrast +0.123 R266 crossing zero and underpowered; H274 Avana CDKN2A-intact MTAP-loss contrast +0.180 R255 crossing zero. These are compatible with attenuation but do not establish it. The registered direct broader probe H295 remains the most informative supplied-dataset follow-up: MTAP-loss effect on USP7 within TP53-loss, CDKN2A-intact cells. It should be accepted only if the signed interval excludes zero with a meaningful magnitude, not merely because the point estimate points toward attenuation. record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this analyze stage selects only new, active, previously registered supplied-dataset comparisons that have not yet produced discovery evidence. The highest-priority run is H295, the direct MTAP-loss contrast on USP7 dependency within TP53-loss, CDKN2A-intact cells. Because the accepted TP53-loss effect is weaker USP7 dependency, attenuation by MTAP loss should appear in the registered negative MTAP-loss direction; under the signed convention, a positive estimate excluding zero would support attenuation, whereas near-zero or unresolved estimates would not establish a separate MTAP-interaction claim. H304 asks whether MTAP loss also attenuates the PTEN-loss/STAT3 association, testing whether MTAP loss is a broad modifier or a narrow USP7-specific interaction. H305 tests whether CDKN2A loss has any WRN association after excluding MSI-high cells, probing specificity relative to the accepted CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 axis. H272 tests whether the KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 association persists among PTEN-loss cells, providing a specificity probe for the KEAP1 axis and whether PTEN loss materially modifies it. The remaining eight claims replicate four accepted axes within high- and low-screen-quality strata using median screen_roc_auc: KEAP1/NFE2L2 (H296/H297), SMARCA4/SMARCA2 (H298/H299), CDKN2A/MDM2 (H300/H301), and MSI-high/WRN (H302/H303). Broad persistence across screen-quality strata argues against screen-quality artifacts; missing or materially weaker stratum effects would identify context dependence. Judgments will use valid cells, signed intervals excluding zero, absolute dependency-score separation, approximate relative magnitude against absolute baseline levels where interpretable, and agreement with prior robustness and validation evidence. Because dependency scores are continuous and can be negative, the 10% relative threshold is applied cautiously as a relative-to-baseline heuristic rather than a strict ratio rule. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset only and do not establish causality, mechanism, clinical relevance, or external generalizability.

Iteration 23/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All twelve newly delivered comparisons had valid Welch cells and were assessed using the already-signed estimates, with positive signed values interpreted in the registered hypothesis direction rather than recoding the raw contrast again. The four screen-quality strata sets, H296-H303, are best viewed as pre-specified robustness checks of already-supported axes rather than as claims that screen_roc_auc is a causal modifier or as independent external validation. They are nevertheless informative because both the high- and low-screen_roc_auc strata showed substantial associations in the registered direction: KEAP1 loss remained associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, signed +0.793 in high-quality screens, R282, and +0.798 in low-quality screens, R283; SMARCA4 loss remained associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, signed +0.791, R284, and +0.778, R285; CDKN2A loss remained associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, signed +0.132, R286, and +0.103, R287; MSI-high remained associated with stronger WRN dependency, signed +0.790 in both screen-quality halves, R288 and R289. These intervals exclude zero and cover magnitudes that are large relative to the relevant dependency-score scales. I therefore accept these stratum-specific associations as evidence that the core KEAP1/NFE2L2, SMARCA4/SMARCA2, CDKN2A/MDM2, and MSI-high/WRN associations are not confined to either screen-quality stratum. This does not eliminate all possible confounding because screen-quality metrics can themselves correlate with biological or technical features, but it argues against the simplest explanation that these main axes are artifacts of poor screen quality. H272 tests whether the KEAP1-loss association with weaker NFE2L2 dependency persists among PTEN-loss cells. The signed estimate is +0.776 with a tight interval, R281, so I accept it. This is conditional-association robustness: it shows the KEAP1/NFE2L2 axis remains present within PTEN-loss cells, but it does not estimate or support effect modification by PTEN loss because no interaction contrast was delivered. H304 tests whether MTAP loss modifies the PTEN-loss/STAT3 association. The signed interaction estimate is small, +0.022, and the interval includes both attenuation-like and enhancement-like effects, R279. It does not support a registered positive interaction claim. Given that this is one of many interaction probes and the evidence is not directionally consistent or statistically supported, I reject H304 as unsupported. I would not interpret the interval as proving the absence of any moderate modification; rather, the supplied data do not warrant accepting a separate MTAP-dependent PTEN/STAT3 claim. H305 tests CDKN2A loss as a predictor of WRN dependency after excluding MSI-high cells. The signed estimate is +0.005 with a narrow interval centered near zero, R280. This is a clear specificity null on the dependency-score scale and supports the conclusion that CDKN2A loss is not broadly associated with stronger WRN dependency in MSI-negative cells, reinforcing the more specific CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 association rather than a generic WRN association. H295 is the most important unresolved probe: MTAP loss among TP53-loss, CDKN2A-intact cells with respect to USP7 dependency. The signed estimate is +0.115, R278, which points in the attenuation direction expected if MTAP loss partially restores USP7 dependency in TP53-loss cells. However, the 95% interval is -0.100 to +0.329 and crosses zero. The exposed cell contains 61 observations and the comparator 264, so the test is not sufficiently powered to distinguish attenuation from no effect or even a modest opposite effect. The broader interval upper bound is compatible with a meaningful attenuation, while the lower bound is compatible with no meaningful attenuation or a small opposite association. Therefore H295 remains unresolved. I closed its investigation because no independent validation capacity remains and further supplied-dataset mining would add multiplicity without solving the precision problem. The attenuation hypothesis should not be promoted to an accepted claim. Overall, these results further support the six stable supplied-dataset axes: MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency; KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency; SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency; CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency; and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. They do not establish MTAP loss as a broad modifier, do not establish MTAP-loss attenuation of TP53-loss USP7 dependency, and do not restore canonical driver-allele self-dependency mappings for KRAS, EGFR, ERBB2, or BRAF. All conclusions remain associations in this supplied dataset, subject to residual confounding and multiplicity, and do not demonstrate causality, mechanism, clinical relevance, or external generalizability.

record.narrative:
No new validation estimates were delivered in this final synthesis window, and no response-deadline claims were listed; the independent validation request budget is exhausted. The final scientific conclusions therefore combine the accumulated supplied-dataset discovery estimates with the earlier independent validation estimates already present in the ledger. All statements are associations within this supplied 2000-cell lung-dominant CRISPR dependency dataset and do not establish causality, mechanism, clinical relevance, or external generalizability.

Supported findings. Six dependency-predictor axes are well supported by large, precisely estimated, replicated associations. First, MSI-high cells show markedly stronger WRN dependency: discovery signed +0.790 and validation signed +0.799. This remains large across screen-quality, Cas9-activity, library, aneuploidy, matched-omics, mutation-burden-adjacent, MTAP, and research-signature contexts. Second, KEAP1-loss cells show markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency: discovery signed +0.796 and validation signed +0.799 for the accepted reverse-direction claim; the original stronger-NFE2L2 hypothesis was rejected. Third, SMARCA4-loss cells show markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency: discovery signed +0.784 and validation signed +0.790, with robustness across ARID1A-loss and ARID1A-intact contexts. Fourth, TP53-loss cells show weaker USP7 dependency: discovery signed +0.396 and validation signed +0.448, robust across screen-quality, Cas9, library, lineage, aneuploidy, mutation-burden, matched-omics, MTAP-intact, CDKN2A-intact, and combined cleaner strata. Fifth, CDKN2A-loss cells show stronger MDM2 dependency: main signed +0.117, with TP53-intact, TP53-loss, and non-Avana validated subeffects around +0.13 to +0.17, plus consistent robustness across Cas9, aneuploidy, screen quality, mutation burden, matched-omics, PTEN, MTAP, and signature strata. Sixth, PTEN-loss cells show stronger STAT3 dependency: discovery signed +0.267 and validation signed +0.283, highly robust across TP53 status, driver-negative cells, serum condition, growth-rate and hypoxia strata, screen quality, arbitrary marker strata, MTAP status, and matched-omics restriction. These effects are large on the observed dependency-score scale and, for validated axes, reproduce in independent splits, so they are scientifically meaningful within this dataset.

Negative findings. The supplied dataset does not support canonical driver-allele self-dependency mappings for the driver loci tested. KRAS mutation is not associated with stronger KRAS dependency overall or within adenocarcinoma; EGFR amplification is not associated with stronger EGFR dependency overall, in adenocarcinoma, in KRAS-WT cells, or by validation; ERBB2 amplification is not associated with stronger ERBB2 dependency or related TMED10, STAT3, or RIT1 contrasts; BRAF V600E is not associated with stronger BRAF dependency. MYC amplification is broadly unassociated with POLR2A, DHX9, RPL11, KIF18A, MDM2, and other tested dependencies. TMED10 is largely unassociated with tested molecular predictors. Media serum percentage is not associated with STAT3 dependency. Several secondary interactions are null or unsupported, including 9p21-low attenuation of the CDKN2A/MDM2 association, MTAP-loss modification of PTEN-loss/STAT3, and broad main effects of arbitrary research markers. These negative results are important because they show that reproducible dependency associations exist in this dataset while the simplest genotype-to-self-dependency model is not supported.

Unresolved uncertainty. The most informative unresolved question is whether MTAP loss attenuates the accepted TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency. Multiple attenuation-direction contrasts point in the same direction but are imprecise: MTAP loss in TP53-loss, CDKN2A-intact cells is signed +0.115 with 95% interval crossing zero; corresponding interaction estimates are also positive but cross zero and are underpowered. These estimates are compatible with attenuation but also compatible with no effect or a modest opposite association. Therefore MTAP-loss attenuation remains unresolved and should not be accepted. A second unresolved issue is TP53-loss USP7 heterogeneity by the constructed research signature A: a very large TP53-loss effect in signature-A-low cells contrasts with a near-null effect in signature-A-high cells. Because signature A is an arbitrary constructed assay, this is dataset-internal heterogeneity, not assigned biology. Many smaller subgroup and interaction claims remain unresolved due to insufficient cells, wide intervals, or lack of testing; additional post hoc mining is unlikely to resolve them without external data.

Conclusion and next analysis. The evidence supports six stable dataset-internal dependency axes: MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. It does not support canonical driver-allele self-dependency associations for KRAS, EGFR, ERBB2, or BRAF in this dataset. It does not establish that MTAP loss attenuates TP53-loss USP7 dependency, although that remains the highest-priority unresolved interaction. The most informative next analysis is a pre-specified external replication study designed to test the TP53-loss by MTAP-loss interaction on USP7 dependency, ideally powered near 0.90 for an interaction around 0.20 dependency-score units, with pre-specified subgroup definitions. The same external analysis should confirm the six stable axes and test whether the observed associations generalize beyond this supplied dataset.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Because the accepted TP53-loss effect is weaker USP7 dependency, attenuation by MTAP loss should appear in the registered negative MTAP-loss direction; under the signed convention, a positive estimate excluding zero would support attenuation, whereas near-zero or unresolved estimates would not establish a separate MTAP-interaction claim. H305 tests whether CDKN2A loss has any WRN association after excluding MSI-high cells, probing specificity relative to the accepted CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 axis. The four screen-quality strata sets, H296-H303, are best viewed as pre-specified robustness checks of already-supported axes rather than as claims that screen_roc_auc is a causal modifier or as independent external validation. They are nevertheless informative because both the high- and low-screen_roc_auc strata showed substantial associations in the registered direction: KEAP1 loss remained associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, signed +0.793 in high-quality screens, R282, and +0.798 in low-quality screens, R283; SMARCA4 loss remained associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, signed +0.791, R284, and +0.778, R285; CDKN2A loss remained associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, signed +0.132, R286, and +0.103, R287; MSI-high remained associated with stronger WRN dependency, signed +0.790 in both screen-quality halves, R288 and R289. record.narrative: No assessments are due and validation capacity is exhausted, so this final explore stage registers supplied-dataset comparisons that add the most remaining information. First, six subgroup main effects test the six accepted axes within STK11-loss cells, a common lung-cancer co-mutation context; persistence in that stratum would further support that the axes are not artifacts of STK11-loss subtype. Second, two PI3K-related tests probe cross-pathway dependence: whether PI3K mutation strengthens STAT3 dependency among PTEN-loss cells, and whether PI3K mutation strengthens MDM2 dependency among TP53-intact cells. Third, two KRAS cross-pathway tests ask whether KRAS-mutant cells show weaker EGFR or BRAF dependency, which would be plausible if KRAS activates downstream RAS/MAPK signaling and reduces upstream-node dependency. Fourth, two refinements reverse prior interaction directions where the already-delivered signed evidence points in the opposite direction: research signature A appears to attenuate the TP53-loss USP7 association, and marker E appears to enhance the PTEN-loss STAT3 association. These are dataset-internal effect-modifier claims about constructed assays, not assigned biology. All returned estimates will be interpreted as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. The 10% relative-dependency heuristic is applied cautiously because dependency scores can be negative. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset only; none establish causality, mechanism, clinical validity, or external generalizability.

Second, KEAP1-loss cells show markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency: discovery signed +0.796 and validation signed +0.799 for the accepted reverse-direction claim; the original stronger-NFE2L2 hypothesis was rejected. Third, SMARCA4-loss cells show markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency: discovery signed +0.784 and validation signed +0.790, with robustness across ARID1A-loss and ARID1A-intact contexts. Fourth, TP53-loss cells show weaker USP7 dependency: discovery signed +0.396 and validation signed +0.448, robust across screen-quality, Cas9, library, lineage, aneuploidy, mutation-burden, matched-omics, MTAP-intact, CDKN2A-intact, and combined cleaner strata. The supplied dataset does not support canonical driver-allele self-dependency mappings for the driver loci tested. KRAS mutation is not associated with stronger KRAS dependency overall or within adenocarcinoma; EGFR amplification is not associated with stronger EGFR dependency overall, in adenocarcinoma, in KRAS-WT cells, or by validation; ERBB2 amplification is not associated with stronger ERBB2 dependency or related TMED10, STAT3, or RIT1 contrasts; BRAF V600E is not associated with stronger BRAF dependency. MYC amplification is broadly unassociated with POLR2A, DHX9, RPL11, KIF18A, MDM2, and other tested dependencies. TMED10 is largely unassociated with tested molecular predictors. Media serum percentage is not associated with STAT3 dependency. Several secondary interactions are null or unsupported, including 9p21-low attenuation of the CDKN2A/MDM2 association, MTAP-loss modification of PTEN-loss/STAT3, and broad main effects of arbitrary research markers. These negative results are important because they show that reproducible dependency associations exist in this dataset while the simplest genotype-to-self-dependency model is not supported.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty. The most informative unresolved question is whether MTAP loss attenuates the accepted TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency. Multiple attenuation-direction contrasts point in the same direction but are imprecise: MTAP loss in TP53-loss, CDKN2A-intact cells is signed +0.115 with 95% interval crossing zero; corresponding interaction estimates are also positive but cross zero and are underpowered. These estimates are compatible with attenuation but also compatible with no effect or a modest opposite association. Therefore MTAP-loss attenuation remains unresolved and should not be accepted. A second unresolved issue is TP53-loss USP7 heterogeneity by the constructed research signature A: a very large TP53-loss effect in signature-A-low cells contrasts with a near-null effect in signature-A-high cells. Because signature A is an arbitrary constructed assay, this is dataset-internal heterogeneity, not assigned biology. Many smaller subgroup and interaction claims remain unresolved due to insufficient cells, wide intervals, or lack of testing; additional post hoc mining is unlikely to resolve them without external data.\n\nConclusion and next analysis. The evidence supports six stable dataset-internal dependency axes: MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. It does not support canonical driver-allele self-dependency associations for KRAS, EGFR, ERBB2, or BRAF in this dataset. It does not establish that MTAP loss attenuates TP53-loss USP7 dependency, although that remains the highest-priority unresolved interaction. The most informative next analysis is a pre-specified external replication study designed to test the TP53-loss by MTAP-loss interaction on USP7 dependency, ideally powered near 0.90 for an interaction around 0.20 dependency-score units, with pre-specified subgroup definitions. The same external analysis should confirm the six stable axes and test whether the observed associations generalize beyond this supplied dataset."}}

record.narrative: All twelve due comparisons were valid Welch contrasts, and the reported estimates are interpreted already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. The six STK11-loss subgroup main effects strongly support persistence of the six core accepted axes in STK11-loss cells. H306-H311 each have large signed point estimates with intervals excluding zero: KEAP1-loss persistence in NFE2L2 (+0.775, R290), SMARCA4-loss persistence in SMARCA2 (+0.769, R291), TP53-loss persistence in USP7 (+0.490, R292), CDKN2A-loss persistence in MDM2 (+0.105, R293), MSI-high persistence in WRN (+0.749, R294), and PTEN-loss persistence in STAT3 (+0.258, R295). H309 has a less precise interval, but its lower bound is positive and the effect is on the same scale as the accepted CDKN2A/MDM2 axis; H310 has only 22 exposed observations, but the effect is extremely large and its interval is still decisive. These are accepted as dataset-internal subgroup persistence claims, not evidence of causal interaction or external generalizability. The PI3K cross-pathway probes do not add a supported new axis. H312 is underpowered in PTEN-loss cells, with a near-zero signed point estimate and a wide interval crossing zero; it remains unresolved and is closed because no validation capacity remains. H313 is a precise near-null test and is rejected. The KRAS downstream cross-dependency probes H316 and H317 are also rejected: the signed estimates are opposite the registered positive weaker-dependency direction and their intervals do not support a meaningful positive effect. H314 is accepted as a very large, precise dataset-internal effect-modifier association involving the constructed research signature A; because signature A has no assigned biological role, this should be reported only as dataset-internal heterogeneity, not as mechanistic or biological validation. H315 is accepted only weakly and with stronger caveats: marker E is an arbitrary constructed binary assay, the interval is moderately wide and its lower bound is close to trivial, and this is one of many data-mined interaction probes. Therefore H315 can be retained as a dataset-internal measured-assay association only, not as a biologically interpretable or generalizable modifier. Overall, the new evidence strengthens subgroup persistence of the six core axes, keeps arbitrary-assay interactions as descriptive dataset associations, and continues to provide no support for canonical driver self-dependency mappings for KRAS, EGFR, ERBB2, or BRAF in this supplied dataset.

Sixth, PTEN-loss cells show stronger STAT3 dependency: discovery signed +0.267 and validation signed +0.283, highly robust across TP53 status, driver-negative cells, serum condition, growth-rate and hypoxia strata, screen quality, arbitrary marker strata, MTAP status, and matched-omics restriction. record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent-validation capacity is exhausted. I therefore register supplied-dataset comparisons that test technical-confounder robustness of the six accepted dependency axes: persistence within screen batch batch_a and within adherent culture.
